  Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 239 arterial phase CT angiography examinations of 230 patients (median age, 65 years [range, 18-99 years]; 163 men) performed between April 2025 and October 2026 (209 electrocardiographically [ECG] gated). The tool locates landmarks from TotalSegmentator segmentations of aortic branches and vertebrae and measures the maximum diameter at each. A senior radiologist reviewed and, where needed, corrected the automated measurements to create the reference standard. Agreement was assessed with mean absolute error (MAE), bias, and differences greater than 2 mm.
  Results: Across all landmarks, MAE was 1.06 mm (95% CI: 0.91, 1.22), and 86.6% (95% CI: 84.4, 88.5) of differences were 2 mm or less. The tool measured slightly larger diameters (bias, 0.45 mm [95% CI: 0.34, 0.57]). The sinuses of Valsalva had the largest MAE (2.17 mm [95% CI: 1.59, 2.86]). For 1.2% of landmarks, the automatic measurement failed. Examination-level MAE did not differ significantly by pathology, atherosclerosis grade (P=.95), or ECG gating (P=.14). Examinations with mural thrombus more often had an MAE greater than 2 mm (50% [95% CI: 31, 69] vs 20%; P=.03).
  Conclusion: The tool measured aortic diameters at 11 landmarks along the entire aorta with an MAE of about 1 mm, below published interreader variability. Agreement was lower at the aortic root and with mural thrombus.
  Code availability: The tool is open source and freely available at https://github.com/wasserth/TotalSegmentator.

title: Wireless Node Ranking via Fourier-Driven Maximum-Likelihood Estimation (extended version)
summary:
We apply non-abelian Fourier theory to the problem of maximum-likelihood estimation of the order of a line topology, based on signal strength measurements under shadowing only. This yields up to a 60-fold speedup over standard methods for uncorrelated shadowing.
  Moreover, for correlated Gaussian shadowing with a singular covariance (e.g. the joint path-loss model), maximum-likelihood recovery is exact and independent of the shadowing variance (an infinite Le Cam threshold), which our implementation confirms for $σ/α$ as high as 7.0. The key object is the covariance's null space. Its dimension is fixed by the topology; its orientation depends on the correlation function only through the per-link variances.
  Although the mechanism formally requires an exact line, it is robust to small perturbations of the formation: an approximate kernel recovers as well as the exact one. We explore the dependence on the perturbation in detail for five nodes.

title: Enhancing Transient Stability of VSG-Controlled Converters Under Grid Frequency Disturbances
summary: Strong damping feedback can substantially improve the transient synchronization stability of renewable energy converters employing virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control. However, conventional damping feedback uses the nominal frequency as its reference. When the frequency of a weak grid deviates from nominal, strong damping tends to keep the VSG frequency near nominal. This can sustain a frequency difference between the VSG and the grid and compromise transient synchronization. To address this problem, this paper proposes a complex-frequency-based method to estimate the grid reference frequency from local terminal measurements. The estimated frequency replaces the nominal reference in the VSG synchronization loop, so that damping acts on the frequency difference between the VSG and the real grid. Controller hardware-in-the-loop tests validate the effectiveness of the proposed method under grid frequency disturbances and its robustness to grid parameter uncertainty and adverse grid conditions.

AI.title_translation: 电网频率扰动下增强VSG控制变流器暂态稳定性的方法
AI.tldr: 提出了一种基于复频率的电网频率本地估计方法，用以改进VSG阻尼回路参考值，显著增强了弱电网频率扰动下的暂态同步稳定性。
AI.motivation: 传统VSG控制采用强阻尼反馈来提升暂态稳定性，但阻尼参考值通常设为额定频率。当弱电网频率偏离额定值时，强阻尼会导致VSG频率被锚定在额定值附近，进而维持VSG与电网间的频差，损害暂态同步稳定性。
AI.method: 提出一种基于复频率（complex-frequency-based）的方法，仅利用本地端测量值估计电网实际参考频率，并用该估计值替代VSG同步环路中的额定频率参考值，使阻尼控制直接作用于VSG与实际电网之间的频差。
AI.result: 控制器在环（CHIL）实验结果验证了所提方法在电网频率扰动下的有效性，以及在电网参数不确定性和恶劣电网条件下的鲁棒性。
AI.conclusion: 基于复频率估计并动态替换VSG阻尼参考频率的方法，能有效解决弱电网频率偏离时的失步问题，大幅提升变流器在频率扰动和恶劣电网工况下的暂态同步稳定性与鲁棒性。
AI.translation: 强阻尼反馈可以显著提高采用虚拟同步机（VSG）控制的可再生能源变流器的暂态同步稳定性。然而，传统的阻尼反馈使用额定频率作为其参考值。当弱电网的频率偏离额定值时，强阻尼往往使VSG频率保持在额定值附近。这会导致VSG与电网之间存在持续的频率差，从而损害暂态同步稳定性。为解决该问题，本文提出了一种基于复频率的方法，利用本地端测量来估计电网参考频率。估计出的频率替代了VSG同步环路中的额定参考值，从而使阻尼作用于VSG与实际电网之间的频率差。控制器硬件在环测试验证了所提方法在电网频率扰动下的有效性，以及其对电网参数不确定性和恶劣电网条件的鲁棒性。
AI.summary: 本文针对弱电网频率偏离额定值时传统VSG强阻尼控制容易损害暂态同步稳定性的缺陷，提出了一种利用本地端量测估计电网参考频率的复频率方法。通过将VSG同步环路的额定参考替换为估计的实际电网频率，使阻尼反馈精准抑制两者间的实际频差。硬件在环测试验证了该方法在频率扰动及恶劣工况下的有效性和鲁棒性。
AI.keywords: 虚拟同步机 (VSG), 暂态稳定性, 复频率, 阻尼反馈, 频率扰动
AI.comments: 该论文针对弱电网下VSG控制中“强阻尼反馈依赖额定频率”与“电网实际频率偏移”之间的冲突问题，提出了基于复频率的本地估计方案。该方法巧妙地仅通过本地量测实现对实际电网参考频率的获取，避免了通信依赖，并在保留强阻尼暂态稳定优势的同时消除了稳态频差风险，具有很强的工程实用价值和创新性。

title: Algorithmic Opacity as a Principal-Agent Problem
summary: Concerns about gaming and trade secrecy, frequently invoked to justify algorithmic opacity, can also mask self-serving strategic behavior by decision-makers, who may prioritize private benefits over social welfare. We develop a principal-agent test for when algorithmic decision-making should trigger disclosure obligations even when concerns about gaming or trade secrecy exist. The test, which is anchored in decision quality, relies on two diagnostics that can be disclosed without enabling gaming or revealing trade secrets: the error profile (false positive and false negative rates, overall and for each group) and the distribution of decision outcomes across groups. These diagnostics make visible whether decision-makers align design and implementation with the public interest or instead use opacity to obscure bias, inefficiency, or strategic shirking. Strong disparities across social groups, and asymmetries in the distribution of decision errors across outcome types, should trigger rebuttable presumptions favoring further disclosure. Where ground-truth error rates are unavailable, outcome distributions across groups can support the same presumption, and a decision-maker's inability to produce an error profile is itself diagnostic. The test thus treats fairness metrics as triggers for further disclosure and extends to generative and agentic systems through analogous metrics. The framework informs differentiated disclosure regimes (staged, partial, mediated, or audience-segmented). Once such regimes are considered, the domain of justifiable algorithmic opacity is significantly narrower than commonly assumed: when gaming or trade secrecy risks are legitimate, actionable disclosures (such as training data characteristics and key system design parameters) ordinarily can be mandated without compromising innovation or enabling gaming, even for technically inscrutable algorithms.

AI.title_translation: 作为委托-代理问题的算法不透明性
AI.tldr: 本文将算法不透明性视为委托-代理问题，提出通过群体错误画像和结果分布等诊断指标触发差异化强制披露，从而大幅压缩算法黑箱的合理保留空间。
AI.motivation: 算法决策者常以防止恶意操纵（gaming）和保护商业秘密为借口保持算法不透明，但这种不透明性也极易被用作掩盖偏见、低效、策略性怠工等谋取自利而牺牲社会福利的行为。
AI.method: 提出了一种基于决策质量的委托-代理测试框架。该框架利用无需泄露商业秘密或促成恶意操纵的两项核心诊断指标——各群体错误画像（假阳性/假阴性率）与跨群体决策结果分布，将显著的群体差异和错误不对称性作为触发强制进一步披露的可反驳推定，并由此指导分阶段、部分或受众细分的差异化披露机制设计。
AI.result: 当算法在不同社会群体间存在显著偏倚或错误类型不对称时，足以建立支持深度披露的法律推定；无法提供错误画像本身可作为决策失职的诊断凭证；该框架证实，即便面对黑盒模型，实施切实可行的披露义务（如训练数据特征和关键设计参数）通常不会妨碍创新或引发对抗性操纵。
AI.conclusion: 受正当理由保护的算法不透明性范围远比通常认为的要窄；在考虑差异化披露机制后，即使存在商业秘密和防操纵等合法风险，监管者亦可且应当在不损害创新和安全的前提下，依法强制披露关键设计参数与训练数据特征。
AI.translation: 对恶意操纵和商业秘密的担忧常常被用来为算法不透明性辩护，但这同样可能掩盖决策者将私人利益置于社会福利之上的自利战略行为。我们构建了一个委托-代理测试框架，用于判定即使存在操纵或商业秘密担忧时，算法决策在何种情况下应触发披露义务。该测试以决策质量为核心，依赖于两项既不会促成操纵也不会泄露商业秘密的诊断指标：错误画像（总体及各群体的假阳性率和假阴性率）以及不同群体间的决策结果分布。这些诊断指标能够揭示决策者究竟是将系统设计和实施与公共利益对齐，还是利用不透明性来掩盖偏见、低效或策略性懈怠。群体间的巨大差异以及不同结果类型间决策错误分布的不对称性，应触发支持进一步披露的可反驳推定。在无法获取真实错误率的情况下，跨群体结果分布也能支持同样的推定，且决策者无法提供错误画像本身就是一种诊断信号。因此，该测试将公平性指标视为进一步披露的触发器，并可通过类似指标拓展至生成式与代理系统。该框架为构建差异化披露机制（分阶段、部分、中介或受众细分披露）提供了指导。一旦引入此类机制，受正当理由支持的算法不透明性范围将远比通常认为的更为狭窄：当操纵或商业秘密风险合情合理时，即使面对技术上难以解释的算法，通常也能在不损害创新或促成操纵的前提下，强制要求进行切实可行的披露（如训练数据特征和关键系统设计参数）。
AI.summary: 本文将算法不透明性构建为一个委托-代理问题，指出决策者常用商业秘密和防操纵为掩护规避责任。作者提出了一套以决策质量指标（错误画像及群体间结果分布）为触发机制的审计测试，通过差异化披露机制，在保护合法商业权益与创新的同时，有效拆解不合理的算法黑箱，强化公共利益问责。
AI.keywords: 算法不透明性, 委托-代理问题, 算法披露, 商业秘密, 算法审计
AI.comments: 该论文从委托-代理理论的经济与法律视角重新审视了算法不透明性，创新性地将模型评估指标（错误率、结果分布等公平性指标）重构为法律上的“披露触发器”。这一框架成功化解了商业机密保护、防恶意操纵与算法透明度问责之间的长久对立，为规制技术上不可解释或黑箱算法提供了高度可操作的分层披露路径。

title: When Does Oversampling Help? A Decision Framework for Imbalanced Data Streams Under Label Delay and Concept Drift
summary: For imbalanced data streams with delayed labels, is it worth adding a streaming oversampler, or does continuous re-evaluation of earlier predictions already recover the cost of the delay? We address this through an extensive experimental comparison of streaming oversampling and continuous re-evaluation under joint class imbalance, concept drift, and label delay. Streaming oversamplers are typically evaluated under the test-then-train assumption of immediate labels; their behaviour under these conditions, assessed through re-evaluation, has not been systematically studied. We close this gap with a decision framework that predicts when oversampling adds value over re-evaluation, organised around three axes: drift density, minority-class learnability, and delay relative to the refinement window, and operationalised as a competition between a recovery channel (re-evaluation) and a minority-coverage channel (oversampling). Evaluating $15$ classifiers on $6$ synthetic and $6$ real streams, we find: re-evaluation recovers delay-induced loss on drift-active streams but is silent on stationary ones; oversampling's marginal contribution over re-evaluation is statistically detectable in only one real-data configuration; and cost--performance Pareto recommendations from synthetic streams do not transfer to real data, where fronts partition by drift regime. Method selection should therefore be conditioned on the stream's profile and re-estimated as it evolves, not inherited from synthetic benchmarks.

AI.title_translation: 过采样何时奏效？标签延迟与概念漂移下不平衡数据流的决策框架
AI.tldr: 在存在标签延迟与概念漂移的不平衡数据流中，持续重评估常可弥补延迟损失，而过采样的边际增益在真实数据中极少显著，算法选择须根据数据流特征动态调整。
AI.motivation: 针对标签延迟的不平衡数据流，流式过采样器通常在标签立即可得的假设下被评估，尚不明确在概念漂移和标签延迟下，增加流式过采样器是否有价值，还是对早期预测的持续重评估就足以弥补延迟造成的损失。
AI.method: 提出了一个决策框架，基于三个维度（漂移密度、少数类可学习性、相对于优化窗口的延迟）预测过采样何时能带来增益，将其操作化为恢复通道（重评估）与少数类覆盖通道（过采样）的竞争；并在6个合成流和6个真实流上对15种分类器进行了广泛的实验比较。
AI.result: 持续重评估可在漂移活跃的数据流上弥补延迟引起的损失，但在平稳数据流上无明显作用；在真实数据中，过采样相比重评估的边际贡献仅在一种配置下具有统计可检测性；从合成流获得的成本-性能帕累托推荐无法直接迁移至真实数据（帕累托前沿受漂移机制划分）。
AI.conclusion: 方法选择应基于具体数据流的特征画像，并在数据流演化过程中进行动态重估，而不应直接套用合成基准的结论。
AI.translation: 对于具有标签延迟的不平衡数据流，添加流式过采样器是否值得，抑或是对早期预测进行持续重评估就已经能弥补延迟的损失？我们通过在类别不平衡、概念漂移和标签延迟共同作用下，对流式过采样和持续重评估进行广泛的实验比较来解决这一问题。流式过采样器通常在标签立即可得的“先测后训”假设下进行评估；而在上述复杂条件下通过重评估对其行为的考察尚未得到系统研究。我们提出了一个决策框架来填补这一空白，该框架围绕漂移密度、少数类可学习性以及相对于优化窗口的延迟这三个维度进行组织，用于预测过采样何时比重评估带来额外价值，并将其具体化为恢复通道（重评估）与少数类覆盖通道（过采样）之间的竞争。通过在6个合成流和6个真实流上评估15种分类器，我们发现：重评估能够弥补漂移活跃流中延迟带来的性能损失，但在平稳流上没有作用；在真实数据中，过采样相比重评估的边际贡献仅在一种配置下具有统计显著性；来自合成流的成本-性能帕累托推荐无法迁移至真实数据，因为真实数据的前沿是按漂移机制划分的。因此，方法的选择应依据数据流的特征画像，并在其演化过程中重新估计，而不是直接套用合成基准的结论。
AI.summary: 本文探讨了在类别不平衡、概念漂移和标签延迟并存的数据流中，流式过采样是否优于持续重评估。作者提出了基于漂移密度、少数类可学习性及延迟程度的三轴决策框架，通过对15种分类器在12个数据流上的实验发现，过采样的边际效益在真实场景中极弱，合成基准的推荐无法直接泛化，因此算法选择需根据流特征动态评估。
AI.keywords: 不平衡数据流, 过采样, 概念漂移, 标签延迟, 持续重评估
AI.comments: 该论文直面流数据学习中三个常见但常被孤立研究的挑战：类别不平衡、概念漂移和标签延迟。论文创新性地构建了重评估与过采样之间的竞争决策框架，并指出了合成数据帕累托前沿无法直接迁移到真实数据的关键局限，对实际数据流系统的算法选型具有高度指导意义。局限在于该结论主要基于15种分类器和12个数据集的实验归纳，其决策框架参数在未知真实场景下的自适应估计复杂度仍待进一步探讨。

title: Interactive deep-learning based interface for brain tumour segmentation
summary: Brain tumour segmentation from MR images is an integral part of their treatment, either through surgical resection or radiotherapy. Both applications require a high degree of precision that can be difficult to ensure for all patients due to the high degree of variability in the size, shape, number, and location of these tumours. This leads to difficulties with their automatic segmentation via deep learning, which can display catastrophic segmentation errors when presented with images that differ, even subtly, in terms of the specific MR sequence used, which varies from vendor to vendor. This article presents a deep-learning-based interactive segmentation system that, while being fully automatic by default, has the capability of being easily corrected by human users, allowing them ensure sufficiently high brain tumour segmentation accuracy for all patients. This interface is evaluated both in terms of the accuracy of its automatic approach as well as its usability through a preliminary observational expert user study.

AI.title_translation: 基于深度学习的脑肿瘤分割交互式界面
AI.tldr: 提出了一种默认全自动但支持专家便捷交互修正的深度学习脑肿瘤分割界面，以解决自动模型在不同MR序列下易出错的问题并确保高分割精度。
AI.motivation: 脑肿瘤在尺寸、形状、数量和位置上具有高度多样性，且不同厂商的MR序列存在细微差异，导致全自动深度学习分割容易出现灾难性错误，难以满足手术切除或放疗所要求的高精度。
AI.method: 提出了一种基于深度学习的交互式脑肿瘤分割系统。该系统默认状态下为全自动分割，同时具备支持人类用户轻松进行交互式修正的功能。
AI.result: 具体量化结果在摘要中未提及（Not mentioned in abstract）。摘要仅说明通过自动分割方法的精度评估以及一项初步的观察性专家用户研究（评估可用性）对该界面进行了验证。
AI.conclusion: 该系统使人类用户能够轻松修正分割结果，从而确保对所有患者均能达到足够高的脑肿瘤分割精度。
AI.translation: 从MR图像中分割脑肿瘤是其治疗（无论是手术切除还是放射治疗）不可或缺的组成部分。由于这些肿瘤在大小、形状、数量和位置上存在极大的变异性，这两种应用都需要极高的精度，而要确保对所有患者都达到这种精度往往十分困难。这给通过深度学习进行自动分割带来了挑战，当输入的图像在不同厂商采用的具体MR序列上存在哪怕细微差异时，深度学习都可能出现灾难性的分割错误。本文提出了一种基于深度学习的交互式分割系统，该系统默认完全自动化，但人类用户能够轻松对其进行修正，从而确保为所有患者提供足够高的脑肿瘤分割精度。本研究从其自动化方法的精度以及通过一项初步的观察性专家用户研究所体现的可用性两方面对该界面进行了评估。
AI.summary: 针对深度学习全自动分割在跨厂商MR图像中易出现灾难性错误的问题，本文开发了一种基于深度学习的交互式脑肿瘤分割系统。该系统默认全自动运行，并允许专家轻松介入修正，以保证临床所需的高精度，并通过算法精度测试和专家可用性研究进行了评估。
AI.keywords: 脑肿瘤分割 (brain tumour segmentation), 深度学习 (deep learning), 交互式分割 (interactive segmentation), 磁共振成像 (MR images)
AI.comments: 该研究的重要价值在于正视了全自动深度学习在临床实际应用（如不同厂商MR序列差异）中容易出现严重误差的局限性，提出了将全自动算法与人机协同交互（human-in-the-loop）相结合的务实方案。其局限性在于摘要中未提供具体的量化指标（如Dice系数提升），且可用性研究目前仅为初步的观察性评估，尚需更大规模的临床验证。

title: The Exact Stabilization Time of Self-Stabilizing Coloring: Mean, Variance, and Distribution
summary: The worst-case stabilization time of a self-stabilizing algorithm usually says little about its typical behavior beyond the order of magnitude. This paper revisits the classical self-stabilizing $Delta+1$ coloring algorithm with vertices activated at random, one at a time (the random central daemon). Considering the number of color changes as a random variable, we study its mean, variance and, on several families of graphs, its exact distribution. The analysis rests on a reduction: a vertex changes color, at most once, exactly when it is not a local maximum of a uniformly random labeling of the vertices, maxima being taken among the neighbors that share its initial color (the monochrome initial configuration is the slowest case). What can be predicted depends on what is known of the graph. The degree distribution (the view at distance one) gives the mean. The variance needs the view at distance two, in particular the triangles, and the full law needs the whole graph. We give closed-form results, from monochrome and from uniformly random initial configurations, on paths, cycles, random trees, Erdős-R{é}nyi graphs and bipartite random graphs. From a monochrome start, the mean stays within a factor two of the worst case, whereas the variance ranges from zero (disjoint cliques) to order $n^2$ (the star on $n$ vertices)..

title: LACCO: Local Accumulation with Computation--Communication Overlap
summary: Training language models across low-bandwidth networks requires reducing synchronization overhead. Local optimization methods such as DiLoCo communicate only after several local steps, but outer gradient averaging and the outer update remain on the critical path. Existing computation-communication overlap methods avoid this stall through delayed or replica-local updates, which can degrade convergence or cause replicas to drift. We propose LACCO (Local Accumulation with Computation-Communication Overlap), a two-stage algorithm that overlaps global communication with local computation while applying globally aggregated updates shared by every replica, without introducing staleness in the outer update. We establish convergence guarantees for smooth non-convex objectives. Experiments on language-model pre-training with FineWeb show that LACCO consistently outperforms communication-overlapped baselines such as Eager and Delayed DiLoCo. These gains remain robust as model size scales up to 0.5B parameters and across a range of communication intervals and numbers of replicas up to 16 workers, while incurring only negligible-or fully overlappable-computational or memory overhead, which demonstrates the strength of LACCO.

title: Understanding the limits of snapshot-based fault diagnosis in distribution networks
summary: Inverter-based resources weaken fault currents in distribution networks, and snapshot-based diagnosis, which classifies a fault from voltage phasors at a few buses at one instant, offers a cheap first-stage screen. Its published accuracies, however, rest on different noise assumptions and do not show whether the error comes from the classifier, the features, the measurement error, or the fault resistance. This paper separates these sources on three IEEE test feeders and a public data set with distributed generation, using four feature sets, thirteen classifiers, and measurement error defined by total vector error classes. The classifier is not the limiting factor, because the full phasor snapshot classifies every fault correctly without noise, and the remaining error comes from measurement error on high-impedance faults. Three voltage sensors classify 90-96% of faults at the 1% accuracy class and 96-99% with distribution micro phasor measurement units (micro-PMUs). A discriminability-margin placement selects them from simulations alone in under one second and matches the best of twelve placement methods. The results show when snapshot-based diagnosis can be trusted.

title: Reusing Locomotion Training Recipes Across Humanoids via Body-Aligned Virtual Joints
summary: Reinforcement learning has enabled robust humanoid locomotion, yet training recipes (rewards, architectures, hyperparameters) remain hard to reuse across robots with different native joint coordinates, since policies output native joint angles while action scales, bounds, gains, and penalties are defined in those robot-specific coordinates. Existing transmission models convert native targets into actuator commands but do not standardize the coordinate interface exposed to the policy. We introduce a body-aligned virtual joint space upstream of this mapping: policy actions and observations follow a common anatomical convention, and a deterministic kinematic layer maps virtual targets to native ones, leaving the existing transmission and low-level control stack unchanged. Under a single unmodified recipe on three humanoids with different leg-axis layouts, it is the only interface that tracks accurately, keeps the feet aligned with the travel direction, and trains stably on all three, and on Unitree G1 hardware it reduces heading drift by nearly a factor of six.

title: RiverScan: Learning to Accumulate on River Networks
comments: 17 pages including references and appendices; 6 figures, 5 tables
summary: Accurate runoff prediction across large river basins requires models to capture heterogeneous local hydrological responses and their accumulation downstream. River-network connectivity provides a natural structure for this task, but using it effectively requires learning how to combine contributions from subcatchments of different sizes. We frame this challenge as learning to accumulate and introduce RiverScan, a spatial operator based on area-weighted selective state-space recurrence. RiverScan recursively combines local temporal representations with accumulated upstream states in topological order. Contributing-area fractions account for subcatchment size, while learned retention controls how upstream information persists downstream. Experiments on 608 stations in the Danube basin show that RiverScan outperforms the evaluated temporal and graph baselines in overall predictive performance. Structural controls and ablations demonstrate that composing heterogeneous subcatchment representations in a manner aligned with hydrological accumulation substantially improves runoff prediction, with the benefits of correct topology growing along the river-network hierarchy. These findings establish physically structured accumulation as an effective inductive bias for hydrological modeling and motivate finer-grained, fully distributed AI-based hydrological models.
comment: 17 pages including references and appendices; 6 figures, 5 tables

title: RecurIR: Learning When and How to Revise Restoration Policies via Recursive Self-Improvement
summary: Agent-based image restoration has achieved promising performance by coordinating restoration tools to handle heterogeneous and coupled degradations. However, existing agents often improve their decisions through accumulated successful and failed executions, without explicitly identifying the conditions under which learned restoration strategies remain effective. Consequently, changes in degradation severity, spatial coverage, or interactions may invalidate previous decisions, while providing limited guidance on how these decisions should be revised. In this paper, we propose \textbf{RecurIR}, a recursive self-improvement framework that enables restoration agents to learn when and how to revise their decision rules. Specifically, we introduce a policy-hypothesis discovery mechanism to identify testable, condition-dependent rules through matched tool executions. We then design a rule-falsification-driven task evolution mechanism to generate targeted degradation variations, examine the validity of learned rules, and identify their applicability boundaries. Based on the resulting evidence, we develop a change-conditioned policy revision mechanism that learns how variations in degradation conditions should modify tool selection, execution order, operation strength, and processing regions. We further incorporate independent verification to retain effective revisions and use the resulting feedback to guide subsequent hypothesis discovery and task evolution. Through this recursive process, RecurIR progressively refines its restoration policies as degradation conditions change. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

title: Sample-Efficient Control of Magnetoconvective Flows via Differentiable Simulation
summary: Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) fluid flows are central to demanding engineering applications, most prominently fusion blanket cooling, where flow control is a promising tool to optimize key properties such as heat transfer. While active flow control (AFC) has recently advanced through machine learning, its application to MHD flows remains largely unexplored. In this work, we present $φ$-PICT, a novel differentiable GPU-accelerated MHD solver targeted at AFC. We validate $φ$-PICT against MHD benchmarks and demonstrate its high computational efficiency. Integrated into FluidGym, $φ$-PICT enables sample-efficient gradient-based algorithms to improve heat transfer by $>25$% and allows optimizers to achieve $10^3\times$ higher accuracy in inverse design than black-box methods. $φ$-PICT is publicly available at https://github.com/upb-sciml/phiPICT.

title: Conflict, Feasibility, Faithfulness, Displacement: Four Quantities That Come Apart in Federated Dual-Cone Aggregation
summary: FedFV, FedGH and FedMGDA+ aggregate client updates with multi-objective gradient aggregators to remove conflict between them. We examine this rationale with UPGrad, which increases no client's loss to first order, in a comparison that changes only the direction of FedAvg's update. Four quantities the rationale treats as one -- conflict between client updates, feasibility of their weighted mean, faithfulness of the transmitted updates to the clients' gradients, and displacement of the update -- come apart. Under Dirichlet partitioning UPGrad improves CIFAR-10 accuracy by +0.78 pp (14/15 seeds, p < 0.001), only with full participation; on Oxford-IIIT Pet its +0.52 pp gain vanishes (+0.07 pp) once the data our protocol left unused are kept. Varying only the Dirichlet concentration, the gain grows with heterogeneity, yet the split with the most conflict shows none. Uniform client weights, blind to conflict, match the CIFAR-10 gain and exceed the Pets gain; a matched random rotation does neither. No fairness effect survives multiplicity correction, and on CIFAR-10 the guarantee does not reach the clients' gradients. We state what evaluations should report.

AI.title_translation: 冲突、可行性、忠实度与位移：联邦对偶锥聚合中分崩离析的四个量
AI.tldr: 论文揭示了联邦学习多目标梯度聚合中梯度冲突与性能收益之间的脱节，指出消除冲突的理论假设在实践中难以成立。
AI.motivation: 现有联邦学习方法（如FedFV、FedGH、FedMGDA+）利用多目标梯度聚合器消除客户端更新之间的冲突，但该研究旨在审视这一基本理论前提是否成立。
AI.method: 采用UPGrad算法（在一阶近似下不增加任何客户端损失）进行受控对比实验，仅改变FedAvg的更新方向，并在不同数据异构度（Dirichlet划分）、参与率及协议设置下系统评估更新方向、冲突与性能的关系。
AI.result: UPGrad在全参与下仅使CIFAR-10精度提升0.78个百分点；在Oxford-IIIT Pet上的提升在计入协议未用数据后降至0.07个百分点；冲突最大的数据划分未带来性能增益；未考虑冲突的均匀客户端权重能达到同等甚至更佳效果；公平性效果在多重性校正后不复存在，且理论保证无法有效传递至客户端真实梯度。
AI.conclusion: 多目标梯度聚合所依赖的理论逻辑在实际联邦学习中存在脱节；现有观察到的性能提升并非真正源于梯度冲突的消除，评估方案应规范报告完整的数据利用率和多重校正结果。
AI.translation: FedFV、FedGH 和 FedMGDA+ 等方法采用多目标梯度聚合器来聚合客户端更新，以消除它们之间的冲突。我们借助 UPGrad（其在一阶近似下不会增加任何客户端的损失）在仅改变 FedAvg 更新方向的对比中审视了这一理论逻辑。该逻辑视为一体的四个物理量——客户端更新之间的冲突、其加权平均值的可行性、传输更新对客户端梯度的忠实度，以及更新的位移——实际上彼此脱节。在狄利克雷划分下，UPGrad 使 CIFAR-10 的准确率提升了 0.78 个百分点（14/15 随机种子，p < 0.001），但这仅在全参与时发生；在 Oxford-IIIT Pet 数据集上，一旦保留我们实验协议中未使用的剩余数据，其原本 +0.52 个百分点的增益便缩减至 +0.07 个百分点。仅改变狄利克雷浓度时，增益随异构性增加而增长，但冲突最严重的数据划分却没有带来任何增益。对冲突完全不敏感的均匀客户端权重能取得与 CIFAR-10 相当的增益，并在 Pets 上表现更优；而匹配的随机旋转则均未达到效果。经多重性校正后，没有任何公平性效应得以留存，且在 CIFAR-10 上，该保证并未触及客户端的实际梯度。我们据此阐明了评估应当报告的内容。
AI.summary: 本文审视了联邦学习中基于多目标梯度聚合消除冲突的合理性。通过UPGrad分析发现，客户端更新冲突、加权均值可行性、更新忠实度以及位移这四种常被混为一谈的量在实际中存在脱节，实验表明所谓冲突消除带来的增益高度受限于特定评估条件，甚至可被简单的均匀加权替代。
AI.keywords: 联邦学习, 梯度冲突, 双锥聚合, 多目标优化, UPGrad
AI.comments: 该论文对当前联邦学习中利用多目标优化（对偶锥聚合）消除客户端梯度冲突的流行范式进行了深入的实证和理论解构。通过严格的控制变量实验，揭示了性能增益并非源于冲突消除，对现有方法的理论前提和评估规范提出了重要质疑。

title: On Structure-Aware SAT Solving
summary: Although modern SAT solvers have made remarkable progress, they still exploit formula structure only to a limited extent. We present two techniques that make SAT solving more structure-aware and provide experimental results showing their promise. The first technique ``$\mathit{melts}$'' the formula by reducing interaction between its parts. This is achieved by adding new variables, using existential quantifiers, and applying a procedure called partial quantifier elimination. The second technique exploits the notion of a $\mathit{local}$ $\mathit{proof}$. The latter establishes that a formula is unsatisfiable by proving that certain literals of its clauses are redundant. We show that using local proofs makes SAT solving more formula-specific.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了公式“融化”和“局部证明”两种使SAT求解更具结构感知性的新技术，有效增强了求解的公式针对性。
AI.motivation: 尽管现代SAT求解器取得了显著进展，但目前对布尔公式结构的挖掘和利用程度依然非常有限。
AI.method: 提出了两种结构感知技术：1. 公式“融化”技术：通过引入新变量、使用存在量词并结合部分量词消去（partial quantifier elimination），减少公式各部分之间的交互；2. 局部证明技术：通过证明子句中特定文字的冗余性来确立公式的不可满足性。
AI.result: 实验结果表明所提技术具有良好的前景，并证实使用局部证明能使SAT求解过程更具公式针对性。
AI.conclusion: 通过公式融化和局部证明等结构感知技术，能够更有效地利用公式内在结构，使SAT求解更具针对性且展现出良好的应用前景。
AI.translation: 尽管现代SAT求解器取得了显著进展，但它们对公式结构的利用仍然十分有限。我们提出了两种使SAT求解更具结构感知性的技术，并提供了展现其前景的实验结果。第一种技术通过减少公式各部分之间的交互来“融化”公式，这是通过添加新变量、使用存在量词并应用称为部分量词消去的过程来实现的。第二种技术利用了“局部证明”的概念，后者通过证明公式子句中的某些文字是冗余的来确立公式的不可满足性。我们证明了使用局部证明可以使SAT求解更具公式针对性。
AI.summary: 本文探讨了结构感知的SAT求解方法。针对现有求解器利用公式结构有限的问题，论文提出了两种新技术：一种是通过添加新变量与部分量词消去来降低各部分交互的公式“融化”技术；另一种是通过证明文字冗余性来判定不可满足性的“局部证明”技术。实验表明这些方法展现了良好的求解前景和更强的公式针对性。
AI.keywords: SAT求解, 结构感知, 公式融化, 部分量词消去, 局部证明
AI.comments: 本文针对现代SAT求解器对公式结构利用不足的瓶颈，创新性地提出了公式“融化”与“局部证明”两种利用深层结构特征的技术，为提高求解的针对性和效率提供了新途径。其局限在于摘要中未提供具体的实验基准与性能提升的量化数据。

title: Data-Driven Output Regulation via Predictive Control
summary: This paper addresses constrained output regulation for unknown linear systems by means of predictive control directly from input-output data. The objective is to reject disturbances and track references generated by a known exosystem, without identifying a plant model or solving the output regulator equations. The first step is a trajectory parametrization for plants driven by exosignals with known dynamics. % By exploiting the known exosystem eigenstructure, Willems et al's fundamental lemma is extended from autonomous input-output trajectories to trajectories coupled with exogenous modes. By exploiting the known exosystem eigenstructure, input-output trajectories driven by an exosignal of known phase are parametrized directly from data, which contains the affine version of Willems et al.'s fundamental lemma as a special case. This parametrization yields a nominal data-driven predictive control (DDPC) regulator, for which a Lyapunov argument proves exponential convergence to the regulator manifold. For periodic exosignals, the steady-state feedforward input is eliminated from the online problem through an incremental-input regularization, leading to an implementable regulator based on measured data and known exosystem information. Bounded output noise is handled by slack and coefficient regularization, with a regularization center computed offline from data; the resulting robust DDPC law is recursively feasible and practically stabilizing, with an ultimate regulation error that vanishes with the noise bound. A constrained lateral vehicle-control example with periodic road curvature illustrates disturbance rejection, input-constraint satisfaction, and the transition from exact regulation with noise-free data to practical regulation with noisy data.

AI.title_translation: 基于预测控制的数据驱动输出调节
AI.tldr: 提出了一种直接利用输入输出数据且无需模型辨识的预测控制方法，成功实现了未知线性系统在已知外部系统驱动下的约束鲁棒输出调节。
AI.motivation: 针对未知线性系统的约束输出调节问题，旨在无需辨识被控对象模型或求解输出调节器方程的情况下，直接利用输入输出数据抑制由已知外部系统产生的扰动并跟踪设定参考。
AI.method: 利用已知外部系统特征结构将Willems等人的基本引理扩展到外部模态耦合轨迹，直接从数据中参数化输入输出行为；构建名义数据驱动预测控制（DDPC）调节器并通过Lyapunov方法证明指数收敛；针对周期外部信号引入增量输入正则化消除稳态前馈；针对有界输出噪声采用离线计算中心的松弛与系数正则化以确保递归可行性和实际稳定性。
AI.result: 通过周期性道路曲率的约束车辆横向控制算例验证了该方法，展示了扰动抑制能力、输入约束满足性，以及从无噪声数据的精确调节向含噪声数据实际调节的平滑过渡。
AI.conclusion: 基于预测控制与扩展的轨迹参数化方法，可仅依赖输入输出数据和已知的外部系统动态，实现未知线性系统的鲁棒约束输出调节。
AI.translation: 本文通过直接基于输入输出数据的预测控制，研究了未知线性系统的约束输出调节问题。其目标是在不辨识被控对象模型或不求解输出调节器方程的情况下，抑制由已知外部系统产生的扰动并实现参考跟踪。第一步是针对由已知动态特性的外部信号驱动的被控对象进行轨迹参数化。通过利用已知的外部系统特征结构，将已知相位的外部信号驱动的输入输出轨迹直接从数据中进行参数化，将Willems等人的基本引理（仿射版本为其特例）进行了推广。该参数化方法推导出了名义数据驱动预测控制（DDPC）调节器，并通过Lyapunov方法证明了其向调节器流形的指数收敛性。针对周期性外部信号，通过增量输入正则化从在线问题中消除了稳态前馈输入，从而构建了基于测量数据和已知外部系统信息的可实现调节器。通过松弛变量和系数正则化（正则化中心由数据离线计算得到）处理有界输出噪声；所得鲁棒DDPC律具有递归可行性并实现实际稳定，其最终调节误差随噪声界限趋于零。具有周期性道路曲率的受约束车辆横向控制示例展示了扰动抑制、输入约束满足情况，以及从无噪声数据的精确调节向含噪声数据的实际调节的过渡过程。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种用于未知线性系统约束输出调节的数据驱动预测控制方法。该方法直接利用输入输出数据和已知的外部系统动态特性对轨迹进行参数化，消除了模型辨识和调节方程求解过程。在名义条件下证明了其指数收敛性，并通过增量输入正则化及松弛机制分别解决了周期外部扰动消除和有界测量噪声下的鲁棒镇定问题，数值仿真验证了算法的有效性。
AI.keywords: 数据驱动控制, 预测控制, 输出调节, Willems基本引理, 鲁棒控制
AI.comments: 该研究的创新之处在于成功将基于Willems基本引理的行为系统理论扩展到了由外部系统驱动的受扰/跟踪场景，避免了复杂的系统辨识及求解Francis输出调节方程的传统步骤。提出的增量输入正则化与松弛变量机制有效兼顾了周期扰动消除和有界噪声鲁棒性。其局限性可能在于依赖外部系统动态特征已知的先验假设，且计算复杂度随数据维度增加而上升。

title: RSSA: Robust Semantic and Spatial Aligner for Collaborative Perception
comments: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. 18 pages, 14 figures, 11 tables. Code: https://github.com/Megalo-f/RSSA
summary: V2X collaborative perception improves single-vehicle perception by aggregating multi-view features from collaborative agents. However, existing methods typically rely on simple spatial warping to align the collaborative features, which can cause semantic misalignment during fusion. Meanwhile, these deterministic warping-based methods are highly sensitive to the positional noises. In this paper, we propose a plug-in module called Robust Semantic and Spatial Aligner (RSSA), which performs semantic and probabilistic spatial transformations for robust feature alignment. Specifically, a Semantic Transformation (SemT) block modulates feature channels based on the observed relative pose to correct semantic inconsistencies. Subsequently, a Probabilistic Spatial Transformation (P-SpaT) block performs probabilistic warping by sampling from the Gaussian-modeled relative pose space. A Relative Transformation Augmentation (RT-Aug) strategy is further introduced to augment the relative poses and facilitate the training of the RSSA. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate that RSSA improves the state-of-the-art methods by a large margin under the configuration of both clean and noisy positions.
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026. 18 pages, 14 figures, 11 tables. Code: https://github.com/Megalo-f/RSSA

title: JaRS: Contrast-Free Localization of Memorized Regions in Diffusion Models via Jacobian Row Sums
summary: Diffusion models sometimes memorize and reproduce regions of their training images, raising privacy and copyright concerns. We aim to localize these regions. Existing contrast-based methods use the diagonal of the denoiser Jacobian, which reflects the posterior variance of each pixel. However, a small diagonal entry is ambiguous: it signals either memorization or averaging over many neighboring pixels in smooth or predictable regions. To resolve this ambiguity, these methods subtract a reference map, which requires a second evaluation with a null prompt or an earlier checkpoint. Unconditional models have no null prompt, and earlier checkpoints are unavailable in general. We show that Jacobian row sums (JaRS), unlike the diagonal, separate memorization from local averaging without a reference map. Pairing JaRS with an image-level detection score that uses the same statistic at an early denoising step yields JaRS+. Across Stable Diffusion v1.4 and v2.1, Realistic Vision v5.1, and an unconditional diffusion Transformer (DiT), JaRS+ outperforms contrast-based localization methods.

title: A Generalizable Approach to Safety-Aware Robotic Behavior Planning with an Explicit Constraint Space
summary: Large language and vision-language models have substantially advanced robotic behavior planning from natural-language instructions and visual observations. However, safe manipulation in tabletop environments remains challenging because the safety constraints required for a task depend on the surrounding scene and may not be explicitly specified in the instruction. We propose a safety-aware behavior planning framework based on an explicit Constraint Space that stores reusable textual safety rules. Rather than retrieving rules solely by semantic similarity, we formulate constraint selection as task- and environment-conditioned applicability learning. A lightweight query-conditioned dual-tower model identifies the constraints applicable to the current context, which are then provided together with the original task and image to a multimodal behavior planner. To handle incorrect constraint selections and previously unseen hazards, we introduce a multimodal Safety Inspector that evaluates generated primitive plans, reconstructs the complete applicable constraint set, and provides corrective planning feedback. Validated inspection feedback is further used for test-time adaptation of constraint applicability and parameter-efficient adaptation of the Safety Inspector through LoRA, while newly identified constraints are incorporated into the Constraint Space. The resulting framework integrates explicit safety knowledge representation,context-aware constraint selection, corrective safety inspection, and test-time knowledge adaptation for safety-aware robotic behavior planning.

title: Beyond Bot Labels: Retrospective Consequence-Grounded Ranking of Attributed Cache Harm in E-Commerce Logs
comments: 11 pages, 4 figures, 7 tables. Accepted to appear in Proc. of the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData 2026), Phoenix, AZ, USA. This is the author's accepted manuscript
summary: Web caches reduce origin load and latency, but automated traffic can either warm them or evict objects shoppers reuse, lowering the cache hit ratio (CHR). Existing bot defenses generally infer automation from User-Agent (UA) strings or behavior rather than identify sessions that impose cross-session cache harm. We instead formulate the task as ranking sessions by eviction damage and propose consequence-grounded session ranking. A single chronological replay attributes each eviction-induced miss by a protected shopping session (a victim) to the session whose insertion last evicted the object. A behavioral model predicts the target from session behavior alone. Selected sessions bypass the cache but remain origin-served. In a controlled check of 539 non-victim sessions selected across harm levels, attribution order tracks victim-hit changes after removal (Spearman correlation 0.80). On a 12.7-million-request real trace, the top 1% of sessions carry 48.8% of attributed harm. Sessions without bot tags contribute 49.1% of this tier's harm. At the 20% request-volume target, the default conditional CHR difference reaches 93% of the UA baseline, which selects 47 times as many sessions. Six training seeds show little variation. This comparison conditions on the victims that remain, so we also report victim bypass. Local replay and retraining on a second store reproduce harm concentration and a top tier dominated by sessions without bot tags. These results establish attributed cross-session harm as an outcome-based target for retrospective cache audits and selective intervention design.
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, 7 tables. Accepted to appear in Proc. of the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData 2026), Phoenix, AZ, USA. This is the author's accepted manuscript

title: Long rational and Gaussian integer multiplication
summary:
Long integer multiplication is a fundamental operation in computational algebra, heavily relying on Toom--Cook and related evaluation-interpolation algorithms. Conventional wisdom dictates that multiplication on the Gaussian integers $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ is reduced to standard rational integer multiplication, since $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ is a ring extension of $\mathbb{Z}$. We show that this approach is far from optimal and moreover inverting this established paradigm, that is reducing rational to Gaussian multiplication, leads to faster rational integer multiplication algorithms.
  We introduce a novel Toom--Cook framework that reduces rational long integer multiplication to Gaussian integer multiplication, yielding a strictly more efficient computational pipeline. By taking advantage of the special properties of the rational integer domain inside the Gaussian integers, we achieve a more favourable algebraic structure that reduces the overall arithmetic cost in every metric. To validate this theoretical shift, we provide a complete implementation of our algorithm. Benchmarks demonstrate that our approach outperforms the highly optimised GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library (GMP) by up to 29\%, bridging a fundamental theoretical insight with significant practical improvements in high-performance computer algebra.

title: PerfArena: Ranking LLMs by Code Performance
summary: Industry now relies on LLMs to write a large share of production code. Although that code is mostly, but not always, correct, correctness alone does not determine whether it is fit for repeated and extensive use, which depends on what the code costs in time, memory and energy. Most code-generation benchmarks nonetheless evaluate correctness in isolation, and most performance-oriented benchmarks cover few languages and rarely measure energy consumption. To address this gap, we present PERFARENA, an open-source, reproducible arena that ranks LLMs by the performance of their generated code across multiple languages and competitions. PERFARENA executes the solutions of each LLM on a Unix-like host and reports correctness together with latency, peak memory, and energy consumption. Correctness oracles, performance oracles, profilers, and code-generation workflows are pluggable in PERFARENA, enabling the integration of new judging backends and measurement tools without changing the pipeline. We evaluate PERFARENA on two competitions: CLBGComp, 10 compute-intensive benchmarks from the Computer Language Benchmarks Game, and LeetCodeComp, 99 LeetCode problems whose accepted solutions differ measurably in latency. Currently, PERFARENA holds 9,455 correct and measured solutions from 13 state-of-the-art LLMs across 7 programming languages. Across both competitions, got-6-astra is the only LLM that no other LLM beats significantly in latency, energy consumption, or peak memory, solving 99.7% of LeetCodeComp and 100% of CLBGComp. All PERFARENA leaderboards and measured solutions are publicly available, providing a continuously updated reference that helps developers choose an LLM per language and metric, instead of relying only on correctness rates or pricing.

title: Latent resonances in oscillator networks
comments: 22 pages, 5 figures, Supplementary Materials included (6 figures, 7 tables)
summary: In networks of coupled oscillators, from neural circuits to power grids, damping is expected to suppress oscillations because of its dissipativity. Here we show that local damping can, counterintuitively, amplify oscillations along some input-output channels, while the network's global oscillation energy decreases and its spectral properties improve. The amplified oscillation arises from a latent resonance that lies in the spectrum yet barely manifests. The added passive damping reshapes this resonance by mixing it with adjacent eigenmodes. In random power-grid networks, damping can boost weakly responding channels by more than an order of magnitude, while subdominant channels can grow to exceed the originally strongest channel. Damping thus not only suppresses oscillations but also provides a way to redistribute oscillatory energy. For any passive network, the amplified response and its upper bound follow exactly from baseline quantities, offering a principled route for network design and control.
comment: 22 pages, 5 figures, Supplementary Materials included (6 figures, 7 tables)

title: Multi-level latent-diffusion adaptation for cross-region point cloud segmentation of ancient terraces
summary: Automated lidar feature detection from lidar point clouds can support archaeological surveys, but models trained in one landscape may transfer poorly to another because of differences in terrain, vegetation, acquisition characteristics, and feature morphology. We address this problem for cross-region detection of ancient terraces using transductive unsupervised domain adaptation that exploits an unlabelled target survey. We propose MELD (Multi-level Embedding-space Latent Diffusion), which trains separate diffusion denoisers on target-domain representations at four hierarchical PointNet++ feature levels. These target distribution priors are then used to refine source representations during supervised training and target representations during inference, allowing adaptation to act directly on the multi-scale features consumed by the segmentation decoder. We additionally investigate local geometric descriptors derived from K-nearest-neighbour neighbourhoods, including surface normals, slope, and aspect. MELD is evaluated bidirectionally between the Teyuna and Miraflores lidar surveys in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Colombia, against a source-only model and nine configurations of established domain adaptation approaches. MELD raises F1 over the source-only model from 0.397 to 0.459 for Teyuna-to-Miraflores transfer and from 0.557 to 0.594 in the reverse direction, achieving the highest F1 among the evaluated adaptation methods in both directions. Adding local geometry further raises F1 to 0.542 and 0.606, respectively. Multi-level ablation shows that refining all four PointNet++ levels provides the strongest performance in both directions. These results show that explicit modelling of target feature distributions in hierarchical point cloud feature space, complemented by local geometry, provides an effective route to cross-region archaeological mapping without target labels.

title: From institutional journalism to political extremes: Structural asymmetries in YouTube's news recommender during the 2022 French presidential campaign
summary: Debate has intensified over how algorithmic recommendations shape news visibility, particularly regarding structural and ideological bias. This study examines YouTube's News Recommender System (NRS) in the French ``News'' section, using a large-scale audit based on automated browsing agents operating under cold-start conditions, without prior viewing history, to isolate the algorithm's structural baseline independently of user preferences. Our results reveal that YouTube's NRS operates within a structurally asymmetric visibility regime: even in the absence of prior user behaviour, recommendation outputs disproportionately privilege platform-native creators and politically engaged content over established journalism. Television channels retain some relative advantage, but institutional news outlets, particularly press and radio, are systematically marginalised across recommendation sequences. Among political content, figures affiliated with far-left and far-right movements occupy a disproportionately visible position in recommendation outputs. Rather than correcting this asymmetry, continuity effects reproduce and stabilise it across recommendation sequences. These results show that visibility in YouTube's News section cannot be reduced to accumulated user preferences alone, but is also shaped by a structural bias embedded in the platform's recommendation system, which plays an important role in sustaining the prominence of political actors affiliated with the far left and far right.

title: RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$: On-Device Reinforcement Learning Runtime
summary: On-device reinforcement learning runs a periodic actor and a learner on one embedded GPU shared with other workloads. Because the learner produces the actor's weights, existing designs stall the actor or let its policy drift. We present RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$, an on-device runtime that makes this coupling a tunable parameter: a refresh bound limits actor releases between refreshes, and a GPU permit with slack-aware admission prioritises the actor and fills spare time with training atop any base scheduler. Under the real refresh cost on two Jetson boards, RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$ keeps a 16.8 M-parameter policy's deadline misses below 1%, against 85 to 100% without it.

title: C-to-Rust Translation Validation at the LLVM IR Level via AI-Assisted Refinement Proof
summary: Migrating C codebases to Rust is a promising approach to securing legacy software, but existing translators do not guarantee that a translated Rust program preserves the behavior of the C program. Neither rule-based nor large language model (LLM)-based translators have been formally verified, and existing approaches to checking translation correctness are limited to testing and bounded checks, which cannot reason about all possible executions. In this work, we present R2C2, which validates C-to-Rust translation by proving in Rocq that the Rust program refines the C program, i.e., every behavior on the Rust side is also a behavior on the C side. Since no formal semantics defines the behaviors of C and Rust programs in the same terms, we prove refinement between the two programs compiled to the LLVM intermediate representation (LLVM IR). In addition, to resolve the discrepancies between the data representations of C and Rust, we introduce a common abstraction that relates two corresponding representations through an abstract value, and specify the behavior of each library function over abstract values. We construct the refinement proof as a chain of refinement relations, where only one relation is program-specific and proved at validation time, while the others are proved for all programs in advance. Proof construction is automated by AI agents, and since Rocq checks the proofs, the agents need not be trusted. We evaluate R2C2 on LLM translations of 519 C programs drawn from a benchmark suite used in prior work on C-to-Rust translation validation. R2C2 proves the translations of 486 programs correct without bounding their executions and discovers three incorrect translations, providing valid counterexamples that existing translation validation tools cannot find. We also conduct a case study on a small real-world image compression library and demonstrate how R2C2 can handle file operations.

title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
summary: Experimental optimization of perovskite solar cells is constrained by combinatorial diversity in absorber compositions, device layers, and processing, which makes virtual screening attractive for prioritizing recipes before fabrication. We develop a surrogate-guided reinforcement-learning framework that casts recipe generation as virtual screening, enriching candidate shortlists near high-performing experimental neighbors. A frozen Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) guides recipe generation, while a reference pool of 890 measured devices enables neighborhood-based assessment. Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices shows top-ten selection raises mean power conversion efficiency (PCE) from 19.68\% to 23.74\%. Three learned policies are compared with six baselines under 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run. In top-100 shortlists, Proximal policy optimization (PPO) and recurrent PPO (RPPO) achieve neighborhood-supported hit rates of 23\% and 24\% (7.9- and 8.3-fold Pure Random's 2.9\%), versus 10\% (3.4-fold) for the baselines with the highest supported hit rate (L-SHADE and Ax BO, tied) at $K = 100$. Gains coexist with weak-support fractions. Of 9,000 recipes, 65.4\% match a composition family at similarity 0.80, falling to 11.7\% at 0.90. Results support enrichment-oriented prioritization but not experimental performance, seed robustness, or matched-budget advantage.

title: FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls
summary: When a conversational Voice AI agent places an outbound call, the far end may be a live person, a voicemail greeting, an interactive voice response (IVR) system, or increasingly another AI system answering on the callee's behalf. Standard Answering Machine Detection (AMD) reports only whether a human or a machine picked up, a design meant for human call centres, where one machine is as uninteresting as another. That single bit does not tell a Voice AI agent what to do, since leaving a voicemail message, navigating an IVR and holding a short exchange with another AI are three different actions and a two-valued label cannot distinguish them. In 1,000 randomly sampled calls from our own outbound deployment, a live person answered 48.1%, a voicemail system 44.6%, an AI 6.9% and an IVR 0.4%. Our proposed framework, FEND, reads the far end's audio and its streaming transcript and runs one detector for each automated class (voicemail, IVR, AI callee), with human the default when nothing fires, returning a single label within 20 seconds. On a public benchmark the voicemail components reach 100% accuracy without ever misclassifying a live human, where Asterisk's AMD misclassifies 30 to 66% of them. For the AI callee, acoustic features do not transfer across recording conditions, but speech timing does, separating AI from human at 0.952 ROC-AUC, because synthesised speech leaves far shorter gaps between words. On production traffic, separating a live person from any automated far end reaches F1 0.979, and only 2.9% of live people are given an automated label, the error that matters most for an agent acting on the result.

title: InfiHall-Bench: A Benchmark for Hallucination Evaluation in Autoregressive Text-to-Image Generation
summary:
Hallucination benchmarks for text-to-image generation are predominantly designed around diffusion models, limiting their diagnostic value for visual autoregressive (VAR) models and the development of mitigation methods. We identify two limitations in existing prompt construction paradigms: many prompts are no longer challenging for modern generators, while category-based construction relies on recurring object-attribute-relation templates and rarely tests interactions among multiple visual requirements within a single image.
  We introduce InfiHall-Bench, a controlled benchmark of 411 prompts constructed by systematically composing five foundational and visually verifiable skills: attribute binding, spatial relation, action relation, part consistency, and scene consistency. Each prompt covers 4.05 annotated skills on average, enabling the evaluation of hallucinations under diverse combinations of visual requirements. Using this benchmark, we find that hallucinations in VAR models exhibit a scale-wise persistence pattern: semantic errors can emerge at different autoregressive scales and are rarely corrected by subsequent fine-scale steps.
  Motivated by this observation, we propose Confidence-Masked Hallucination Mitigation (CMHM), which estimates the prediction confidence of target visual tokens at each autoregressive scale during teacher-forced fine-tuning. CMHM downweights reliably predicted tokens, allowing optimization to focus on uncertain predictions across scales. Experiments show that InfiHall-Bench distinguishes models that existing compositional benchmarks rate as comparable, while CMHM consistently outperforms uniform LoRA fine-tuning for VAR-based text-to-image generation.

title: DeCompCert: A Verified Decompiler for CompCert-Generated AArch64
summary: DeCompCert is a Rocq-verified decompiler for AArch64 assembly generated by CompCert. It reconstructs CompCert C through nine reverse passes, combining deductively verified transformations with translation validation. Untrusted OCaml and Datalog analyses propose candidate reconstructions, while verified validators accept only candidates that satisfy the required semantic correspondence. The composed correctness theorem guarantees that every defined, safe behavior of an accepted C reconstruction is matched by the input CompCert assembly; under a safety assumption, the two programs are observationally equivalent. We evaluate DeCompCert on approximately 2.16 million lines of C. With exact function and call signatures, it reconstructs and recompiles all 3,173 eligible contexts under both unoptimized and optimized CompCert pipelines. Without retained signatures, its cumulative inference portfolio validates 2,606 of 3,164 contexts (82.4%), while the platform-plus-IDA configuration validates 2,407 contexts (76.1%). Native execution and output-quality experiments further evaluate the generated C and characterize the remaining limitations in signature recovery and source resemblance.

title: SWAM: Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging for Efficient Vision Transformers
summary: Vision Transformers (ViTs) achieve strong performance on image recognition tasks, yet their quadratic self-attention complexity over input tokens creates prohibitive computational costs for practical deployment. Token reduction methods offer a practical solution by progressively reducing the token sequence during the forward pass. We propose Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging (SWAM), a training-based token merging framework that extends the Bipartite Soft Matching (BSM) with two saliency-aware mechanisms. We introduce a two-step matching formulation in which cosine similarity decides candidate pairs, while a multiplicative maximum saliency penalty regulates their selection for merging. We then further use asymmetric exponential saliency-weighted aggregation, which allows more salient tokens to contribute more strongly to the merged representation. A lightweight MLP-based saliency prediction module (75k parameters per stage, 1% of backbone parameters) supervised via attention rollout is trained end-to-end jointly with a DeiT-Small backbone using a composite cross-entropy, knowledge-distillation, and saliency-alignment objective. On CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-100, under a conservative schedule that reduces tokens from 196 to 100 patch tokens, with the CLS token retained throughout, 27.5% FLOPs reduction and 1.35 times speedup, SWAM matches or exceeds baseline across the reported results. Under an aggressive schedule (196 to 70 tokens with the CLS token kept throughout, 33.8% FLOPs reduction, and 1.46 times speedup), accuracy gains are achieved on ImageNet-100 (+0.23%) with minimal losses on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet.

title: A$^3$: Adaptive Audio Agent Framework for Collaborative Edge Computing
summary: Embedded audio agents need a nearby edge server for speed, but a server-dependent agent returns nothing when the link fails. We present A$^3$, an adaptive audio agent framework that places whole pipeline stages on the server, keeps a complete fallback agent on devices that can host one, and hedges both paths with a link-aware deadline that decides when to give up on the server. On Jetson devices and an RTX A4500 server, A$^3$ matches the server-only agent on a healthy link, answers every request in a full outage on the AGX, and beats a percentile hedge in simulated outages.

title: Agent-as-a-Judge
summary: Artificial intelligence has progressed from task-specific systems toward general models spanning perception, generation, reasoning, and autonomous interaction, making reliable evaluation essential for comparison, deployment, and post-training feedback. At scale, modern evaluation pipelines increasingly rely on LLM-as-a-Judge to produce scores, preferences, and critiques; in its fixed-context setting, the judge relies on the supplied evaluand and evaluation materials. Yet a reliable verdict may require evidence beyond the supplied evaluand and context---either because critical environmental states remain unrecorded in the static execution log, or because controversial factual claims require external verification. Passive judges cannot obtain that missing evidence before deciding, especially when evaluating agent trajectories, executable artifacts, or domain-specific reports. Recent work therefore develops active evaluators that seek missing evidence and update their grounds for judgment before deciding. We bring these advances together through Agent-as-a-Judge, focusing on how evaluators construct and control checking processes within the broader LLM-based judging landscape. We define the scope through evaluation-directed checks and the use of their results, covering both structured workflows and observation-driven control. We organize the design space by multi-agent collaboration, tool integration, memory, and planning, and show how these mechanisms supply the checks and evidence on which a verdict rests. We consolidate published scores and reproduce missing entries for key agentic judges; the comparison reveals uneven agentic gains and motivates dedicated agentic evaluation. We conclude by characterizing application demands and open challenges in cost, reliability, safety, and governance that condition trusted deployment of agentic judges at scale.

title: A Realizability-Based Kinetic-Fluid Domain Decomposition Method for Single-Temperature Gas Mixtures
summary: This paper introduces a domain-adaptive numerical method for multi-species kinetic models that relax toward a single-temperature and single-velocity hydrodynamic limit. To this end, we derive moment realizability matrices for this regime. In this way the ideas of Levermore, Morokoff, and Nadiga are extended to non-equilibrium mixtures in which inter-species and intra-species collisions occur at comparable rates, so that all species relax to a common velocity and a common temperature. The realizability conditions are used as an indicator to divide the computational domain, at each time step, into macroscopic and kinetic regions. In the kinetic regions, where the continuum description fails (e.g., across strong shocks, non-equilibrium interfaces, or kinetic boundary layers), the method solves the multi-species kinetic equations. Close to local thermodynamic equilibrium, the Euler equations of the mixture are solved instead. Confining the kinetic computations to the non-equilibrium regions reduces the simulation time, while the results remain close to those of the full kinetic solver. The method is discretized on Cartesian grids with high-order schemes in space and time. The kinetic equations are integrated with an Asymptotic-Preserving Implicit-Explicit (IMEX) scheme, so that a consistent discretization of the single-velocity, single-temperature Euler system of the mixture is recovered when the Knudsen number goes to zero. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first realizability-based adaptive spatial domain decomposition method for gas mixtures in this single-velocity, single-temperature setting.

title: Quantifying the Advantage of Coarser DPOR
summary:
Dynamic partial-order reduction (DPOR) has emerged as a promising approach to addressing interleaving explosion in bounded model checking of concurrent programs. Given an equivalence relation on interleavings, the model checker explores a program's executions while minimizing repeated visits to the same class; optimal model checkers avoid such repetition altogether. A coarser equivalence promises faster exploration by reducing the number of classes. This has motivated alternatives to Mazurkiewicz's trace equivalence such as reads-from and reads-value-from equivalence. This promise, however, does not always materialize in practice: while a coarser equivalence can yield exponentially fewer classes on some families of programs, it may offer little or no reduction for the program at hand.
  We show how to quantify the advantage of coarser equivalences for individual programs. We focus on the problem of counting the reads-from (RF) equivalence classes induced by a given program, as well as the problem of computing the ratio of RF to Mazurkiewicz class counts under sequential consistency. We show that both problems are $\#\mathrm{P}$-hard and that the reduction ratio remains hard to approximate accurately under standard complexity assumptions.
  Guided by these limits, we present CoEst, a sampling-based algorithm for estimating both the RF count and its ratio to the Mazurkiewicz count. For a fixed number of threads, each trial runs in polynomial time and yields unbiased count estimates. As the number of independent trials grows, the count and ratio estimates converge almost surely to their true values. Our algorithm can provide statistical evidence for deciding whether Mazurkiewicz or RF model checking is likely to be faster for a given program. In experiments across 34 benchmark configurations, our method selects the faster checker in 99.4% of runs using a one-minute estimation budget.

title: Measuring Public Participation in Local Government: An Audio-Based Instrument for Classifying Speakers in City Council Meetings
summary: How much does the public actually speak in local government? Despite sustained interest in democratic participation, we lack large-scale measures of public voice at the local level, because the underlying record -- audio of open meetings -- has been prohibitively costly to convert into data. We contribute a measurement instrument: an audio-analysis pipeline that classifies each speaker in a city council meeting as an elected official or a member of the public directly from audio, and aggregates these labels into validated measures of participation such as floor-time share. The pipeline first segments each recording by speaker, then classifies each speaker with a multimodal large language model (MLLM), using the meeting's own temporal structure (neighboring speakers, iterative refinement, and a majority vote across three classifiers) as supporting components. We collect 1,618 recordings from seven U.S. cities (2017-2023); after diarization and quality control, the analytic corpus is 1,565 meetings from five cities. The task is non-trivial: audio quality is uneven, members of the public speak informally and are often introduced only briefly, and speech frequently overlaps. Even so, segmentation reaches 89% accuracy (mean pairwise kappa=0.84), and the classifier reaches 87.7% accuracy (kappa=0.736, public-participant F1=0.832) on ground truth from five cities (N=1,761 speakers) -- agreement comparable to that among the human annotators themselves. At scale, members of the public receive a median of just 10% of floor time, the top speaker is an official in over 94% of meetings, and public participation declined over COVID-19 without recovering by 2023. The instrument measures participation directly from audio, without transcription or linkage to external voter or property records, establishing audio-as-data as a practical approach for the study of local politics.

title: Learning nonlinear interactions and cross-feature couplings with product-unit residual networks
summary: Understanding nonlinear feature interactions is crucial in science and engineering, yet standard multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) often capture such interactions only implicitly, leading to entangled representations that can impair robustness and interpretability. We investigate complex-valued product-unit residual networks (CV-PURe) that integrate multiplicative product units with residual connections to explicitly model cross-feature couplings while stabilizing optimization. We conduct a systematic evaluation on an interaction-driven synthetic benchmark and real-world datasets and evaluate prediction together with input-level interaction recovery under a reproducible protocol. Across five data splits and five training seeds, CV-PURe achieves the lowest mean RMSE on four of six scientific benchmarks, reducing Friedman error by 53.9% relative to MLP. Its Friedman interaction maps assign 60.7% of total strength to the known interacting pair, compared with 31.0% for MLP. On a synthetic task containing third- and fourth-order products and 20 distractors, CV-PURe reduces RMSE from 0.1376 to 0.0797 relative to a complex-valued MLP and recovers all nine true pairwise projections in every training/sampling repetition. Bike Sharing experiments connect improved prediction to the contribution of temporal, calendar, and seasonal context through paired ablations of both PURe variants. Parkinsons Telemonitoring extends the context analysis to repeated measurements. Noise and learning-curve evaluations demonstrate sustained predictive gains under perturbed inputs and limited supervision, while inference measurements quantify computational cost. This article extends our ICCS 2026 paper, Modeling Nonlinear Feature Interactions with Product-Unit Residual Networks (doi:10.1007/978-3-032-29921-5_6).

title: Zero-SM NCCL: A Systematic Guide to Designing and Deploying SM-Free GPU Communication
summary: GPU communication libraries such as NCCL use Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs) for data movement and synchronization, slowing overlapped computation at a cost that grows with interconnect bandwidth. We present Zero-SM NCCL, which communicates within and across scale-up domains without launching any SM kernel. It synchronizes through CUDA stream memory operations, moves data asynchronously with copy engines within a scale-up domain, and drives network RDMA from a stream-ordered CPU proxy. It supports data-movement collectives such as AllGather and AlltoAll, plus one-sided ncclPutSignal and ncclWaitSignal APIs. On GB200 NVL72 and B200 NVL8 systems, Zero-SM collectives reach up to 1.36x higher AllGather bandwidth than NCCL's legacy SM-based kernels and cut the median slowdown of overlapped GEMMs from 33% to 4%, at a higher latency per operation. In Megatron-LM training, they accelerate FSDP by up to 3.5%, and one-sided puts accelerate pipeline parallelism by up to 15%. Zero-SM communication is not a universal win, however. Through an end-to-end study across models and parallelism strategies, we show that it pays off for large transfers in GPU-bound workloads and for deep pipelines with large bubbles, but loses on small messages and host-bound workloads. We distill these findings into guidelines for enabling zero-SM communication in NCCL and building it into other libraries.

title: Grid-Compliance Testing of Wind Turbines through Virtualized Component Tests: Testing Concept and Test Bench
comments: 10 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables, peer-reviewed journal article
summary: As the proportion of inverter-connected wind turbines increases, test methods for evaluating their grid behavior are becoming increasingly important. This paper presents a Power Hardware-in-the-Loop (PHiL)-based method for grid connection testing of wind turbines. For the first time, geographically distributed simulations of aerodynamics via the Internet and of the grid model via a fiber-optic connection are integrated into certification-relevant tests. The concept expands upon the methods described in IEC TS 61400-21-4. Initial experimental results confirm high emulation quality and sufficiently low latencies, and meet the requirements for a standards-compliant grid emulation.
comment: 10 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables, peer-reviewed journal article

title: TelePhysica: Agentic Reconstruction of Physically Interactive Scenes
summary: Direct image-to-video diffusion models entangle pixel synthesis with implicit latent motion, precluding persistent 3D mechanical equilibrium, mid-rollout intervention, and counterfactual force control. Conversely, single-pass programmatic 3D reconstruction from an uncalibrated photograph leaves monocular depth and support clearance underconstrained, causing reconstructed scenes to interpenetrate or collapse under gravity. We present TelePhysica, a closed-loop framework that reconstructs an executable, multi-regime physical world from a single photograph to drive stateful 3D interaction and trajectory-grounded video synthesis. A vision-language coding agent synthesizes separable visual meshes and declarative physical models within a two-stage verification loop that pairs pixel-aligned silhouette critique with a zero-force gravitational equilibrium preflight. The verified world compiles into a unified solver coupling rigid bodies, articulated chains, co-dimensional cloth shells, and 3D tetrahedral elastodynamics, whose simulated rollouts condition pretrained video diffusion models through pixel-aligned structural streams. On a 100-scene single-image benchmark, closed-loop execution raises equilibrium-verified world recovery from $0\%$ in single-pass synthesis to $81\%$. Controlled constitutive ablations show over an order-of-magnitude larger localized corner displacement and out-of-plane pleating in finite-element cloth than in matched rigid-plate proxies. Conditioning video diffusion on simulated trajectories increases dynamic motion-mask overlap by $2{\times}\text{--}5{\times}$ and preserves motion direction under counterfactual force reversals where direct image-to-video models fail.

title: High-order IMEX local discontinuous Galerkin methods with sparse grids for high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDEs
summary: In this work, we develop a high-order IMEX-LDG scheme on sparse grids for solving nonlinear parabolic PDEs in moderate to high dimensions. The method combines the advantages of LDG methods for convection--diffusion problems, IMEX-RK time integrators for stiff systems, and sparse-grid techniques to mitigate the curse of dimensionality. The resulting scheme is fully parallelized in MPI, is robust, efficient, and scalable, making it suitable for a wide range of applications involving high-dimensional nonlinear parabolic PDEs.

title: Generalized hydraulic neural operators turbocharging sewer digital twins
summary: Hydraulic digital twins are emerging as the next-generation paradigm for operating and managing sewer systems. Conventional hydraulic digital twinning relies on running physics-based models (e.g., Saint-Venant equations), which are computationally expensive and often too slow for real-time applications. Although surrogates (e.g., neural networks) can be fast, existing approaches are typically non-generalizable, requiring costly retraining for unseen pipes, networks, or flow conditions. Here, we develop a fast, generalized and differentiable multi-branch neural operator trained on solutions of the Saint-Venant equations that predicts in-pipe hydraulics. The learned operator reproduces complex hydraulic dynamics with high fidelity while achieving thousand- to million-fold speedups for online prediction, data assimilation, and diagnostics. Equally importantly, the learned operator generalizes to unseen pipes, networks, and flow conditions without retraining. These advances address key computational barriers to real-time sewer digital twins, opening new opportunities for more responsive flood-risk management and protection of urban water environments.

title: On Applications of Polynomial-Time Group Isomorphism Algorithm
summary: The group isomorphism problem is a fundamental problem in computational group theory and is closely related to many other problems. Recently, Qiao and Zhang proposed a polynomial-time algorithm for finite group isomorphism in the multiplication-table model that computes the coset of all isomorphisms. Based on the algorithm of Qiao and Zhang, we study applications to finite associative ring isomorphism, bilinear map isotopism over finite commutative rings and free three-tensor isomorphism over finite commutative rings. First, we obtain a polynomial-time algorithm that returns the coset of all isomorphisms for finite associative rings. Second, we extend efficient isotopism and isomorphism algorithms for bilinear maps and free three-tensors from fields to general finite commutative rings.

title: Distributed Output-Feedback Control for Linear Multichannel Systems
summary: This paper investigates distributed output-feedback stabilization of linear multichannel systems in which agents exchange state estimates without disclosing local control inputs or feedback gains. Remote control actions are treated as unknown inputs and geometrically decoupled from stable quotient-error dynamics. The proposed framework accommodates nontrivial intersections of local loss subspaces by retaining the coupling between the plant and common estimation errors. A Hurwitz condition on the coupled dynamics, together with a sufficient consensus-gain bound, guarantees exponential closed-loop convergence for every fixed feedback selection in a compact family. For polytopic feedback families, a quotient-preserving parameterization of output injections enables joint synthesis of nominal feedback and observer gains via alternating linear matrix inequalities, followed by a convex semidefinite program certifying a common consensus gain. A numerical example demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed design.

title: Two-Clustering Regime of Token Dynamics in Causal Attention
summary: We partially resolve Conjecture 1 of [Karagodin et al., Clustering in Causal Attention Masking (NeurIPS 2024)] and extend it to time-dependent parameter regimes. The conjecture predicts that causal attention dynamics converge to two clusters aligned with the eigenvectors associated with the largest eigenvalue $λ_{\max}$ of the value transformation. We prove that this behavior holds when $λ_{\max}>0$ and is generally false when $λ_{\max}\le0$. The resulting two-cluster regime is common in practice and substantially more challenging than the classical single-cluster setting studied previously. A central contribution of our work is the identification of a rigorous dimension reduction phenomenon: despite evolving in a high-dimensional embedding space, token trajectories collapse onto a two-dimensional structure governed by a small number of dominant directions. Building on this insight, we introduce a new analytical framework--instability within the flow--inspired by instability phenomena in physical systems. This framework enables the analysis of steady-regime behavior in non-monotone, non-autonomous attention dynamics. Our theoretical findings are illustrated through simulations and experimental studies using Group Query Attention (GQA) layers.

title: Deep Latents, Long Memory: Latent persistence explains temporal correlations in transformer activations
summary: The hidden layers of Large Language Models (LLMs) are believed to encode representations of the data whose abstraction increases with depth. However, in the absence of an operational notion of abstraction, this statement is hard to test quantitatively. Here, we propose an alternative view, building on the principle that the correlations of a sequence reflect the structure of the process that generated it. We define the autocorrelation function of a layer as the average dot product between its activations at two context positions separated by a lag. Latent variables encoded persistently along the context create slowly decaying tails in the autocorrelation, and we find these tails to grow across layers in both synthetic and natural data. In synthetic data with controlled hierarchical latent structure, this growth stems from the encoding of abstract latent variables, which govern long stretches of the input. Indeed, the persistence of latent codes predicts the qualitative structure of autocorrelations and accounts for most of the empirical measures. In real text, we take sparse-autoencoder features as proxies for latent variables, and find that their persistence correlates strongly with the magnitude of autocorrelations across datasets and LLMs. In particular, the persistence time increases with depth, as do autocorrelations, implying that deeper latent features persist for longer context spans. We complement this analysis by explicitly ablating the persistent sparse-autoencoder features and observing a consequent decrease in the autocorrelations.

title: Bound-preserving finite volume scheme for a coupled parabolic system with nonlinear and nonlocal drift
summary: We propose a bound preserving finite-volume scheme for a coupled system of partial differential equations with nonlinear, nonlocal drift. The main contribution of this work is twofold: $(1)$ we show that the proposed scheme preserves physically motivated bounds; $(2)$ we prove that the scheme is well-posed and leads to a sequence of approximate solutions converging to the weak solution of the original problem. This setting is motivated by questions related to morphology formation in organic solar cells.

title: Beyond Scalar Inertia: Frequency-Response-Based Assessment of Finite-Duration Inertial Support in Grid-Forming Converters
comments: This paper has 6 pages with 5 figures. The target journal will be determined at a later stage
summary: Conventional scalar inertia characterizes only the low-frequency terminal behavior of grid-forming converters (GFMs) and cannot fully predict inertial energy delivery during short-duration frequency disturbances. This letter proposes a frequency-response-based method to assess finite-duration inertial support using complex terminal power--frequency responses, such as those provided by Network Frequency Perturbation (NFP) plots. For GFMs with nonzero steady-state droop, a duration-dependent energy-equivalent inertia is defined after subtracting the ideal static-droop contribution. An exact spectral relationship is established, expressing this metric as a duration-weighted integral of frequency-dependent inertia, without requiring knowledge of the internal controller structure and parameters. The duration dependence of the metric is further shown to encode observable oscillation frequencies and damping ratios.
