title: Grid-Forming AI Data Centers: Coordinated Grid Support Control from IT Loads and Energy Storage
summary: To exploit the grid-support capability of AI data centers (AIDCs), this paper proposes a grid-forming (GFM) control scheme which coordinates the IT loads and energy storage (ES) in the AIDC. First, the framework of a grid-connected AIDC is presented, with the multi-stage power conversion from the grid to the IT loads presented. A dual GFM scheme is then proposed for the back-to-back converters to provide grid support through coordinated power adjustments from IT loads and ES. In addition, an aggregated power response model is established to characterize the IT-load flexibility considering multiple IT servers executing diverse tasks. Time-domain simulations of a 100 MW grid-connected AIDC demonstrate that the proposed control scheme can effectively support the grid.

title: Do Underwater Image Quality Metrics Agree with Human Perception? A Benchmark with Human Choices, Simple Edits and Generative Drift
comments: Accepted at the 6th WVAQ Workshop, WACV 2027. 18 pages including appendix
summary: Underwater image enhancement is challenging to evaluate due to the lack of clean reference images, so researchers rely on no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) metrics. However, it remains unclear whether these metrics agree with human judgments. We evaluate 73 handcrafted underwater, learned underwater, vision-language and general-purpose metrics against human preferences on five references: four published opinion-score sets and a new paired-comparison study. For each metric, we measure how often it selects the same image as people when comparing versions of the same scene. We further test whether simple image edits and small adversarial perturbations raise metric scores above the enhancement people preferred, and whether scores decrease as repeated generative edits add noise. Our results show that no metric consistently matches human preferences. The best worst-case Cohen's kappa over the five references is only 0.23 (Q-Align), while two raters in our study agree with a median kappa of 0.41. The widely used UCIQE often favors edits that people reject. On a Nano Banana Pro replica chain that should leave the image unchanged, only 22 of 73 scores decrease at every checkpoint, while noise grows by 2.5 times. We also introduce TrustUIQA, a benchmark that combines the human references, our study choices, the edited, attacked and generated images, and the scores of every metric on every image. The code is available at https://github.com/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA and TrustUIQA at https://huggingface.co/datasets/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA.
comment: Accepted at the 6th WVAQ Workshop, WACV 2027. 18 pages including appendix

title: Towards Explainable Sleep Stage Classification using Single-Channel Electroencephalogram
comments: 8 pages, 4 figures. Accepted at AgIA4BioHealth Workshop, IEEE BIBM 2026, Dallas, Texas, December 1-4, 2026
summary: Automated sleep staging has achieved strong bench- mark accuracy; however, clinical adoption remains limited due to a lack of interpretability. In this work, we fill the research gap by extending the SleepXAI sleep staging framework to systematically compare five different XAI methods. Further, attribution fidelity is evaluated using Spearman rank correlation with AASM-defined EEG frequency bands, serving as clinically grounded reference signals. In this paper, we focus on single- channel Electroencephalogram (EEG), which is more amenable to practical clinical deployment compared to full polysomnography setups. Experiments are conducted on the Sleep-EDF benchmark dataset and the DREAMT dataset. In DREAMT, we stratified subjects based on OSA into four Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) severity groups. We observed that the SleepXAI model achieves strong classification performance on both datasets. Among the evaluated methods, Integrated Gradients (IG) consistently achieves the highest mean attribution fidelity across all five sleep stages on Sleep-EDF and across all AHI groups on DREAMT, outperforming all other evaluated methods under the Spearman rank correlation metric. These findings highlight the importance of attribution method selection as a key factor for ensuring reliable and clinically interpretable automated sleep staging systems.
comment: 8 pages, 4 figures. Accepted at AgIA4BioHealth Workshop, IEEE BIBM 2026, Dallas, Texas, December 1-4, 2026

title: Efficiency Gains in Social Science Research: A Prospective Silicon Sampling Protocol for Pre-Treatment and Code Optimization
summary: This study evaluates the methodological potential of using large language models (LLMs) to generate synthetic datasets prior to real-world data collection, thereby streamlining subsequent processing and statistical analysis. The approach is applied to a survey conducted within the France Life Imaging (FLI) network, leveraging three distinct LLMs (Sonnet 4.6, GPT 5.3, and Kimi 2.6) to simulate responses and prepare data processing workflows. The findings demonstrate significant time savings in code development (85% to 90% reuse rate) and highlight the conditional validity of this preprocessing method, which depends on the thematic predictability of the models. While synthetic data effectively captures collective perceptions, it struggles with specialized or contextualized practices, reflecting limitations documented in the silicon sampling literature, such as homogenization and reduced variance. This work extends the Phase 0 concept (Trojacka et al. 2025) from instrument validation to a full-fledged methodological preprocessing step, paving the way for scalable applications in survey research.

title: Accounting for Trust and Safety: Bounding Content-Moderation Quality from Records You Already Hold
summary: Platforms use expert audits to measure content-moderation quality. This paper develops a formal method for checking those claims using records platforms already maintain, such as appeal reversals and confirmed reports. These records provide one-sided bounds: they can show that a stated quality target was missed, but cannot prove that it was met. The paper presents the theory, limitations, constructed examples, and a prospective protocol for future evaluation. It reports no analysis of Meta operational data, no experiment, and no production result.

title: Toward On-Device Markerless 6DoF Tracking of a Physical Manipulative on a Mixed-Reality Headset: A Preliminary Study
summary: AR-Classroom uses physical models and virtual overlays to help learners explore spatial transformations. To align these overlays on a standalone headset, we developed a markerless six-degree-of-freedom(6DoF) tracker for a LEGO airplane on the Meta Quest 3. A compact YOLO model trained on synthetic Unity renders predicts 20 keypoints from dynamic RGB crops resized to 128 by 128 pixels. A perspective-n-point solver estimates the airplane's pose from these predictions and the corresponding 3D landmarks. In a paired evaluation on 1,000 synthetic validation images, cropping guided by ground-truth boxes increased the detection rate on annotated images from 32.5 to 46.2 percent. Mean keypoint F1 increased from 42.9 to 44.6 percent, with lower keypoint precision in the cropped view. In preliminary headset tests, 2 Hz was the highest tested tracking target at which the application maintained approximately 72 frames per second. A headset demonstration illustrates virtual overlay alignment with the physical airplane before and after a manual rotation. Quantitative 6DoF pose accuracy on real headset footage will be measured in future work.

title: Between Obligations and Evidence: A Participatory Study of Translating the EU AI Act into Technical Requirements
summary: The EU AI Act imposes technical and organizational requirements for high-risk AI systems, but applying these requirements involves contextual choices about what to measure and what evidence supports a compliance claim. We investigate these challenges through a participatory workshop involving 32 researchers, policymakers, and practitioners from different disciplines, using realistic scenarios in healthcare, recruitment, and public transport to examine how regulatory obligations are interpreted, translated into technical requirements, and evaluated in practice. Through a thematic analysis of workshop data, we identify recurring tensions between how regulatory obligations are translated into measurable system properties, how responsibility and human oversight are exercised in practice, and how the validity of compliance evidence is affected by changing operational conditions and system uses. For example, participants highlighted how fairness metrics could conceal discrimination in recruitment, how time pressure and limited information could undermine human oversight in public transport, and how changes in patient populations could invalidate previously established evidence of system performance. Our findings suggest that technical, organizational, and evidentiary challenges are interdependent, and that establishing and maintaining compliance requires attention not only to technical assessments but also to how AI systems are used, governed, and monitored over time. We discuss implications for supporting context-sensitive and ongoing compliance.

title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving
summary: Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data. However, removing GPS coordinates from driving logs does not erase the location information carried by vehicle signals. While prior route-inference attacks have demonstrated that speed, steering, and driving events can be matched to road networks to reconstruct trajectories, existing studies rely on inconsistent prior assumptions and evaluation metrics and are tested only on small, restricted datasets, making their results difficult to compare and their real-world effectiveness uncertain. We release CANTraj, a naturalistic driving dataset pairing decoded CAN events with time-aligned GNSS trajectories (3,940 drives, 454 drivers), and CANTraj-Bench for evaluating trajectory recovery (3,675 drives, 431 drivers, 1,380 hours, 85,919 km). On 776 evaluation drives from 94 unseen drivers, we compare six re-implemented attacks and benchmark baselines under explicit information-access protocols, paired comparisons, and metrics incorporating failures. Experiments show that combining steering signals with road-network constraints yields the largest gain: With a known start and heading, adding steering to speed raises the online map filter's five-minute route recovery from 56% to 87%, with a median average displacement error of 43 m versus 921 m for map-free dead reckoning. Offline beam search recovers 88% of test routes with the heading and 81% without it. Because methods fail on different windows, we also evaluate an LLM harness that selects among candidate routes on 659 five-minute windows; its best configuration recovers 79% of routes on test and 83% on few-shot, outperforming the best baseline on test and matching it on few-shot. Data and code at huggingface.co/datasets/HenryYHW/CANTraj and github.com/WangYuHang-cmd/GPS--CAN.

title: HerAgent: A Block-Level Checkpointing Harness for Coding-Agent Environment Setup
summary: Modern coding agents rely on establishing executable software environments before they can perform software engineering tasks such as testing, debugging, and patch validation. Existing setup agents typically control progress at either single-command or whole-script granularity, making recovery either too local to remove polluted state or too coarse to preserve useful progress. We present HerAgent (Harness EnviRonment Setup Agent), a block-level harness for coding-agent environment setup. HerAgent's main contribution is semantic setup blocks: a single progress-control abstraction used for execution, validation, checkpointing, repair, and rollback. Evaluated against six prior agents on four environment-setup datasets, HerAgent improves setup success in every comparison, achieving the largest gains on Installamatic-Bench (52.0% to 85.0%) and SetupBench (46.3% to 70.4%). It also reduces setup costs by up to 94.5%, showing that block-level progress control improves reliability and efficiency.

title: Deterministic ECDSA on secp256k1: the RFC 6979 assumption, a counterexample, and the state of deployed implementations
summary: RFC 6979 derives the ECDSA nonce as $k = F_x(h)$, with $F_x$ HMAC_DRBG keyed by the signing key x. We isolate the assumption its security rests on, A*: at known public key $Q = xG$, the signing transcript under nonces $F_x()$ is indistinguishable from the transcript under uniform nonces. A* suffices, and it is neither PRF security of HMAC nor auxiliary-input PRF security (AI-PRF) of $F_x$. A function $F'(x, h) = P_{Ext(xG)}(h)$ is a PRF under standard assumptions yet leaks x from one signature; the same holds for unmodified RFC 6979 over a compression function that keeps the PRF and dual-PRF properties used in proofs of HMAC, given a collision-resistance premise. A* and AI-PRF are separated in both directions. A* does not imply AI-PRF if the one-bit hidden number problem is hard. Conversely, in the standard model: any AI-PRF can be modified so that it stays one while two chosen-digest signing queries reveal x; under DDH with one public random point, or decisional square Diffie-Hellman without it, there is an AI-PRF whose key is recovered from signatures on two ordinary hashed messages; and a third function, under PRF security and DLP, violates A* while the scheme stays unforgeable. With an ideal compression function, A* follows tightly from DLP in the presence of a randomized-ECDSA signing oracle, and a nonce key independent of x removes the assumption. The secret HMAC message block is $2^{-127.65}$ from uniform on secp256k1, $2^{-32}$ on P-256 and 0.336 on brainpoolP256r1. An audit of 31 secp256k1 implementations finds that 28 sign deterministically without added entropy and that the raw-message deviation from bits2octets of libsecp256k1 before 0.2.0 survives in NBitcoin, dcrd and btcec v2. Low-R grinding needs no assumption beyond A*, and every nonzero Fourier coefficient of the low-R nonce set is below $2^{-116.9}$ unconditionally. We give test vectors for the untested $h >= n$ branch

title: PACT: A Decoder-Confidence-Guided Two-Round Receiver for Joint Channel and Phase-Noise Estimation in Sub-THz OFDM
summary: Frequency-selective fading and oscillator phase noise (PN) jointly impair coded sub-THz OFDM reception. We propose a decoder-confidence-guided two-round receiver combining a {pilot-aware complex transformer} (PACT) estimator, banded linear minimum mean-square error equalization, and neural normalized min-sum decoding. PACT jointly estimates the frequency-domain channel and effective time-domain PN through interacting complex-valued branches. Decoder-derived pseudo-pilots and continuous constellation-aware confidence guide second-round refinement through PACT inputs and attention, with parameters shared across rounds. At $E_b/N_0=30$~dB, the PACT receiver achieves approximately $70\%$ and $57\%$ lower code-block error rates than the best-performing learning-based baseline in the two benchmark settings, respectively. Frozen-weight tests further demonstrate applicability across channel/PN models, carrier frequencies, and FFT/bandwidth configurations.

title: Policy-Conditioned Koopman Representations for Parameterized Closed-Loop Systems
summary: Predicting the response of a nonlinear system across different feedback controllers requires a model that captures how the closed-loop dynamics change with the controller parameters. In a finite-dimensional Koopman model, these changes may affect both the latent dynamics and the observable coordinates used to represent them. In this paper, we propose a policy-conditioned Koopman representation framework to address this problem. This framework allows a single learned model to predict a family of closed-loop trajectories without retraining for each controller. We test the framework on four nonlinear prediction benchmarks, where the model stays below a 15% error threshold on every system, while each baseline exceeds it on at least one. As an example application, the resulting surrogate supports one-shot feedback-parameter selection: an optimization at the initial state selects a controller that then operates with fixed parameters and ongoing state feedback. On nonlinear control benchmarks including MuJoCo, the selected controllers stabilize every system with 3 to 97 times less online computation than nonlinear model predictive control. These results demonstrate how policy-dependent coordinates can support both prediction across closed-loop systems and controller selection without repeated online trajectory optimization.

title: Black-Box Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Ensemble-of-Ensembles
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 54 pages (10 pages main text), 3 figures, 38 tables. Code: https://github.com/wma17/Black-box_UQ_for_LLMs_Ensemble_of_Ensemble
summary: Reliable use of large language models (LLMs) requires uncertainty estimates that separate ambiguity intrinsic to a prompt from genuine knowledge gaps. Bayesian and deep-ensemble methods deliver this aleatoric/epistemic decomposition in principle, but are computationally prohibitive at LLM scale and require white-box access. Existing black-box methods, in contrast, summarize to a single scalar that cannot make the distinction. We introduce a two-level ensemble that bridges this gap. Stochastic decoding of a fixed prompt forms the inner ensemble; meaning-preserving semantic perturbations of the prompt form the outer ensemble. Variability is measured in a continuous embedding space, and the law of total covariance gives an exact within-/between-perturbation decomposition to estimate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty (AU/EU); it requires only black-box sampling access. On top of this estimator, we contribute three theoretical results that ground the framework: (i) a finite-sample bias identity for nested Monte Carlo with a closed-form bias-corrected epistemic estimator; (ii) a Bayesian bridge bounding the gap between perturbation-population AU/EU and Bayesian targets; and (iii) a separation result identifying a class of failure modes that any consistency-only black-box method provably misses while perturbation-based EU detects. Across five short QA benchmarks and four instruction-tuned LLMs spanning two families and two scales, our estimator is competitive with strong white-box baselines, and at a matched generation budget it matches leading black-box methods on error ranking while decomposing AU and EU; controlled paired interventions show that AU and EU respond selectively to distinct, actionable sources of failure: prompt ambiguity and model knowledge gaps; and a long-form pilot on the NQ long-answer split shows the framework extends to claim-level factuality without retraining.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 54 pages (10 pages main text), 3 figures, 38 tables. Code: https://github.com/wma17/Black-box_UQ_for_LLMs_Ensemble_of_Ensemble

title: When to Trust Simulated Patient Responses:Support-Gated World Models for Vasopressor Decision Support
summary: Clinical world models expose language-model agents to predicted patient responses, but simulations can be unreliable for poorly supported treatments or unfamiliar hospitals. We introduce Support-Gated World-Model decision support, a lightweight extension of a propose--simulate--refine agent. A recurrent dynamics ensemble predicts short-horizon physiological responses to documented norepinephrine dose categories, while a behavior model estimates observational action support. The interface withholds predictions with insufficient support or excessive ensemble disagreement and abstains when no candidate qualifies. Evaluation on eICU-CRD includes 70 hospitals and 30,700 decision transitions, with 14 hospitals held out for testing. At 62.0% factual-transition coverage, joint gating yields a MAP mean absolute error of 7.3 mmHg, compared with 9.2 mmHg for random selection at the same coverage. The gated agent achieves 60.0% agreement with recorded actions at 81.0% decision coverage, compared with 55.0% agreement and 99.5% coverage for an ungated ensemble agent. Component ablations show lower factual risk with joint gating than with either gate alone.These results characterize a reliability--coverage trade-off in selective clinical simulation; they do not identify individualized treatment effects or establish improved patient outcomes.

title: Callo: Serving Cache-Miss Requests with Speculative Decoding on Invalidated KV under Prefill-Decode Disaggregation
summary: Agent sessions may involve frequent context edits, which effectively invalidate cached KV state and force requests to wait for re-prefill before decoding. We present Callo, a disaggregated serving system that leverages invalidated KV for speculative drafts to reduce this latency, while verifying drafts against the exact KV after prefill before committing tokens. Callo makes effective use of decode resources by scheduling speculations during periods of underutilization and preempting speculations when drafts are likely to not be accepted. We evaluated Callo on a two-GPU testbed using SWE-agent sessions across three model families, observing all-request speedups of 1.05-1.19x over vLLM at moderate load. We demonstrate that these gains are also realized at scale through cluster-level simulations driven by real-world traces.

title: Sample-efficient prediction of high-entropy alloy strength through outcome-aware robust sequential learning
summary: Accurate prediction of high-entropy alloy (HEA) strength can guide composition and processing decisions; however, obtaining tensile-test data for HEAs can be costly and experimentally demanding. This study proposes Robust Outcome-aware Sequential Experimentation for High-Entropy Alloys (ROSE-HEA), a sample-efficient framework for predicting ultimate tensile strength (UTS) from alloy composition and processing conditions. Its acquisition policy anticipates how possible UTS outcomes update predictions and the support for complementary Gaussian process (GP) descriptions. It then reassesses the worst-case expected predictive risk remaining across a reference domain to select informative candidates. A retrospective evaluation on 501 HEA records compares ROSE-HEA with expected-improvement (EI) and upper-confidence-bound (UCB) Bayesian optimization (BO), random GP sampling, and eight conventional regressors across 30 matched runs with shared initial observations and test conditions. Starting from 25 initial observations and acquiring 100 additional responses, ROSE-HEA achieves the lowest mean root-mean-square error (RMSE), at 152.84 MPa, and the highest mean R^2, at 0.7443. Mean RMSE is reduced by 6.16% and 6.37% relative to EI and UCB, respectively. The selected observations improve prediction across six regressor families and provide broader design-space coverage. ROSE-HEA also surpasses the strongest conventional regressor's mean predictive performance using 125 rather than 185 observations, corresponding to 32.4% fewer training observations. These findings demonstrate the potential of outcome-aware robust sequential learning to improve UTS prediction in HEAs under constrained training budgets.

title: VellSSLH: Sound Type-Guided Selective Speculative Load Hardening for LLVM IR
summary:
Constant-time cryptographic programs written in C can still leak secrets during speculative execution. Mispredicted branches may allow instructions to access secret data and expose it through observable behavior. Speculative load hardening (SLH) addresses these leaks, but protecting values unnecessarily can introduce significant runtime overhead. We present VellSSLH, which selectively inserts speculative load hardening at LLVM IR. Programmers specify Public and Secret inputs in annotated C programs, and our analysis infers which values may become secret during speculation. The transformation then inserts misspeculation-flag operations and protections only where needed. VellSCT, our extracted checker, validates the resulting LLVM IR.
  We formalize speculative constant-time (SCT) security by extending Vellvm's LLVM semantics with speculative execution, attacker directives, and leakage observations. Our security type system reasons about SSA joins, symbolic values, poison, pointer provenance, and observable faults, and supports declared declassifications and trusted external services. In Rocq, we prove that programs accepted by the checker satisfy SCT, and that a reference hardening transformation preserves architectural behavior. Evaluated optimized variants are rechecked for SCT but are not covered by this preservation proof. Our mechanized guarantees apply at LLVM IR; security of the generated binary additionally depends on backend and hardware assumptions.
  We evaluate VellSSLH on 24 cryptographic entries on a bare-metal Intel processor. VellSSLH achieves 4.03% lower geometric-mean runtime than LLVM SLH, with 13 comparisons favoring VellSSLH, eight favoring LLVM SLH, and three inconclusive. For X25519, VellSSLH improves runtime by 22.69% over LLVM SLH with only 1.86% overhead over unprotected code. Compared with Ultimate SLH, VellSSLH achieves 19.65% lower runtime.

title: Typing Matters: Muscle, Language and Typing Behaviour in Live Keystroke Decoding from sEMG
summary: Surface electromyography (sEMG) from the wrists can recover typed text without a keyboard. It is usually posed as a signal-inference problem: characters are read out of the muscle signal and character error rate is reported offline. We argue that this framing removes most of the problem. The decoder is constrained simultaneously by the muscles, by the language being typed, and by typing behaviour such as typos, corrections, backspaces and line breaks, and a usable system must predict keys live while the hand keeps moving. Existing systems fall short on two counts: (1) they process sEMG in fixed windows and carry nothing from one window to the next, discarding context accumulated over a session, and (2) they lack any understanding of the linguistic structure that drives typing, so every keystroke is inferred from the muscle signal alone. We propose a fully causal, zero-lookahead sEMG typing decoder built on a state space model (SSM), in which a single model decodes a whole session without windowed partitions, conditioned on what has already been typed. We achieve this by fusing a traditional typing decoder with an efficient autoregressive language model, instilling both sEMG and linguistic understanding in one model. To train such a model for per-character typing rather than whole-word text, we introduce a retokenization method that rewrites ordinary prose as human-like typing, with keystrokes, typos, backspaces and line breaks included, converting WikiText into a large typing corpus where none existed. Our model, having never seen a single sEMG-to-character transcript in typing, achieves a state-of-the-art character error rate of 25.13% on emg2qwerty's cross-user benchmark, a 5.4% relative improvement over the previous best with 6.7 times fewer parameters, while running strictly causally with no future context.

title: Score-based neural ordinary differential equations for reaction-diffusions
summary: A diffusion equation can be rewritten as a transport equation driven by the score function of the evolving density. Conventional probability-flow formulations, which move particles deterministically with this score-driven velocity, typically conserve total mass. In this work, we develop a Lagrangian method for reaction-diffusion equations in which each particle carries a position and a physical weight. The characteristic ODEs incorporate source terms into the evolution of the log-density and its gradient, while particle weights track changes in mass. We combine this representation with a learned velocity field and weighted particle training to approximate these dynamics. For non-increasing reaction rates, a relative-entropy inequality supports the mass-normalized self-consistency residual as the training objective. This objective can control the error of the induced density when the growth rate is bounded. The algorithm divides the time interval into short windows. In each window, a frozen velocity generates the particle data for a regression of the network velocity. We draw the particles from period-adapted initial sampling distributions and weight them in the loss partly by their predicted future mass, because the reaction can make regions with little initial mass important later. We numerically investigate the method on the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck (OU) equation with a linear source term, Fisher--KPP equations, and Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao gradient flows.

title: Disenfranchisement in Spatial Voting Games
summary: The questions of voting rights, group membership, and the boundaries of acceptable discourse all involve a recursive, self-stability issue, wherein the voters, group members, and acceptable commentators are often the ultimate arbiters of their own rules for inclusion and exclusion. In order to understand how ideological or issue diversity may impact the stability of such inclusion and exclusion, we introduce franchise elections, where voting members of a group vote to change the electorate. In particular, when agents are positioned inside an ideological or issue space, a social choice function that aggregates agent viewpoints induces a preference for agents over group composition, where agents prefer groups that improve the social choice function outcome for them. We demonstrate that when ideological space is two-dimensional, these franchise elections can generate complex behavior and that this complexity exists for any social choice function. Using the Yolk social choice function from voting theory, we illustrate that franchise elections can predict that agents attempting to introduce a new ideological axis perpendicular to an existing left-right spectrum risk disenfranchisement unless they ally with either side of the spectrum, and that franchise elections can cycle with any period.

title: Stochastic Games with Distributional Entropy Objectives
summary:
We introduce \emph{stochastic games with distributional entropy objectives}, two-player zero-sum games whose configurations are probability distributions over the states of a finite arena and whose stage reward is Shannon entropy. Over an infinite discounted horizon, MIN seeks to concentrate the distribution, while MAX seeks to disperse it. Because entropy is nonlinear, it matters whether strategic and transition randomness are averaged before entropy is evaluated or sampled first. We formalise three resulting semantics: averaged-distribution, sampled-profile, and sampled-transition.
  This semantic choice fundamentally changes the game-theoretic structure. Averaged-distribution games need not be determined, even on a four-state deterministic arena, whereas both sampled semantics are determined and admit optimal stationary randomised strategies. We give contractive Bellman characterisations and convergent finite-horizon approximations for the upper and lower averaged values and the two sampled values. Moreover, even the lower value under averaged-distribution semantics dominates the value under either sampled semantics, while the sampled-profile and sampled-transition values are incomparable in general.
  For fixed rational discount and positive rational promise gap, the averaged-distribution (upper and lower value) gap problems and both sampled gap problems lie in PSPACE; for a single entropy minimiser, the averaged and sampled-profile problems lie in NP. Finally, under all three semantics, entropy optimisation is NP-hard to approximate within a suitable fixed additive constant, already for deterministic one-player games, where pure memoryless strategies are optimal.

title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Who Verifies the Agents? Toward Reliable Agent Development
summary: LLM-based verifiers are increasingly used to evaluate agent executions, but their reliability is typically measured under a single representation of the trajectory. In deployed agent systems, the same execution may be exposed through composed tools, delegation boundaries, or compacted histories, changing what execution evidence is directly observable to the verifier. It therefore remains unclear whether correct verifier judgments persist across such abstraction boundaries. We introduce Verification Transport, a reliability test that measures judgment stability under abstraction-induced changes in execution observability. We construct matched native, abstracted, and restored views of the same frozen executions while holding the task, realized trajectory, outcome, ground truth, evaluation criterion, and verifier fixed. Across four agent-evaluation benchmarks, seven verifier backbones, four verification protocols, and three abstraction boundaries, we find substantial transport failure, reaching about 31% under macro abstraction and delegation. Verification protocols exhibit distinct failure modes: direct verification more often produces incorrect verdicts, whereas evidence-grounded and deliberative protocols tend to abstain under limited observability. This suggests that lower transport failure rates do not necessarily imply greater reliability. Restoring the corresponding execution provenance recovers 85.5% of transport failures, while recovery is lower when provenance is lossy or unavailable. These results show that native-view accuracy alone is insufficient to characterize verifier reliability when execution evidence crosses abstraction boundaries.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Who Verifies the Agents? Toward Reliable Agent Development

title: Beyond Blossom: Accelerating MWPM Decoding for Surface Codes With Local Predecoding and Architecture-Aware Optimizations
summary: Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is widely used to decode surface codes, but its computational cost increases with code distance. We present Beyond Blossom, a state-of-the-art CPU-based MWPM decoder for surface codes. It combines algorithmic optimization through local predecoding, architecture-aware optimization, and pipeline-wide parallelism to reduce matching workload and execution overhead while preserving MWPM optimality. Across rotated surface codes with distances 9-33 and circuit-level physical error rates of 0.05%-0.3%, on a single CPU core, Beyond Blossom achieves a 4.23$\times$ geometric-mean speedup and up to 5.58$\times$ speedup over Sparse Blossom in PyMatching. At distance 33 and a physical error rate of 0.1%, with 8 CPU cores, decoding a block of 33 measurement rounds takes 21.40 $μ$s on average, equivalent to 0.65 $μ$s per round.

title: Evaluating Feedback-Driven Black-Box Processes via Stochastic Modeling and Simulation
summary: We study feedback-driven black-box processes across software engineering and machine learning. These processes are inherently sequential: policies generate inputs, observe outputs/feedback from systems, and use the feedback to guide the design of subsequent inputs. While many policies are developed under structural assumptions on the underlying systems, many real-world systems operate without such knowledge, necessitating black-box policies that lack a unified evaluation framework. We introduce a stochastic framework that models and evaluates such policies using Markov chains and simulation, thereby connecting empirical practice with theory. We instantiate the framework in mutation-based fuzzing (widely used for discovering software bugs via sequential input mutation), by a novel Markov chain model of fuzzing whose transitions are governed by the mutation strategy and whose feedback is given by program execution. We develop a rigorous evaluation paradigm with new performance measures, sound estimators, and evaluation procedures with provable guarantees. Guided by the theory, we evaluate 9 fuzzers on 18 widely used fuzzing benchmarks and conduct case studies in 4 non-fuzzing domains. These results show that the framework provides a principled basis for evaluation while connecting to practice, with implications beyond fuzzing.

title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
summary: Speculative decoding accelerates generation by letting a lightweight drafter propose tokens for parallel verification by a target model. Diffusion drafters such as DFlash propose an entire token block in a single forward pass, but mainly focus on text-only tasks, leaving multimodal drafting underexplored. To study this setting, we first introduce a metric of token-level visual dependence based on the KL divergence between next-token distributions with and without visual input. We find that acceptance rates decrease from 46% in the lowest visual-dependence quartile to 22% in the highest, with this disparity persisting after multimodal training. Motivated by this observation, we propose MMFlash, a simple and effective framework that adaptively upweights visually dependent tokens that the drafter predicts poorly. For long video inputs, MMFlash further employs sparse attention to reduce redundant attention computation and improve drafting quality. Across various multimodal benchmarks, MMFlash achieves lossless decoding speedups of up to $3.58\times$, outperforming EAGLE-3 and DFlash by up to 195.4% and 17.1%, respectively.

title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
comments: 34 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems, Volume 10 (2027)
summary: AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is evolving beyond passive data collection toward agentic AI systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate action across domestic and clinical settings. This structured scoping review finds that mature agentic care has not yet emerged: Most systems remain human led, while stronger decision-action coupling and embodied AI remain largely confined to prototypes and pilots. Healthcare robotics makes the transition from monitoring to action especially visible by translating AI-generated recommendations and decisions into speech, movement, prompting, physical assistance, escalation, and care coordination, making embodiment, clinical integration, human oversight, and governance fundamental design requirements. Further progress requires safe and interoperable care architectures in which intelligent components operate through clinically validated and accountable workflows. We propose agentic robotics as a future direction for supervised systems embedded in the care ecosystem, connecting AI agents and robots with clinicians, caregivers, and patients through auditable workflows that can be interrupted and remain subject to human oversight and explicit AI governance.
comment: 34 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems, Volume 10 (2027)

title: Interactive Program Induction with Language Model Priors
summary: Program induction refers to the process in which a learner aims to recover a program from a few given input-output examples. This paradigm broadens programming access by letting users demonstrate the rule-based behavior they want to apply to unseen data, instead of having to implement it themselves. However, recovering a program from finite input-output examples is fundamentally ambiguous, as a finite set of input-output examples is theoretically consistent with infinitely many programs whose output diverges on unseen inputs. We view this problem from a Bayesian perspective, where, given a prior $p^0$ over programs, identifying the target program means concentrating posterior probability mass on it by observing additional input-output examples. In the interactive program induction setting, the learner chooses maximally informative inputs and queries an oracle, such as the user, for their outputs. We derive a greedy query-selection algorithm and show that it terminates after $\mathcal{O}(\frac{1}γ\log 1/p^0(f^\star))$ informative oracle queries, and returns the target program $f^\star$ up to approximate equivalence when no other class outweighs it under the prior. The algorithm uses a language model as the prior under a PAC-style relaxation of program equivalence, where the query-selection objective is estimated using importance sampling. On the CodeARC benchmark, the algorithm improves accuracy over the LM only agent by up to 22 percentage points while observing up to 10.5 fewer input-output examples.

title: When Will You Hand It Over? A Hidden Start Delay Makes Self-Play Handover Robust to Unfamiliar Partners
comments: CoRL 2026, Human-Centered Robot Learning and Interaction (HumanRLI) Workshop. Code: https://github.com/mkhoshnam/Selfplay-PPO-handover
summary: Cooperative self-play can teach a humanoid to receive an object without any human data, but the partner it meets after training is never the one it trained with; we show that a fluent self-play handover policy breaks with unfamiliar partners, identify the main cause, and repair it. In a physics-based parcel handover between a Unitree G1 and a learned giver, both trained by alternating PPO self-play, the receiver completes 95% and 90% of handovers with its own partner (two training seeds) but only 31% with scripted partners it has never met. Paired interventions isolate the cause: under a shared reward the learned giver always starts its offer at once, so the receiver learns a single rendezvous, and delaying its own partner by one second cuts success from 95% to 6% (87% to 34% in the second seed). We introduce hidden start-delay randomisation (HSD), a one-line rule on the learned partner that the receiver never observes. After 300 further updates, success with unseen scripted partners rises from 31% to 80% in both seeds, against 35--41% for a budget-matched control. The gain holds on a fresh scenario seed, on eleven held-out partner conditions and on partners that start later than any training delay; it cuts high-force contact three- to five-fold and needs no retraining of the partner.
comment: CoRL 2026, Human-Centered Robot Learning and Interaction (HumanRLI) Workshop. Code: https://github.com/mkhoshnam/Selfplay-PPO-handover

title: TradeGauntlet: Evaluating Compliance Controls for Autonomous Trading Agents
comments: 21 pages, 5 figures. Code and saved results: https://github.com/tokencraftdata/agentic-compliance
summary: Autonomous trading agents need controls that prevent problematic orders without making legitimate tasks impractical. We study this aspect of agentic compliance with TradeGauntlet, a replayable limit-order-book simulator that separates detection, prevention, and execution cost. In 1,680 simulated sessions with Claude Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, all conduct alerts were self-matches. Gates eliminated those alerts by rejecting self-crossing orders, while the aggregate-gate condition reduced Sonnet's two-sided fills by about 15%. A conduct reminder reduced Sonnet's alert rate but reduced Haiku's fills without a detectable alert benefit. These results show why zero alerts alone do not establish an agent's compliance. Scripted probes and two search methods test weaknesses beyond those observed in the LLM runs. The searches find split-order schedules that evade the implemented conduct rules; a learned baseline catches all 2,400 tested searched episodes but also flags 15% of a large maker's sessions. Aggregate caps reduce the response-dependent gain unevenly, with smaller reductions when only near-touch depth affects prices. A response fitted to five Nasdaq stocks and a separate ABIDES experiment expose the dependence of these estimates on market assumptions. A distinct adversarial prompt elicited refusals from Sonnet in all 240 rounds, yielding no candidate strategies to evaluate. TradeGauntlet provides reproducible tests of controls around trading agents; the experiments do not establish legal compliance or real-market detection accuracy.
comment: 21 pages, 5 figures. Code and saved results: https://github.com/tokencraftdata/agentic-compliance

title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
summary: Small language models are attractive for local, low-cost, and privacy-sensitive deployment, but they remain unreliable on mathematical reasoning tasks that require decomposition, exact computation, tool use, and verification. We introduce \textbf{ARCHER}: \textbf{A}ction-trace \textbf{R}einforcement for \textbf{C}alculator-grounded \textbf{H}ierarchical \textbf{E}xecutable \textbf{R}easoning, a two-stage framework for training small language models (SLMs) to produce executable and auditable reasoning trajectories. In the first stage, ARCHER compiles free-form chain-of-thought rationales into typed action traces containing reasoning steps, calculator calls, deterministic runtime observations, verification actions, and final answers. This shifts the supervision target from imitating explanatory text to learning a tool-grounded reasoning policy. In the second stage, ARCHER refines this policy through asymmetric hierarchical reinforcement learning, using grouped and conditionally gated trajectory rewards for answer correctness, tool grounding, process discipline, and trace alignment. Across five standard sub-10B backbones, ARCHER improves over the strongest tool-augmented baseline by 5.51 percentage points on macro-average across benchmark accuracies, including gains of 8.95 points on MATH-500 and 5.33 and 5.34 points on AIME-2024 and AIME-2025. Evaluations on two additional reasoning-specialized 7B backbones further show that executable grounding remains beneficial after reasoning-focused reinforcement learning or distillation. These results demonstrate that executable supervision and reward-guided behavioral refinement provide a general and effective training paradigm for compact mathematical reasoners.

title: Toward Resilient Self-Driving Laboratories through Telerobotic Interventions
summary: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific research by integrating robotics, automated experimentation, and machine learning to execute experiments autonomously. Biology and chemistry have adopted these systems. However, increasing SDL complexity heightens susceptibility to unexpected faults in automated workflows, highlighting the need for efficient recovery mechanisms. In this study, we investigate telerobotic interventions to enhance SDL resilience against unexpected failures. We developed a teleoperation interface enabling human operators to resolve disruptions during automated tasks. The interface enables precise control of a six-degree-of-freedom (DOF) robotic arm (UR3e) using a 3D mouse (3Dconnexion SpaceMouse Pro). Two velocity-based controller strategies were evaluated: (i) a coupled mode mapping all six DOFs to the 3D mouse's central knob and (ii) a decoupled mode separating translational and rotational motions. To evaluate the framework, teleoperators intervened across three SDL fault scenarios. In the first study, comparative trials showed that the decoupled controller was associated with shorter completion times and reduced rotational motion. In a second study, teleoperators performed an aiming task with and without reference-path guidance. Users were more target-driven and risk-tolerant without guidance but showed behavioral differences under different guidance strategies. These findings suggest that controller configuration and reference-path design influence operator performance during SDL fault recovery, informing teleoperation interface optimization. This work demonstrates the potential feasibility of teleoperation as a human-in-the-loop recovery mechanism for SDL workflows, combining robotic precision with human adaptability and problem-solving. These findings also provide a foundation for future studies in shared autonomy and semi-autonomous intervention.

title: A Common Improved Bound for Asymmetric TSP and Path TSP
summary: We give polynomial-time $(R_*+\varepsilon)$-approximation algorithms for asymmetric TSP and asymmetric path TSP, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, where $R_*=6+\sqrt2+\sqrt{15+6\sqrt2}\approx12.2604$. Both guarantees hold relative to the corresponding subtour relaxations, whose integrality ratios are therefore at most $R_*$. This improves the previous guarantees of below $14.7$ for asymmetric TSP and $15$ for asymmetric path TSP [Vygen, 2026]. Our algorithms strengthen subtour covers and recursive augmentation in the laminar framework [Svensson, Tarnawski, Vegh, JACM'20; Traub, Vygen, 2025]. The recursive analysis retains the paths through contracted regions and accounts jointly for their cost and the dual mass they visit. We also improve the reduction from asymmetric path TSP to vertebrate pairs [Traub, Vygen, 2025] by comparing two initial walks with complementary completion bounds. Applied to Vygen's existing vertebrate-pair algorithm, this reduction alone improves the path factor from $15$ to below $14.7$, matching his asymmetric TSP guarantee.

title: In Situ Monitoring and Predictive Modeling of Harmful Algal Blooms with Autonomous Surface Vehicles
summary: Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) pose significant environmental, economic, and public-health challenges in coastal and inland water bodies, creating a need for scalable methods to collect spatially distributed water-quality data. This paper presents an autonomous surface vessel-based sensing system for in-situ water-quality monitoring related to harmful algal bloom detection. The system integrates a BlueBoat Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV), a motorized winch for depth-controlled sonde deployment, a multiparameter water-quality sonde, side-scan sonar, and an event-camera payload. Autonomous waypoint missions were used to collect measurements across selected sampling regions and multiple depths, enabling both horizontal and vertical characterization of environmental conditions. Field deployments were conducted in Lake Pontchartrain, Louisiana, with additional measurements collected in False River, Louisiana to increase dataset diversity. The collected measurements included algal pigment indicators, nutrient concentration, turbidity, temperature, and other water-quality parameters relevant to bloom formation. In addition, complementary sonar and event-camera data were collected during vehicle operation to provide contextual environmental information. A machine-learning classification approach was also evaluated using the collected water-quality measurements to support HAB and non-HAB classification. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using a modular ASV platform for repeatable, multi-modal water-quality data collection and support future development of autonomous monitoring systems.

title: EPIGRIDS: Documentation and Validation of Seven Open Synthetic Transmission Grid Cases
comments: 10 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Submitted to the IEEE Open Access Journal of Power and Energy. Cases: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23814538; load series: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24151084; construction method: arXiv:2611.16222
summary: This paper documents and checks EPIGRIDS, seven open synthetic transmission grid cases from four independently built networks, made with an optimization-based construction method instead of the graph-statistics method behind most large public synthetic grids. The cases range from 250 to 78,484 buses, with geolocated substations, voltages up to 765 kV, and line parameters taken from conductor data. Each ships under an open license in three common power flow formats that agree at the solved operating point, and the six larger cases have a companion hourly, bus-level load series for one year. The Texas, Florida, and Michigan, Ohio, and Indiana cases are sub-networks of the Eastern case. Every case solves an alternating-current power flow from its stored operating point. With parallel circuits merged, the Eastern and Western cases are 9 and 16% denser than the real interconnections, while graph-statistics cases on the same footprints lie within 6% and meet more published realism criteria. A full single-outage contingency analysis completes on every case, and in an optimal power flow benchmark every case except the New England base case and one of its 12 operating points solves in polar form.
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Submitted to the IEEE Open Access Journal of Power and Energy. Cases: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23814538; load series: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24151084; construction method: arXiv:2611.16222

title: Disturbance-Aware Informative Planning in Spatiotemporal Environments
comments: Submitted to Learning for Dynamics and Control Conference 2027. Project website: https://kalebbennaveed.github.io/dist-aware-ipp/
summary: Autonomous robots are widely used for persistent monitoring of spatiotemporal environments, where quantities of interest (QoI) change across space and time and require repeated measurements. In practice, robot motion can be affected by external disturbances that vary across the environment. When such external disturbances are not considered in trajectory optimization, it can lead to inaccurate predictions of robot motion and, consequently, the information acquired about the QoI during execution. However, estimating disturbances throughout the environment can be inefficient, as disturbances in regions with little overlap with monitoring trajectories have limited impact on monitoring performance. We therefore propose a two-stage informative planning framework for unknown, spatially varying but time-invariant disturbances, combining informed disturbance sampling with disturbance-aware trajectory optimization. First, we identify where QoI measurements are needed and generate alternative paths to these locations using the environment geometry. We then prioritize disturbance measurements based on their expected reduction of disturbance uncertainty along these paths. Second, rather than optimizing information acquisition based on nominal robot motion, we incorporate the learned disturbance belief into trajectory optimization to account for its effects on robot motion and information acquisition. Across four simulation scenarios, the proposed method reduces disturbance-learning time by 25.0--52.3 percent compared with environment-wide estimation and identifies paths that appear costly under nominal dynamics but become preferable when disturbances are considered.
comment: Submitted to Learning for Dynamics and Control Conference 2027. Project website: https://kalebbennaveed.github.io/dist-aware-ipp/

title: Agentic induction of common data elements and information extraction from sarcoma case report abstracts
summary: Common data elements (CDEs) support clinical data comparability but are usually defined manually. We investigated whether large language model agents could derive a CDE schema from sarcoma case report abstracts and apply it at scale. An agent proposed 72,909 candidate CDEs from 24,588 PubMed abstracts; agentic consolidation yielded 1,570 CDEs. We retained 53 supported by at least 50 abstracts and attempted evidence-linked extraction across the corpus. Processing succeeded for all retained CDEs in 79.2% of abstracts, including responses indicating non-mention. Two human reviewers approved 83.0% of retained CDEs for relevance, 67.9% for clarity, and 56.6% for correctness. In 100 sampled abstracts, exact agreement with the value extracted by the LLM was 94.9% among 1,116 pairs with a non-empty answer (abstract-level bootstrap 95% CI, 93.0-96.4%). Errors concentrated in anatomical and temporal fields. These findings support agent-assisted schema drafting followed by expert curation before large-scale extraction.

title: Asymptotic Margins and Feature Confinement in Conic Classification Heads under Softmax Cross-Entropy
comments: 22 pages, 2 figures. Companion paper: to be uploaded. Code: https://github.com/ongerek/Conic
summary: Classification heads built on conic functions give each class a bounded region of the feature space, and such regions are used to reject samples of unseen classes. We ask whether these regions also keep the features bounded when the head is trained with softmax cross-entropy. For a head whose class scores combine a linear term with a Euclidean norm, we first show that the region of each class is bounded by a quadric of revolution, whose eccentricity is the reciprocal of one learned ratio. We then attach to each class an asymptotic margin, which compares the growth of its score with the growth of all the other scores and can be computed by a second-order cone program. The loss of a class has infimum zero exactly when its margin is positive, and it then approaches zero only along diverging features. When the margin is negative, the loss is coercive and its minimizers lie in an explicit ball. Since softmax depends only on the differences between scores, a class with a bounded region can still have a positive margin, so bounded regions do not confine the features. The result extends to other norms, including the polyhedral conic functions. On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, all 1210 cells of 67 trained conic heads have positive margins, whereas a prototype head keeps nine of its ten cells bounded, as the theory predicts.
comment: 22 pages, 2 figures. Companion paper: to be uploaded. Code: https://github.com/ongerek/Conic

title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
summary: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions. This includes the forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), as well as Monte Carlo KL estimates and entropy. When the distributions are nearly equal, rounding and cancellation issues affect the forward and gradient computations. These issues can affect settings using divergences in optimization objectives, such as knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods. We propose numerically stable reformulations and provide example implementations for each setting, validated by property-based tests.

AI.title_translation: 近似相等分布之间散度计算的数值问题研究
AI.tldr: 论文指出了近乎相等分布间散度计算（KL、JSD等）的前向和梯度数值不稳定性，并提出了经过验证的数值稳定重构方法。
AI.motivation: 继近期研究发现softmax与软交叉熵存在数值缺陷后，作者探究发现分类分布之间在几乎相等时计算散度（如KL、JSD）同样存在前向与梯度的舍入和数值抵消问题，这会直接危害知识蒸馏、强化学习及近端优化等下游任务的稳定性。
AI.method: 针对前向/反向KL散度、广义JSD、蒙特卡洛KL估计及熵计算，设计了数值稳定的重构计算公式，并提供了通过基于性质的测试（property-based tests）验证的具体实现。
AI.result: 证实了标准散度运算在微小分布差异下的数值不稳定表现，并开发且验证了一整套适用于各类散度计算场景的数值稳定重构实现。
AI.conclusion: 在分布近似相等时，标准散度及其梯度的前向计算存在舍入和抵消误差；所提出的数值稳定重构方案能够有效消除这些计算异常，保障优化算法的稳定收敛。
AI.translation: Barron 等人（2026）最近指出了 softmax 和软交叉熵损失中存在的数值问题。我们证明了分类分布之间的标准散度运算中也存在类似的问题。这包括前向与反向 Kullback-Leibler (KL) 散度、广义 Jensen-Shannon 散度 (JSD)，以及蒙特卡洛 KL 估计和熵。当分布近似相等时，舍入和抵消误差会严重影响前向计算与梯度计算。这些问题会影响在优化目标中使用散度的应用场景，例如知识蒸馏、强化学习和近端优化方法。我们提出了数值稳定的重构形式，并为每种设置提供了示例实现，且均通过了基于性质的测试验证。
AI.summary: 本文系统研究了近乎相等的分类分布之间散度计算的数值问题。作者指出标准KL散度和JSD等操作在前向与梯度计算时会遭遇浮点舍入与抵消误差，从而危害知识蒸馏和强化学习等依赖散度优化的场景。为此，本文提出了数值稳定的重构形式，并提供了经过严密测试验证的参考实现。
AI.keywords: 数值稳定性, KL散度, Jensen-Shannon散度, 梯度计算, 强化学习
AI.comments: 该论文关注了一个在现代机器学习（特别是知识蒸馏、RLHF近端策略优化等任务）中极其基础却常被忽略的底层数值精度问题。当教师与学生模型或新旧策略分布极度接近时，微小的浮点舍入与抵消误差极易引发梯度异常。作者提出的数值稳定重构公式和基于性质的验证具有很强的工程实践价值与理论指导意义。

title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
comments: 15 pages, 4 figures. Preprint (submitted version) of a paper published in ICCCI 2026, CCIS vol. 3044, Springer
summary: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware. Unlike conventional Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems that process documents/books online in an all-texts-at-once type of way, thereby risking narrative spoilers, MeReader confines both retrieval and generation to the reader's distinct position in the text. The system integrates a hybrid retrieval architecture, combining vector similarity, BM25, and summary embeddings, to ensure high fidelity to the reader's current context. We evaluate the system across classical English books using both quantitative comprehension metrics and qualitative LLM-based independent judging. The results identify a quality-latency frontier, showing that mid-sized local models (2b-4b) can achieve comprehension parity with larger counterparts (5b+) while maintaining acceptable response quality. Importantly, the proposed progress-aware boundary mechanism is shown to prevent future content leakage without compromising retrieval quality and correctness. These findings suggest that a localized, privacy-centric approach can augment, rather than replace, the digital reading experience, offering a good alternative to cloud-dependent services. Therein, there remains a lack of amalgamate systems which combine progress-aware, privacy-preserving, and narrative eBook reading with AI support. It is in this very gap that the development of MeReader came to be; synthesizing said strands into an offline, book-constrained assistant focused on enhancing comprehension without compromising narrative continuity or user privacy.
comment: 15 pages, 4 figures. Preprint (submitted version) of a paper published in ICCCI 2026, CCIS vol. 3044, Springer

AI.title_translation: MeReader：一种用于叙事电子书阅读的离线、保护隐私且具备进度感知的AI助手
AI.tldr: MeReader是一款在本地离线运行的电子书AI阅读伴侣，通过将检索和生成限制在当前阅读进度内，杜绝剧透并保护隐私。
AI.motivation: 现有的基于大语言模型的系统通常在线且一次性处理整本书籍，存在泄露后续情节（剧透）及侵犯隐私的风险，目前缺乏将进度感知、隐私保护与叙事电子书阅读融为一体的AI辅助系统。

AI.result: 评估表明存在质量与延迟的前沿平衡，2B-4B的中型本地模型能够达到与5B+较大模型相当的理解水平，且提出的进度感知边界机制能有效防止未来内容泄露，同时不损害检索质量与准确性。
AI.conclusion: 本地化且注重隐私的AI方案能够有效增强而非取代数字阅读体验，在不破坏叙事连续性或侵犯用户隐私的前提下，为依赖云端服务的阅读辅助工具提供了可靠的替代方案。
AI.translation: 本文介绍了MeReader，这是一款注重隐私保护、离线且具备进度感知能力的AI助手，旨在消费级硬件上作为叙事阅读的上下文伴侣。与传统基于大语言模型（LLM）的系统不同（后者在线且以一次性处理全部文本的方式运作，从而带来叙事剧透的风险），MeReader将检索和生成严格限制在读者当前所处的特定文本位置。该系统集成了混合检索架构，结合了向量相似度、BM25和摘要嵌入，以确保对读者当前上下文的高保真度。我们在经典英文书籍上，利用定量理解指标和基于LLM的独立定性评判对系统进行了评估。结果揭示了质量与延迟的前沿平衡，表明中型本地模型（2B-4B）能够达到与更大模型（5B+）相当的理解能力，同时保持可接受的响应质量。重要的是，所提出的进度感知边界机制被证明可以在不影响检索质量和正确性的前提下，防止未来内容的泄露。这些发现表明，本地化、以隐私为中心的方法可以增强而不是取代数字阅读体验，为依赖云端的服务提供了良好的替代方案。目前，仍缺乏将进度感知、隐私保护以及结合AI辅助的叙事电子书阅读融为一体的系统。MeReader的开发正是为了填补这一空白，将上述要素综合为一个离线、受书籍边界约束的助手，专注于在不影响叙事连续性或用户隐私的情况下提升阅读理解能力。
AI.summary: 本文提出了MeReader，这是一款面向消费级硬件的离线、注重隐私且具备阅读进度感知能力的叙事电子书AI助手。它通过进度边界机制和混合检索架构，将知识检索与问答生成严格限定在读者当前阅读进度内以防剧透，实验证明中型端侧模型即可实现良好的理解能力和响应质量。
AI.keywords: 叙事阅读, 隐私保护, 进度感知, 离线AI助手, 混合检索
AI.comments: 该研究针对叙事性电子书阅读中的核心痛点——剧透（spoiler）和用户隐私泄露问题，提出了兼顾进度感知与离线运行的AI伴读系统。其创新之处在于通过进度边界机制将检索与生成严格限制在读者已读范围内，并结合端侧轻量级LLM实现了低延迟与高准确度的平衡，对推动本地化智能阅读助手的落地具有实用价值。

title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
summary: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures. We focus on one such failure: web agents hallucinating actions that are not available on a website. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations before generation begins (0.80 AUC) and steering along a probe direction corrects 85\% of hallucinations, but disrupts 7\% of valid actions. However, these results only provide a partial explanation of why the agent hallucinates. The probe direction is sensitive to prompt formatting, losing much of its steering effect after a minor change to how actions are represented. Additionally, circuit identification can be difficult as the computation is distributed across multiple components and positions, and the information the agent relies on varies across examples. We discuss how these observations challenge the assumptions underlying standard MI methods for circuit discovery and feature identification, and outline future directions for making these methods better suited to explain failures in LLM-based agents.

AI.title_translation: 机制可解释性能否帮助解释大语言模型智能体的失败？以网页元素幻觉为例的研究
AI.tldr: 本文探究了机制可解释性在解释大语言模型智能体网页元素幻觉失败中的作用，发现探针虽能预测并引导纠正大部分幻觉，但标准MI方法在特征稳定性和回路识别上面临严峻挑战。
AI.motivation: 机制可解释性（MI）在解释LLM内部计算方面进展显著，但在解释基于LLM的智能体决策过程及现实失败场景（如网页智能体幻觉出网页上不存在的操作）中的表现尚未得到充分验证，亟需探讨MI在此类复杂任务中的适用性与局限。
AI.method: 以Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct与真实网站交互为实验场景，采用在提示词最后一个token上训练线性探针以预测幻觉、沿探针方向进行激活引导（steering）修正行为，并尝试进行回路识别（circuit identification）等机制分析方法。
AI.result: 在提示词最后一个token训练的线性探针可在生成前预测幻觉（AUC达到0.80）；沿探针方向引导可修正85%的幻觉，但会破坏7%的有效动作；该探针方向对提示词格式高度敏感，细微改动即会导致引导效果大幅下降；由于计算分散在多个组件与位置，且不同样本依赖的信息差异大，回路识别难度极高。
AI.conclusion: 机制可解释性工具目前只能对智能体的幻觉失败提供部分解释。智能体计算的分布式特性以及对上下文格式的高敏感性，挑战了标准MI在回路发现和特征识别上的核心假设，未来亟需发展更适用于智能体失败归因的可解释性方法。
AI.translation: 机制可解释性（MI）在解释大语言模型（LLM）内部计算方面取得了重大进展；然而，这些技术在解释基于LLM的智能体决策过程方面尚未展现出同等的成功。本文研究了MI工具在应用于现实智能体失败场景时所面临的挑战。我们聚焦于其中一种典型失败：网页智能体产生幻觉，生成了网页上并不存在的操作。我们对与真实网站交互的Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct应用了一系列机制分析。我们发现，在提示词最后一个token上训练的线性探针可以在生成开始前预测幻觉（AUC达0.80），并且沿探针方向进行引导可以纠正85%的幻觉，但会破坏7%的有效操作。然而，这些结果仅能对智能体为何产生幻觉提供部分解释。探针方向对提示词格式非常敏感，在对动作表示方式进行微调后便会丧失大部分引导效果。此外，由于计算分散在多个组件和位置，且智能体依赖的信息在不同样本之间存在差异，因此回路识别非常困难。我们讨论了这些观察结果如何挑战标准MI在回路发现和特征识别上的基本假设，并指出了使这些方法更好地解释基于LLM的智能体失败的未来方向。
AI.summary: 本文评估了机制可解释性（MI）在解释大语言模型智能体失败（特别是网页动作幻觉）中的有效性。通过对Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct的分析发现，虽然探针和引导技术可在一定程度上预测和纠正幻觉，但敏感的提示词依赖性和分散的内部计算阻碍了完整的因果回路解释，表明标准MI方法难以直接迁移到复杂的智能体场景。
AI.keywords: 机制可解释性, LLM智能体, 网页元素幻觉, 线性探针, 回路识别
AI.comments: 该论文的创新与重要性在于首次将机制可解释性（MI）系统性地应用于真实的LLM智能体复杂任务（Web Agent的动作幻觉问题），不仅验证了表征探测和激活引导在智能体行为控制中的潜力，更深刻揭示了现有MI方法在面对高度上下文敏感、计算高度分散的真实智能体系统时的脆弱性与局限性，为未来智能体级别的可解释性研究指明了方向。

title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval
summary: Screen history can serve as searchable visual memory for people and agents, but unlike an offline corpus, it must be encoded and indexed as each screenshot arrives. OCR-based indexing is fast but loses visual information; visual encoding takes over two seconds. Yet screens change incrementally: most pixels repeat within and across screenshots. This raises a question: do visual encoders need to recompute their representations from scratch for every new screenshot? We present StreamEmbed, a system for incremental visual embedding that exploits this redundancy. Guided solely by pixel differences, it combines spatial token pruning, which skips blocks that repeat a neighbor, with temporal KV reuse, which reuses cached keys and values for blocks unchanged across screenshots. A small learned adapter compensates for pruning and reuse to preserve fidelity to full-screenshot embeddings. On ScreenMemEval, our benchmark of 10,426 questions over 184 hours of screen histories from two humans and a computer-use agent, StreamEmbed sets a new accuracy-latency Pareto frontier on an M2 Pro GPU: it encodes up to 3.7x faster than full-screenshot encoding without sacrificing accuracy and improves accuracy over OCR-based indexing by up to 6.3 Recall@10 points at matched latency. A memory-efficient vector index stores a simulated year of screenshots in 0.13 GB of RAM. Together, these results make real-time indexing of screen history in its native visual form practical, laying a foundation for fully local visual assistants.

AI.title_translation: StreamEmbed：面向屏幕截图检索的像素级实时索引
AI.tldr: StreamEmbed利用屏幕变化的时空像素冗余，通过空间剪枝与时间KV复用实现低延迟、高精度的原生截图实时视觉索引。
AI.motivation: 屏幕历史可作为重要的视觉记忆，但必须实时编码索引。现存方法中OCR索引速度快却丢失布局与视觉特征，而从头进行完整视觉编码延迟过高（>2秒）。由于屏幕内容在空间和时间上通常呈现渐进式微小变化、存在大量冗余像素，无需对每张新截图从零重新计算嵌入。
AI.method: 提出StreamEmbed增量视觉嵌入系统：仅基于像素差异，结合空间Token剪枝（跳过与邻近块重复的图像块）和时间KV复用（跨截图复用未变动块的KV缓存），并通过小型可学习适配器补偿特征损失，最后配合内存高效的向量索引存储嵌入向量。
AI.result: 在包含184小时屏幕历史的ScreenMemEval基准上，StreamEmbed在M2 Pro GPU上达到新的帕累托最优：比完整截图编码快达3.7倍且无精度损失；在同等延迟下比OCR索引高出最多6.3个Recall@10点；高效向量索引仅需0.13 GB RAM即可存储模拟一年的屏幕历史。
AI.conclusion: StreamEmbed使得以原生视觉形式实时索引屏幕历史成为现实，且资源占用极低，为完全本地化运行的视觉助手奠定了实用基础。
AI.translation: 屏幕历史可以作为人类和智能体的可检索视觉记忆，但与离线语料库不同，它必须在每张屏幕截图生成时即刻进行编码与索引。基于OCR的索引速度虽快但会丢失视觉信息；而完整的视觉编码耗时超过两秒。然而，屏幕内容的变化通常是增量式的：大多数像素在单张截图内部以及跨截图之间重复出现。这提出了一个问题：视觉编码器是否需要对每张新截图都从头开始重新计算其表示？我们提出了StreamEmbed，这是一个利用该冗余特性的增量视觉嵌入系统。该系统仅由像素差异引导，结合了跳过重复相邻块的空间Token剪枝，以及复用跨截图未发生变化块的缓存键与值的时间KV复用。一个轻量级的可学习适配器弥补了剪枝和复用带来的偏差，以保持对完整截图嵌入的高保真度。在ScreenMemEval基准（涵盖来自两名人类和一个计算机操作智能体的184小时屏幕历史、共计10,426个问题）上，StreamEmbed在M2 Pro GPU上建立了新的准确率-延迟帕累托前沿：其编码速度比完整截图编码快达3.7倍且不牺牲准确率，在同等延迟下比基于OCR的索引最多高出6.3个Recall@10点。一个高内存效率的向量索引仅需0.13 GB的RAM即可存储一整年模拟的截图。这些结果使以原生视觉形式实时索引屏幕历史变得切实可行，为完全本地运行的视觉助手奠定了基础。
AI.summary: 针对屏幕截图检索中视觉编码延迟高的问题，本文提出了StreamEmbed系统。该方法直接利用屏幕图像的时空像素冗余，结合空间Token剪枝、时间KV缓存复用以及轻量补偿适配器，实现了免于从头计算的高速增量视觉编码，在保持甚至超越基线精度的同时大幅降低延迟与内存占用。
AI.keywords: 屏幕截图检索, 增量视觉嵌入, Token剪枝, KV缓存复用, 实时索引
AI.comments: 该研究精准切中了本地化屏幕AI助手在实时处理高频截图流时的核心算力痛点。其核心创新在于巧妙利用了UI界面高度的局部平坦性和时间连续性，以无额外大模型开销的像素差异驱动时空KV复用与剪枝，在端侧（如M2 Pro）实现了高帧率和极低显存/内存占用。局限性在于：摘要未说明在全屏高动态变化（如频繁滚动或视频播放）等像素剧烈变动场景下系统的退化程度。

title: OpenLayout: An Open and Agentic-Driven Platform for Holistic VLSI Physical Design and Benchmarking
summary:
Physical design automation of very large-scale integrated circuits (VLSI) has made significant strides, progressing from single-stage placement and routing toward increasingly integrated full-flow implementation. Yet, existing approaches struggle with the vast design space optimization (DSO) arising from diverse technology nodes, circuit designs, and varied constraints. The substantial runtime of physical-design tools further exacerbates this challenge, leaving industrial workflows heavily dependent on experienced engineers to navigate the design space and achieve power, performance, and area (PPA) targets, incurring significant engineering effort.
  We argue that large language models (LLMs) with strong reasoning capabilities, enriched with distilled human design expertise, offer a promising path toward efficient and automated DSO. Unlike traditional algorithms, LLMs can interpret complex design contexts and naturally incorporate human expertise expressed in natural language for reasoning, acting, observing, and adapting throughout the design process, a capability that conventional optimization methods cannot exploit. To this end, we present OpenLayout, an agentic platform that leverages multi-agent collaboration with embedded design knowledge to enable self-iterative DSO. We further introduce OpenLayout-Bench, a benchmark targeting advanced technology nodes with commercial EDA tools to systematically evaluate physical design automation capabilities of LLMs. Experimental results demonstrate that OpenLayout achieves state-of-the-art performance, with approximately 20% accuracy improvement over baseline methods. Our work is open-sourced at https://github.com/fenggev56/OpenLayout

title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
summary: Detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) objects is essential for ensuring the reliability and safety of object detectors in real-world deployment. We treat the decision on a detected box as a hypothesis test with the null hypothesis that the box covers an object of an in-distribution (ID) class. The null distribution changes with the size of the box and its contact with the image border, and the detector observes both. The test can therefore rank a box only against ID boxes of the same size and border contact, which gives a distribution-free bound on the false-alarm rate for each of them and uncovers the separation that one null distribution hides. The power of the test also rests on the layer it reads. Layers built only for the ID classes have no reason to keep what sets an unknown object apart, so the test reads the features before them. We propose \textbf{PLUM}, a training-free score that pools the last backbone stage inside the box and ranks its distance to the ID classes among ID boxes of the same size and border contact. On the standard benchmark, PLUM reaches the highest AUROC among the compared methods without external models, with 91.5 and 94.5 on PASCAL-VOC and 95.1 and 97.5 on BDD100K. Code: https://github.com/DDOZMI/PLUM

AI.title_translation: 用于分布外目标检测的框条件假设检验
AI.tldr: 提出了一种免训练的OOD目标检测方法PLUM，通过结合框尺寸与边界接触属性进行条件假设检验排序，并利用主干网络特征实现了最先进的AUROC表现。
AI.motivation: 在分布外（OOD）目标检测中，检测框的零假设分布会随着框的大小及其与图像边界的接触状态而动态变化。传统的全局统一零分布会掩盖这种分离边界；此外，专门针对ID类别训练的深层网络往往会丢弃区分未知目标的关键特征，导致常规检验难以有效识别OOD目标。
AI.method: 提出了名为PLUM的免训练（training-free）评分方法：1. 将检测框判别建模为零假设检验（零假设为框内目标属于ID类别）；2. 提取检测器主干网络（Backbone）最后阶段的框内池化特征，以保留未被ID任务消除的未知目标特征；3. 仅在具有相同尺寸和边界接触情况的ID框集合中，对当前候选框到ID类别的距离进行条件相对排序打分。
AI.result: 在无需依赖外部模型的情况下，PLUM在标准基准测试中取得了最高的AUROC得分：在PASCAL-VOC基准上分别达到91.5和94.5，在BDD100K基准上分别达到95.1和97.5。
AI.conclusion: 通过利用检测框的几何属性（尺寸与边界接触）进行条件假设检验，并提取保留未知目标特征的主干网络层表征，能够有效突破传统全局分布评估的局限，显著提升分布外目标检测的准确度与可靠性。
AI.translation: 检测分布外（OOD）目标对于确保目标检测器在实际部署中的可靠性和安全性至关重要。我们将针对检测框的决策视为一项假设检验，其零假设是该框覆盖了分布内（ID）类别的目标。零分布会随框的大小及其与图像边界的接触情况而改变，而检测器能同时观察到这两者。因此，该检验可以仅针对相同尺寸和边界接触的ID框对某个候选框进行排序，从而为每个框提供无分布假警报率界限，并揭示出单一零分布所掩盖的分离界限。检验的效能还取决于其读取的特征层；仅针对ID类别构建的层没有理由保留区分未知物体的特征，因此该检验读取这些层之前的特征。我们提出了PLUM，这是一种免训练的评分方法，它在检测框内池化主干网络最后阶段的特征，并在具有相同大小和边界接触的ID框中对其到ID类的距离进行排序。在标准基准上，PLUM在无需外部模型的对比方法中达到了最高的AUROC，在PASCAL-VOC上分别达到91.5和94.5，在BDD100K上达到95.1和97.5。代码：https://github.com/DDOZMI/PLUM
AI.summary: 本文针对分布外（OOD）目标检测提出了基于框条件假设检验的免训练方法PLUM。作者指出ID目标的零分布与检测框尺寸及边界接触显著相关，且主干网络特征更适于保留未知物体信息。PLUM通过在相同几何条件的ID框中对框内主干特征距离进行条件排序，在不依赖额外模型的前提下在PASCAL-VOC和BDD100K基准上均刷新了最高AUROC纪录。
AI.keywords: 分布外目标检测 (OOD Detection), 假设检验 (Hypothesis Testing), 条件排序 (Conditional Ranking), 免训练 (Training-free)
AI.comments: 1. 创新性：该研究敏锐地观察到目标检测中零分布受检测框几何属性（尺寸与边界接触）影响的特性，打破了以往全局统一评估的范式，采用条件假设检验思路，理论逻辑严密且新颖；2. 实用性：PLUM方法无需额外训练或引入复杂外部模型，即插即用，在保持高效的同时大幅刷新了基准性能；3. 局限性：摘要未详细说明条件分组（分箱）的具体离散化策略与匹配开销，在超高分辨率或密集场景下的计算耗时有待进一步评估。

title: Patient-specific Modeling of the Tricuspid Valve from 3D Transesophageal Echocardiography
comments: Draft manuscript of 3D TEE to FEM modelling pipeline for human tricuspid valves
summary: Purpose: Image-based patient-specific simulations of the tricuspid valve (TV) could support repair planning. However, clinical images incompletely resolve the chordal anatomy and cannot directly determine tissue properties, which hinders the development of such models. We developed and evaluated a framework that simulates the TV from clinical images and addresses these limitations using measurements on explanted human valves. Methods: We reconstructed ten functionally competent human TVs from 3D transesophageal echocardiography. Following manual segmentation, we automatically built finite element models with synthetic chordae and with leaflet thickness, chordal insertion density, and tissue properties informed by ex vivo human measurements. Next, we used shape matching and force-based chordal-length adjustment to simulate valve closure. We also assessed inter-observer segmentation variability and sensitivity to chordal insertion density, leaflet stiffness, leaflet thickness, and chordal size and material properties. Results: Per-valve median geometric errors were 0.61-1.13 mm relative to the morphed references and 0.55-0.95 mm relative to the image-derived surfaces. Coaptation covered 20-42% of the leaflet area, and median leaflet stresses ranged from 7.6 to 16.9 kPa. Inter-observer variability in segmentation most strongly affected coaptation area. Of the population-based inputs, insertion density and leaflet stiffness most affected geometric error. Thickness primarily affected stress, whereas chordal size and material properties had limited effects. Conclusion: Clinical echocardiography, supplemented with ex vivo human tissue data, enabled patient-specific simulation of ten human TVs. This framework provides a foundation for investigating valve mechanics and developing repair-planning tools, while sensitivity analyses identify priorities for model refinement and uncertainty assessment.

AI.title_translation: 基于三维经食管超声心动图的患者特异性三尖瓣建模
AI.tldr: 本研究结合3D经食管超声与离体人体组织数据构建了患者特异性三尖瓣有限元闭合模型，实现了高精度模拟并揭示了关键力学参数敏感性。
AI.motivation: 基于影像的患者特异性三尖瓣模拟有助于辅助瓣膜修复规划，但临床影像难以清晰分辨腱索解剖结构且无法直接测量组织力学属性，阻碍了此类模型的开发。
AI.method: 从10例功能正常的人体三维经食管超声心动图（3D TEE）中手动分割并重建三尖瓣；利用离体人体测量数据赋予瓣叶厚度、腱索插入密度和组织力学特性，自动构建带有合成腱索的有限元模型；采用形状匹配与基于力的腱索长度自适应调整算法模拟瓣膜闭合；评估了观察者间分割差异，并对腱索插入密度、瓣叶刚度与厚度、腱索尺寸及力学参数进行了敏感性分析。
AI.result: 各瓣膜相对于变形参考面的几何误差中位数为0.61~1.13 mm，相对于影像衍生表面的几何误差中位数为0.55~0.95 mm；对合面积占瓣叶面积的20%~42%，瓣叶应力中位数为7.6~16.9 kPa；观察者间分割变异对对合面积影响最显著；在群体先验参数中，插入密度和瓣叶刚度对几何误差影响最大，厚度主要影响应力，而腱索尺寸和材料特性的影响有限。
AI.conclusion: 结合临床超声心动图与离体人体组织数据，成功实现了10例人类三尖瓣的患者特异性模拟。该框架为研究瓣膜生物力学和开发修复规划工具奠定了基础，敏感性分析也指明了模型优化与不确定性评估的重点方向。
AI.translation: 目的：基于影像的患者特异性三尖瓣（TV）模拟有助于辅助修复手术规划。然而，临床影像无法完全分辨腱索解剖结构，也无法直接测定组织特性，这阻碍了此类模型的发展。我们开发并评估了一个基于临床影像模拟三尖瓣的框架，并利用离体人体瓣膜的测量数据解决了上述局限性。方法：我们基于三维经食管超声心动图重建了10例功能健全的人体三尖瓣。在手动分割后，结合离体人体测量获得的瓣叶厚度、腱索插入密度和组织力学特性，自动建立了带有合成腱索的有限元模型。随后，采用形状匹配和基于力的腱索长度调整方法模拟瓣膜闭合。我们还评估了观察者间的分割变异性，以及对腱索插入密度、瓣叶刚度、瓣叶厚度、腱索尺寸和材料特性的敏感性。结果：每个瓣膜相对于变形参考的几何误差中位数为0.61-1.13毫米，相对于影像衍生表面的中位误差为0.55-0.95毫米。对合区域覆盖了20-42%的瓣叶面积，瓣叶应力中位数为7.6至16.9千帕。分割中的观察者间变异对对合面积的影响最为显著。在基于人群的输入参数中，插入密度和瓣叶刚度对几何误差的影响最大。厚度主要影响应力，而腱索尺寸和材料特性的影响较为有限。结论：临床超声心动图辅以离体人体组织数据，使得对10个人体三尖瓣进行患者特异性模拟成为可能。该框架为研究瓣膜生物力学和开发修复规划工具奠定了基础，同时敏感性分析也确定了模型改进和不确定性评估的重点。
AI.summary: 针对临床影像中腱索结构不清晰及材料特性无法直接获取的问题，本研究提出了一种结合三维经食管超声心动图与离体人体测量数据的患者特异性三尖瓣有限元建模框架。对10例三尖瓣的闭合模拟显示出亚毫米级的几何重建精度，并通过敏感性分析揭示了分割变异、瓣叶刚度与腱索插入密度对模拟结果的关键影响，为临床三尖瓣修复手术规划工具的开发提供了重要支撑。
AI.keywords: 三尖瓣, 经食管超声心动图, 患者特异性建模, 有限元模拟, 生物力学
AI.comments: 该研究的创新之处在于将临床3D TEE影像与离体人体组织测量数据相结合，通过合成腱索及力学调整算法克服了临床影像中腱索结构与组织力学特性难以直接获取的瓶颈。研究不仅实现了闭合模拟，还系统分析了分割差异及参数敏感性，为未来三尖瓣修复手术规划提供了有力工具。局限在于依赖人工分割，且腱索参数和材料属性采用群体先验数据而非完全患者特异性。

title: Mutable Inference: Architecting LLM Accelerators for Inference-Time Learning
summary:
Long-context LLMs must retain growing histories, but full attention makes each new token increasingly expensive. Inference-time learning (ITL) offers another approach. The model keeps training on the context during inference, retaining what it learns in its weights. Recent work shows that ITL can match full-context attention quality while attending only to a recent fixed-size window. This bounds attention costs but adds Learning (backward computation and weight updates) alongside Prediction (the forward pass) costs. Inference accelerators assume fixed weights, while training accelerators target complete training steps.
  This work identifies two opportunities. Attention's non-matrix operations leave enough idle matrix capacity for Learning, while selected layers can tolerate delayed weight updates with little quality loss. We exploit both with Learning While Serving (LWS), an inference accelerator architecture that shares compute hardware between latency-critical Prediction and deadline-flexible Learning. Hardware-managed per-layer weight versioning allows Learning to publish updates while in-flight computations read older versions. Resumable reduction blocks let Learning kernels span fragmented idle windows and yield to Prediction, while dedicated softmax-gradient units relieve vector contention.
