title: Directional Confusions Reveal Divergent Inductive Biases Through Rate-Distortion Geometry in Human and Machine Vision
summary: Humans and modern vision models can reach similar classification accuracy while making systematically different kinds of mistakes -- differing not in how often they err, but in who gets mistaken for whom and in which direction. We show that these directional confusions reveal distinct inductive biases that are invisible to accuracy alone. Using matched human and deep vision model responses on a natural-image categorization task under 12 perturbation types, we quantify asymmetry in confusion matrices and link it to the shape of the information-error trade-off. We characterize this trade-off geometry using three signatures extracted from the rate-distortion (RD) frontier: slope beta, curvature kappa and efficiency (AUC). We find that humans exhibit broad but weak asymmetries, whereas deep vision models show sparser, stronger directional collapses. Robustness training reduces global asymmetry but fails to recover the human-like breadth-strength profile of graded similarity. Mechanistic simulations further show that different asymmetry organizations shift the RD frontier in opposite directions, even when matched for performance. Together, these results position directional confusions and RD geometry as compact, interpretable signatures of inductive bias under distribution shift.

title: Explicit Planar Finite Element Elasticity Complexes and $C^1$ Elements on Barycentric Refinements
summary: We give a closed-form realization of the finite element elasticity complex associated with the Arnold--Douglas--Gupta family on barycentric refinements. Their construction implies the existence of minimal $C^1$ potential spaces, but does not provide explicit general-degree scalar enrichments. On each macrotriangle, we derive three divergence-free stress enrichments and their Airy potentials. For every degree $q\geq4$, the resulting potential space enriches $\mathbb P_q$ by three explicit functions. A geometric decomposition yields unisolvent degrees of freedom and $C^1$ assembly without vertex supersmoothness. The space attains the dimension bound for macroelements containing $\mathbb P_q$ with full polynomial boundary trace freedom. Its Airy image is the divergence-free subspace of the corresponding stress space, and global assembly gives an exact discrete elasticity complex on simply connected domains. The low-order spaces $U_2$ and $U_3$ recover the reduced and full Hsieh--Clough--Tocher spaces, respectively.

title: Analytically Characterized Optimal Power Control for Signal-Level-Integrated Sensing, Computing and Communication in Federated Learning
summary: In next-generation wireless edge systems, efficient functionality integration is essential to address the growing demands of communication, computation, and sensing. Signal-level integrated sensing, computing, and communication (Sig-ISCC) is envisioned, where a single waveform simultaneously supports sensing, computing and communication via over-the-air computation (AirComp). Meanwhile, federated learning (FL) is widely regarded as a promising distributed machine learning framework that enables network intelligence in a privacy-preserving and secure manner, and exhibits strong synergy with AirComp, which alleviates the communication bottleneck of FL. In this paper, we study uplink Sig-ISCC design for AirComp-FL with joint target detection. We formulate the joint power and receive-scaling control problem, where edge devices' transmitted signals should serve both sensing and AirComp purposes. The goal is to minimize the AirComp aggregation distortion subject to a joint target-detection requirement. Although the resulting problem is non-convex in the original variables, we show that it admits an equivalent convex reformulation after a suitable variable transformation. By exploiting analytical optimality properties, we develop a robust, optimal, and polynomial-time-complexity algorithm that efficiently achieves the optimal transmit powers and receive scaling factor. Simulation results validate the optimality and numerical robustness of the proposed algorithm and show its superior FL performance compared to baseline methods.

title: BoostLoRA: Growing Effective Rank by Boosting Adapters
summary: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods face a tradeoff between adapter size and expressivity: ultra-low-parameter adapters are confined to fixed low-rank subspaces, capping performance even with extended training. We propose BoostLoRA, a gradient-boosting framework that overcomes this limit by iteratively training and merging minimal adapters on the examples the current model gets wrong. A ROTATE SVD basis strategy assigns each round to an orthogonal subspace, so cumulative effective rank grows linearly with the number of rounds while each adapter remains ultra-low-rank. After merging, adapters are discarded, leaving zero inference overhead. On Qwen2.5-3B, BoostLoRA reaches 89.1% on GSM8K and 68.8% on MATH-500, surpassing both the best single-shot ultra-low parameter adapter (TinyLoRA) and full fine-tuning; on code generation it reaches 57.2% on MBPP and 80.4% on HumanEval while full fine-tuning drops below the zero-shot baseline. We also demonstrate cross-architecture transfer on protein binding classification with ESM2-650M and cross-entropy training. BoostLoRA is, to our knowledge, the first PEFT method whose effective rank grows with training, separating per-round parameter cost from total representational capacity.

title: SoCal: A Language for Memory-Layout Factorization of Recursive Datatypes
summary: Array-of-structures (AoS) to structure-of-arrays (SoA) is a classic compiler transformation that improves memory locality and enables data-parallel execution. Existing AoS-to-SoA transformations target regular, array-based programs in imperative languages, such as C. However, many applications traverse tree-shaped data such as ASTs in compilers, DOM trees in browsers, and k-d trees in scientific workloads. Prior work speeds up functional programs over trees by serializing algebraic datatypes (ADTs) into one contiguous buffer. Such a representation interleaves the fields of every node, similar to an AoS layout. We introduce a factored layout of ADTs, which stores its fields in separate buffers, producing a layout that resembles SoA. In a factored layout, a traversal can focus on relevant fields and ignore the rest, similar to extracting a column from a SoA representation; in this setting, traversals over scalar fields can be vectorized. Working with raw byte arrays is error-prone, though: wrong indexing can silently read bytes from a wrong field or write past the end of a value. We therefore introduce SoCal, a type-safe language for expressing traversals over factored ADTs. Our compiler, Colobus, transforms a simple functional language with ADTs reminiscent of Haskell to C, using SoCal as the intermediate representation. Colobus generates traversals over byte arrays in the factored representation and performs optimizations such as field skipping and vectorization. Across a suite of benchmarks, Colobus shows the average speedups of 3.8x and 5.2x over fold and map passes, respectively.

title: Time series causal discovery with variable lags
summary: Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) are a powerful tool for reasoning under uncertainty about complex real-world problems. Such problems evolve over time, responding to external shocks as they occur. To support decision-making, CBNs require a cause-and-effect map of the variables under consideration, known as the network's structure. Learning the graphical structure of a causal model from data remains challenging; learning it from time-series data is even harder because dependencies may arise at different time lags. We construct a method that jointly learns a temporal ordering and a dominant lag for each selected ordered variable pair. Our contribution is a decomposable BIC-style objective score for mixed data that combines node-specific sample sizes with a penalty favouring recent lags. We optimise this objective using a Tabu search augmented with change-lag moves and greedy per-child lag tuning, while its node-wise decomposition supports cached and parallel neighbourhood evaluation. We establish acyclicity and complexity results and derive recovery limits when effects are distributed across multiple lags. In simulations, we show that the proposed method outperforms an inflexible lag-1 score-based learner in most evaluated settings, whereas most specialised methods achieve higher recovery accuracy on data that satisfy their assumptions. On a real-world UK COVID-19 dataset, the method learnt an expected short-lag-skewed structure; nevertheless, 46.8% of selected edges had lags greater than one, showing that longer delays can be retained when their improved fit offsets the penalty. Under its no-contemporaneous-edges and causal-sufficiency assumptions, the method provides a computationally tractable subroutine for edge-specific single-lag optimisation, complementing score-based causal discovery methods.

title: Finding accurate eigenvalues and eigenvectors of positive semi-definite matrices given a subspace
summary: We revisit a classical problem in numerical linear algebra: given a $k$-dimensional subspace $\mathcal{Q}$ with orthonormal basis $Q$ that approximates the leading eigenspace of an $n\times n$ positive semi-definite matrix $A$, the goal is to extract high-accuracy eigenvalues. The Rayleigh-Ritz (RR) method is the standard algorithm for the task, which has been shown to be optimal in several ways (when $A$ is symmetric, not necessarily positive semi-definite $A\succeq 0$). In this paper, we show that when $A\succeq 0$, alternative methods can outperform RR, including Nystr{ö}m and one-sided projected SVD, while having the same computational complexity; that is, the main cost is in computing $AQ$, plus an $O(nk^2)$ term. In particular, we advocate the use of Nystr{ö}m's method, quantitatively showing that the approximate leading eigenvalues have better accuracy than RR, and the improvement can be arbitrarily large. The significant accuracy improvement occurs for the first $i$ eigenvalues if $λ_i \gg λ_{k+1}$ and uniformly for all $k$ eigenvalues if $λ_k \gg λ_{k+1}$. This theoretical observation can be extended to the case where we extract $k$ leading eigenvalues from a larger-dimensional subspace. A similar improvement is numerically observed for the purpose of approximating the leading eigenvectors. In contrast, when the target eigenvalues are the trailing ones, the situation is reversed, and the Nystr{ö}m method performs poorly; we suggest a remedy based on a shift for this situation.

title: Retrieval of Coastal Biogeochemical Parameters From Near-Surface Hyperspectral Remote Sensing Reflectance Using Physics-Aware Meta-Learning
summary: Hyperspectral in situ sensing has shown promise in retrieving aquatic water quality (WQ) parameters, such as total suspended solids (TSS), dissolved organic carbon (DOC), and total chlorophyll-a (TChl-a), for cost-effective management of coastal WQ. However, generalising such retrieval algorithms across water bodies remains challenging, as the relationship between remote sensing reflectance ($R_{rs}$) and WQ parameters can vary considerably from one region to another due to regional distinctions in environmental conditions and biogeochemistry that lead to different WQ ranges and bio-optical properties. In this study, we propose a two-stage physics-aware meta-learning framework for retrieving coastal WQ parameters from near-surface $R_{rs}$ observations. Unlike purely data-driven approaches trained solely on paired observations, the proposed framework incorporates physical knowledge through a two-stage learning process. In the first stage, a region-agnostic base model is pretrained using meta-learning on synthetic WQ--$R_{rs}$ samples generated by a bio-optical forward model parameterised with an in situ bio-optical spectral library. In the second stage, the pretrained model is fine-tuned using local samples to adapt to regional conditions. To evaluate the proposed approach, we collected in situ hyperspectral $R_{rs}$ and WQ measurements from five geographically distinct sites in Australian coastal waters.

title: Exposing and Mitigating Temporal Attack in Deepfake Video Detection
summary: While spatiotemporal deepfake detectors achieve high AUC, our experiments reveal their susceptibility to evasion attacks. These models tend to overfit on fragile temporal spectrum cues, rather than learning robust semantic causality. To mitigate this vulnerability, we propose SpInShield, a temporal spectral-invariant defense framework explicitly designed to decouple semantic motion from manipulatable spectral artifacts. We propose a learnable spectral adversary that dynamically synthesizes severe spectral deformations, simulating extreme attack scenarios. By employing a shortcut suppression optimization strategy, SpInShield compels the encoder to extract reliable forensic cues while purging unstable spectral statistics from the latent space. Experiments show that SpInShield obtains competitive performance on widely used datasets and outperforms the strongest baseline by 21.30 percentage points in AUC under simulated amplitude spectral attacks.

title: InsHuman: Towards Natural and Identity-Preserving Human Insertion
summary: Human insertion aims to naturally place specific individuals into a target background. Although existing image editing models may have such ability, they often produce failure cases, including inappropriate human pose in new background, inconsistent number of people, and modified facial identity. Moreover, publicly available human datasets often lack full-body portraits and realistic physical interaction between humans and their background. To address these challenges, we propose InsHuman for natural and identity-preserving human insertion. Specifically, we propose Human-Background Adaptive Fusion (HBAF), which detects foreground humans to obtain a binary mask and applies region-aware weighting to align the human regions between predicted and ground-truth latents, ensuring the person's pose, count, and overall appearance are coherently adapted to the target background.We further propose Face-to-Face ID-Preserving (FFIP), which detects and matches faces between the generated image and the source image in terms of face recognition features to enforce identity consistency for each face.In addition, we propose Bidirectional Data Pairing (BDP) strategy to construct BDP-InsHuman, a high-quality dataset with realistic human-background interactions. Experiments demonstrate that InsHuman achieves significant improvements in generating plausible images while keeping human identity unchanged.

title: Multi-Environment POMDPs with Finite-Horizon Objectives
summary: Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) are systems in which one agent interacts with a stochastic environment, and receives only partial information about the current state. In a multi-environment POMDP (MEPOMDP), the initial state is unknown, and assumed to be adversarially chosen. In this work we focus on computing the optimal value and policy in MEPOMDPs with finite-horizon objectives. That problem is known to be PSPACE-complete in POMDPs. The extension is nontrivial: MEPOMDPs require reasoning about beliefs and payoffs across environments, and deterministic policies are no longer enough for optimal payoff. While the lower bound transfers immediately, the upper bound requires new techniques: we prove that mixtures of at most $n$ deterministic policies suffice for $n$ environments and show how to explore them without storing exponential-size policy descriptions. Our main results are as follows: (1) we establish that it is also PSPACE-complete in the more general setting of MEPOMDPs; (2) we present a practical algorithm and evaluate it on classical benchmarks, significantly outperforming the only previously known algorithm.

title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Domain Shift in Permission-Based Android Malware Detection
summary: Machine learning-based Android malware detectors often fail in real-world deployment due to domain shift, where models trained on one data source perform poorly on applications from another. This paper presents a comprehensive study on the generalizability and interpretability of permission-based detectors under cross-domain conditions. Using two complementary datasets (PerMalDroid and NATICUSdroid) and five ensemble classifiers, we first establish an intra-domain baseline, where models achieve over 92% accuracy, and then quantify a severe asymmetric performance drop. While models trained on PerMalDroid generalize well to NATICUSdroid (86% accuracy), the reverse direction sees a drastic drop to 73% accuracy. Explainable AI analysis reveals bimodal feature distributions and shows that feature importance is highly unstable, with key permissions losing or gaining influence across domains. The predictive feature sets for different domains are fundamentally mismatched, as models rely on different, dataset-specific permissions. Most importantly, an ablation study demonstrates that for most models, training on a noisy feature set leads to poor generalization, confirming that domain-specific artifacts are a greater obstacle than missing features. To mitigate this, we validate a hybrid training strategy based on the intersection of common features and successfully recover cross-domain performance, achieving 88% accuracy on PerMalDroid and maintaining 97% on NATICUSdroid. These findings highlight the importance of explainable, cross-domain-robust malware detection systems and provide a practical pathway toward improving real-world deployment of permission-based Android malware detectors.

title: Do LLMs Experience an Internal Polylogue? Investigating Reasoning through the Lens of Personas
summary: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) encode behavioural traits ("personas") as linear directions in activation space, often called "persona vectors". Prior work has used such directions as static handles for behavioural steering. We instead treat them as dynamic signals: probes we can monitor and intervene on as reasoning unfolds. We use the term polylogue to denote the time series of alignments between persona vectors and hidden activations over the course of generation. Experiments across four open-weight models show that polylogue features predict correctness on MMLU-Pro on par with low-dimensional activation baselines, while remaining interpretable through their associated persona directions. They also suggest concrete steering targets, namely which latent directions to modulate at different stages of a response. We instantiate this as a simple paragraph-conditioned intervention that improves accuracy on three of four models but degrades the fourth, suggesting that stage-aware latent steering is possible but not yet robust. Together, this positions the polylogue as an interpretable tool for reasoning-time monitoring and intervention.

title: When Adaptation Fails: A Gradient-Based Diagnosis of Collapsed Gating in Vision-Language Prompt Learning
comments: Revised technical descriptions and diagnostic interpretations; clarified gate definitions, effective-length normalization, and regularization formulas. Reported benchmark results remain unchanged
summary: Adaptive prompting mechanisms have been proposed to enhance vision-language models by dynamically tailoring prompts to inputs. However, in frozen few-shot prompt learning with CLIP-style backbones, we systematically observe that adaptive gates and prompt-selection modules often collapse: they produce nearly constant outputs, contribute negligible gradient signals, and frequently fail to outperform fixed prompts. To further explore this issue, we present a systematic diagnostic study to uncover the underlying causes and conditions of adaptation failure. Through controlled experiments across datasets and multiple prompt learning architectures, we identify two recurring failure modes: gradient magnitude imbalance and gate degradation. Our findings invite a re-examination of indiscriminately adding architectural complexity in parameter-efficient learning and clarify when prompt-level adaptive gating is, and is not, effective in this regime.

title: Hybrid Mechanical and Agentic Specification Inference
summary: Adoption of formal verification has long been hindered by the cost of manual specification. To prove high-level properties, one must also write contracts for supporting functions, many of which are mechanical and low-level. Specification inference automatically derives such contracts from the program. We present a hybrid of mechanical and agentic inference for Move, a smart contract language, integrated into its verifier, the Move Prover. A large language model (LLM) agent drives inference and verification through a tool that calls the Move Prover and derives specifications from code by weakest-precondition (WP) analysis. We evaluate our approach on 26 targets, 24 of them extracted from public Move functions of the Aptos framework that have no specifications, under a frontier model and a mid-tier model of the same family (Sol 5.6 and Terra 5.6). With and without WP, the agent completes over 90% of its runs, so agentic inference is effective on its own. Adding WP lowers its cost by 11-21% overall and by 40-64% on targets without loops.

title: Adaptive Calibration in Non-Stationary Environments
summary: Making calibrated online predictions is a central challenge in modern AI systems. Much of the existing literature focuses on fully adversarial environments where outcomes may be arbitrary, leading to conservative algorithms that can perform suboptimally in more benign settings, such as when outcomes are nearly stationary. This gap raises a natural question: can we design online prediction algorithms whose calibration error automatically adapts to the degree of non-stationarity in the environment, smoothly interpolating between i.i.d. and adversarial regimes? We answer this question in the affirmative and develop a suite of algorithms that achieve adaptive calibration guarantees under multiple calibration measures. Specifically, with $T$ being the number of rounds, $W$ being the unknown number of i.i.d. segments of the environment, and $C\in[0,T]$ being another unknown non-stationary measure defined as the minimal $\ell_1$ deviation of the mean outcomes, our algorithms attain $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\min\{\sqrt{T}+(TC)^{\frac{1}{3}}, \sqrt{WT}\})$ for $\ell_1$ calibration error and $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\min\{(1+C)^{\frac{1}{3}}, W\})$ for both $\ell_2$ and pseudo KL calibration error. These bounds match the optimal rates in the stationary case ($C=0$ and $W=1$) and recover known guarantees in the fully adversarial regime ($C, W=Ω(T)$). Our approach builds on and extends prior work (Hu et al., 2026; Luo et al., 2025), introducing an epoch-based scheduling together with a novel non-uniform partition of the prediction space that allocates finer resolution near the underlying ground truth.

title: Memory Constrained Adversarial Hypothesis Testing
summary: We study adversarial binary hypothesis testing under memory constraints. The test is a time-invariant randomized finite state machine (FSM) with S states. Associated with each hypothesis is a set of distributions. Given the hypothesis, the distribution of each sample is chosen from the set associated with the hypothesis by an adversary who has access to past samples and the history of states of the FSM so far. We obtain upper and lower bounds on the minimax asymptotic error probability that are tight to within one state. These bounds determine the exact error exponent in S, and coincide under a weak least-favourability condition. For time-invariant deterministic FSMs, we also extend known achievable error-exponent bounds from the non-adversarial Bernoulli setting to the adversarial case with parameters in two separated intervals.

title: D-VLA: A High-Concurrency Distributed Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: The rapid evolution of Embodied AI has enabled Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to excel in multimodal perception and task execution. However, applying Reinforcement Learning (RL) to these massive models in large-scale distributed environments faces severe systemic bottlenecks, primarily due to the resource conflict between high-fidelity physical simulation and the intensive VRAM/bandwidth demands of deep learning. This conflict often leaves overall throughput constrained by execution-phase inefficiencies. To address these challenges, we propose D-VLA, a high-concurrency, low-latency distributed RL framework for large-scale embodied foundation models. D-VLA introduces "Plane Decoupling," physically isolating high-frequency training data from low-frequency weight control to eliminate interference between simulation and optimization. We further design a four-thread asynchronous "Swimlane" pipeline, enabling full parallel overlap of sampling, inference, gradient computation, and parameter distribution. Additionally, a dual-pool VRAM management model and topology-aware replication resolve memory fragmentation and optimize communication efficiency. Experiments on benchmarks like LIBERO show that D-VLA significantly outperforms mainstream RL frameworks in throughput and sampling efficiency for billion-parameter VLA models. In trillion-parameter scalability tests, our framework maintains exceptional stability and linear speedup, providing a robust system for high-performance general-purpose embodied agents.

title: Shortcut Mitigation via Spurious-Positive Samples
summary: Shortcut mitigation strategies commonly rely on training data annotations, group-balanced held-out data or the presence of all groups, i.e., all combinations of (spurious) attributes and classes, in the training data. However, these requirements are rarely met in practice. We instead propose a method for targeted model analysis to identify a small set of instances in which the model relies on spurious attributes. Using that set and following ``this feature should not be used for prediction'' reasoning, we identify highly relevant neurons in an intermediate layer and regularize their impact. This ensures that models learn to depend on informative features rather than being right for the wrong reasons, thereby improving robustness without requiring additional balanced held-out data or annotations.

title: Adequate Losses via Quantitative Linear Logic
comments: Numerous tweaks and small corrections. To appear at POPL 2027
summary: As neural components are increasingly embedded in existing symbolic software -- including safety-critical systems -- the question arises of how to specify and enforce the safety of the newly introduced neural parts. Unlike traditional logical specifications, these must be amenable not only to the standard Boolean interpretation, but also to training and optimisation. The latter calls for a quantitative interpretation of the logical syntax, subject to further requirements such as smoothness and differentiability. Moreover, the qualitative and quantitative sides of the logic must share a unifying proof-theoretic and categorical semantics. Finally, the new logic should link cleanly to the substructural and program logics that underpin the verification of existing symbolic programs. In this paper, we present a logic that ticks all of these boxes. We introduce a family of calculi, $p$QLL, indexed by a hardness degree $p$, prove a cut-elimination theorem for them, and establish completeness with respect to enriched residuated `soft' lattices. At $p = \infty$, $p$QLL reduces to multiplicative additive linear logic (MALL), and provability in $p$QLL converges to provability in MALL as $p \to \infty$. We express optimisation objectives in the syntax of this logic and prove the quantitative adequacy of neuro-symbolic loss functions -- a result that has eluded the neuro-symbolic machine learning community for nearly a decade.

AI.summary: 本文提出了名为 $p$QLL 的定量线性逻辑演算族，兼具逻辑证明与可微优化的特性，在富集剩余软格上具备完备性并满足割消定理。当硬度参数趋向无穷时其收敛于乘法可加线性逻辑，并首次在理论上严格证明了神经符号损失函数的定量充分性。
AI.keywords: 定量线性逻辑 (Quantitative Linear Logic), 神经符号学习 (Neuro-symbolic Learning), 定量充分性 (Quantitative Adequacy), 割消定理 (Cut-elimination), 损失函数 (Loss Functions)
AI.comments: 该论文的创新之处在于利用定量线性逻辑（$p$QLL）成功在神经符号学习中架起了可微优化与形式逻辑证明的桥梁，首次严格证明了神经符号损失函数的定量充分性（quantitative adequacy），填补了该领域近十年来的理论空白，为安全关键型神经符号系统的验证与训练提供了坚实的数理逻辑基础。

title: ShopGym: An Integrated Framework for Realistic Simulation and Scalable Benchmarking of E-Commerce Web Agents
summary: Developing and evaluating e-commerce web agents requires environments that preserve meaningful task structure while enabling controllable, reproducible, and scalable scientific comparison. Existing methods force a tradeoff: live storefronts provide realism but are non-stationary, difficult to inspect, and irreproducible, while hand-built sandbox benchmarks provide control but cover only a narrow range of layouts, catalogs, policies, and interaction patterns. We argue that the core bottleneck is methodological: the field lacks a scalable way to construct evaluation settings that are simultaneously realistic, diverse, controllable, inspectable, and reproducible. We introduce ShopGym, an integrated framework for realistic simulation and scalable benchmarking of e-commerce web agents. Its simulation layer, ShopArena, converts live seed storefronts into self-contained sandbox shops through anonymized shop specifications and a staged, validated generation process. On top of these simulated storefronts, ShopGuru synthesizes benchmark tasks across seven skill categories, grounding each task in the shop's catalog, navigation structure, policies, and interaction affordances. Together, ShopArena and ShopGuru produce self-contained, resettable, inspectable, and stable evaluation artifacts that preserve structural properties and agent-evaluation signals relevant to shopping tasks. We validate the framework through graph-based structural analysis and agent-based behavioral evaluation with 224 generated tasks across six sandbox shops (three with synthetic data, three with real data). Results show that synthetic shops preserve key structural properties of live storefronts, and that agent success rates on synthetic twins closely track live storefronts, with matching per-skill profiles and failure modes. Generating ten shops shows the pipeline scales at about $60 per shop with declining human effort.

AI.title_translation: ShopGym：用于电子商务Web智能体逼真模拟与可扩展基准测试的集成框架
AI.tldr: ShopGym通过结合沙盒商店生成（ShopArena）与评测任务合成（ShopGuru），以低成本、可扩展的方式构建了兼具高度真实感、可控性与可复现性的电商Web智能体基准测试环境。
AI.motivation: 开发和评估电商Web智能体亟需兼顾任务真实性与实验可控/可复现性的环境。现有的实时网店具有真实感但不可复现且不可控，而手工构建的沙盒虽可控但覆盖模式狭窄，领域内缺乏一种兼具真实性、多样性、可控性与可扩展性的评估构建方法。
AI.method: 提出了ShopGym集成框架：1）模拟层ShopArena：通过匿名化商店规范与分阶段验证生成流程，将实时种子网店转化为自包含的沙盒网店；2）任务合成层ShopGuru：基于网店的目录、导航结构、政策与交互功能，合成跨越7个技能类别的基准任务，共同生成自包含、可重置、可审查且稳定的评测环境。
AI.result: 通过图结构分析及6个沙盒网店（含224个任务）的智能体行为评测表明，合成网店保留了真实网店的关键结构属性；智能体在合成孪生网店中的成功率、各技能画像及失败模式均与真实网店高度贴合；生成10家网店证明该管线平均每家成本仅约60美元且人工干预逐渐减少。
AI.conclusion: ShopGym成功提供了一种兼具高真实感、多样性、可控性、可审查性与可复现性的评测方案，能够以低成本可扩展地构建电商沙盒环境，有效保留了与真实网店高度一致的智能体评估信号。
AI.translation: 开发和评估电子商务Web智能体需要能够保留有意义的任务结构，同时支持可控、可复现和可扩展的科学比较的环境。现有方法被迫面临权衡：实时在线网店具有真实感，但具有非平稳性、难以审查且不可复现；而人工构建的沙盒基准虽然可控，但仅覆盖狭窄的布局、目录、政策和交互模式。我们认为核心瓶颈在于方法论层面：该领域缺乏一种可扩展的方法来构建兼具真实性、多样性、可控性、可审查性和可复现性的评估环境。我们介绍了ShopGym，这是一个用于电子商务Web智能体逼真模拟与可扩展基准测试的集成框架。其模拟层ShopArena通过匿名化的商店规范以及分阶段、经过验证的生成过程，将真实的种子网店转换为独立的沙盒商店。在这些模拟网店的基础上，ShopGuru跨七个技能类别合成基准任务，将每项任务扎根于商店的目录、导航结构、政策和交互功能中。ShopArena和ShopGuru共同产生了自包含、可重置、可审查和稳定的评估产物，这些产物保留了与购物任务相关的结构属性和智能体评估信号。我们通过基于图的结构分析以及在六个沙盒商店（三个具有合成数据，三个具有真实数据）上生成的224个任务的智能体行为评估验证了该框架。结果表明，合成商店保留了实时网店的关键结构属性，并且智能体在合成孪生网店上的成功率与实时网店紧密吻合，具备相匹配的单项技能画像和失败模式。生成十家网店表明该流水线具有扩展性，成本约为每家商店60美元，且人工工作量不断下降。
AI.summary: 本文提出了用于电商Web智能体模拟与基准评测的ShopGym框架，该框架包含沙盒生成层ShopArena和多技能任务合成层ShopGuru。实验表明，ShopGym能以低成本（约60美元/店）生成保留真实网店结构和智能体行为信号的自包含沙盒，成功化解了评测中真实感与可复现性的矛盾。
AI.keywords: 电商Web智能体, 沙盒模拟, 基准测试, ShopGym, 可复现性
AI.comments: 该研究的创新之处在于通过ShopArena和ShopGuru的模块化设计，首次系统性地解决了Web智能体评测在“真实环境不可复现”与“手工沙盒缺乏多样性与真实度”之间的权衡难题，实现了约60美元/店的高性价比扩展。重要性在于为电商Agent的标准化对比提供了自包含、可重置且可审查的测试平台。局限性在于当前仅基于种子商店进行转换和6-10个商店的测试，生成流程对极其动态复杂的现代复杂Web架构的泛化能力仍有待更大规模的实证。

title: Wavelet Flow Matching for Multi-Scale Physics Emulation
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026; camera-ready version. Please check the project webpage for links to the source code, pre-trained weights, and datasets: https://gabrieleaccarino.github.io/wavelet_flow_matching/
summary: Accurate emulation of multi-scale physical systems governed by PDEs demands models that remain stable over long autoregressive rollouts while preserving fine-scale structures. Deterministic emulators produce overly smoothed predictions, while generative approaches better capture details but are costly. Latent-space generative models have emerged as a compromise but with the additional cost of separately pre-trained autoencoders. We propose Wavelet Flow Matching (WFM), a generative emulator that overcomes current trade-offs between cost and skill by performing optimal-transport flow matching directly in the multi-scale wavelet space. Rather than learning a latent compression, WFM leverages the hierarchical structure of a U-Net to jointly predict the transport velocities of a prescribed, lossless wavelet representation. On three challenging systems of chaotic fluid dynamics, WFM achieves superior spectral coherence and competitive or better long-horizon accuracy compared to state-of-the-art models. Our results position the wavelet space as an effective training-free representation for generative emulation of complex physical dynamics.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026; camera-ready version. Please check the project webpage for links to the source code, pre-trained weights, and datasets: https://gabrieleaccarino.github.io/wavelet_flow_matching/

AI.title_translation: 用于多尺度物理仿真的小波流匹配
AI.tldr: 提出小波流匹配（WFM），通过在免训练的无损小波空间中直接进行最优传输流匹配，以低成本实现高保真、长周期的多尺度物理动态仿真。
AI.motivation: 现有偏微分方程物理系统仿真中，确定性模型易产生过度平滑的预测，而生成模型计算昂贵，隐空间生成模型又需要额外单独预训练自编码器，难以兼顾长周期模拟稳定性、细微尺度结构保留与计算成本。
AI.method: 提出小波流匹配（WFM），免去学习隐空间压缩的过程，直接在预设的无损多尺度小波空间中执行最优传输流匹配，并利用 U-Net 的层次结构联合预测其传输速度。
AI.result: 在三个具有挑战性的混沌流体动力学系统上，WFM 相比最先进模型实现了更优异的频谱相干性，并在长周期预测精度上达到相当或更好的表现。
AI.conclusion: 小波空间是一种高效且免训练的表示方式，适用于复杂物理动力学系统的生成式仿真建模。
AI.translation: 精确仿真由偏微分方程（PDE）控制的多尺度物理系统，需要模型在长周期自回归推演中保持稳定，同时保留细尺度结构。确定性仿真器会产生过度平滑的预测，而生成式方法虽能更好地捕捉细节但成本昂贵。隐空间生成模型作为一种折衷方案出现，但带来了单独预训练自编码器的额外开销。我们提出了小波流匹配（WFM），这是一种通过直接在多尺度小波空间中执行最优传输流匹配，从而克服现有成本与表现之间权衡的生成式仿真器。WFM 无需学习隐式压缩，而是利用 U-Net 的层次结构来联合预测预设无损小波表示的传输速度。在三个极具挑战性的混沌流体动力学系统上，与最先进的模型相比，WFM 实现了更优的频谱相干性以及有竞争力或更好的长周期精度。我们的结果确立了小波空间作为复杂物理动力学生成式仿真中一种高效的免训练表示。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为小波流匹配（WFM）的生成式仿真方法，直接利用预设的无损多尺度小波空间与 U-Net 架构执行最优传输流匹配，摆脱了对预训练自编码器的依赖，在混沌流体系统上实现了高精度且长周期稳定的多尺度物理仿真。
AI.keywords: 小波变换, 流匹配, 物理仿真, 多尺度系统, 偏微分方程
AI.comments: 该研究创新性地将经典的免训练、无损小波变换与现代最优传输流匹配结合，避免了昂贵的神经自编码器预训练过程，在成本与精细尺度保真度之间取得了良好平衡。其潜在局限性在于主要验证于混沌流体动力学系统，针对非均匀网格或复杂几何边界的适应性仍有待观察。

title: Federated Learning by Utility-Constrained Stochastic Aggregation for Improving Rational Participation
summary: Federated Learning (FL) algorithms implicitly assume that clients passively comply with server-side orchestration, sharing local model updates upon the server's request. However, this overlooks an important aspect of real-world cross-silo environments: clients are often rational agents who may prioritize their own interests, such as local model performance, over that of the global model. In settings with significant statistical heterogeneity, rational clients may opt out of the federation if the perceived benefits of collaboration fail to meet their local utility thresholds. Such attrition degrades global model performance and can lead to the collapse of the federated training process. To avoid such a scenario, in this work, we introduce FedUCA (Federated Learning by Utility-Constrained Stochastic Aggregation for Improving Rational Participation), a non-monetary framework that establishes a non-payment channel through which clients communicate their willingness to participate via their utilities. The server acts as an optimizer, identifying aggregation parameters that satisfy clients' individual rationality (IR) constraints to sustain the global model performance. FedUCA achieves this through a stochastic aggregation mechanism over Dirichlet-sampled mixture strategies, which induces an implicit utility surplus that helps satisfy participation constraints. Supported by theory and extensive experiments, FedUCA's focus on participation feasibility improves client retention and global model performance.

AI.title_translation: 基于效用约束随机聚合提升理性参与的联邦学习
AI.tldr: FedUCA 提出了一种基于效用约束和狄利克雷随机聚合的非货币机制，通过满足理性客户端的参与约束来提升留存率与全局模型性能。
AI.motivation: 现存联邦学习常默认客户端无条件顺从调度，但现实跨孤岛场景中客户端均为理性主体。在强统计异质性下，若参与协作带来的本地效用未达预期阈值，理性客户端会退出联邦，进而导致全局模型性能下降甚至训练崩溃。
AI.method: 提出了非货币框架 FedUCA：构建非支付渠道供客户端通过效用传递参与意愿；服务器作为优化器求解满足客户端个体理性（IR）约束的聚合参数；设计了基于狄利克雷采样混合策略的随机聚合机制，诱导产生隐式效用盈余以满足参与约束。
AI.result: 理论证明与大量实验表明，FedUCA 能够有效提高客户端的留存率，并显著提升全局模型性能。
AI.conclusion: 关注并满足理性客户端的参与可行性（个体理性约束），能有效抑制客户端流失，从而保障并提升联邦学习的全局模型表现。
AI.translation: 联邦学习（FL）算法通常隐含地假设客户端会顺从地配合服务器端的编排，根据服务器的请求共享本地模型更新。然而，这忽略了现实世界跨孤岛（cross-silo）环境中一个重要的方面：客户端通常是理性主体，它们可能优先考虑自身利益（例如本地模型性能），而非全局模型的性能。在存在显著统计异质性的环境中，如果协作所带来的感知收益无法达到其本地效用阈值，理性客户端可能会退出联邦。这种流失会降低全局模型的性能，并可能导致联邦训练过程的崩溃。为了避免这种情况，我们在本工作中提出了 FedUCA（基于效用约束随机聚合以提高理性参与度的联邦学习），这是一个非货币框架，它建立了一个非支付渠道，客户端可以通过该渠道借助其效用来表达其参与意愿。服务器充当优化器，确定满足客户端个体理性（IR）约束的聚合参数，以维持全局模型性能。FedUCA 通过在狄利克雷采样的混合策略上采用随机聚合机制来实现这一点，从而诱导出有助于满足参与约束的隐式效用盈余。在理论和广泛实验的支持下，FedUCA 对参与可行性的关注提高了客户端留存率和全局模型性能。
AI.summary: 针对异质环境下理性客户端易因效用不足而退出联邦学习的问题，本文提出了无需货币激励的 FedUCA 框架。该框架允许客户端通过效用表达参与意愿，并借助基于狄利克雷采样的随机聚合策略创造隐式效用盈余，从而满足客户端的个体理性约束，有效改善了客户端留存并增强了全局模型性能。
AI.keywords: 联邦学习, 理性参与, 效用约束, 随机聚合, 个体理性
AI.comments: 该研究的创新之处在于从机制设计与博弈论角度切入跨孤岛联邦学习中的客户端留存问题，提出了一种无需真实货币激励的非支付调节机制，通过在聚合层面利用狄利克雷采样引入随机混合策略来创造隐式效用盈余，兼顾了个体理性与全局优化。局限在于摘要中未详细说明其计算与通信开销，以及在极端异质分布下的具体理论收敛界。

title: SpecHop: Continuous Speculation for Accelerating Multi-Hop Retrieval Agents
comments: Accepted at the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
summary: Large language models increasingly use external tools such as web search and document retrieval to solve information-intensive tasks. However, multi-hop tool use in complex tasks introduces substantial latency, since the model must repeatedly wait for tool observations before continuing. We study how to accelerate such trajectories without changing the final trajectory the model would have taken without acceleration, assuming access to faster but less reliable speculator tools. We develop a theoretical framework for lossless speculation in multi-hop tool-use settings, characterizing the optimal achievable latency gain. We propose SpecHop, a continuous speculation framework that maintains multiple speculative threads, verifies predicted observations asynchronously as target tool outputs arrive, commits correct branches, and rolls back incorrect ones. This preserves accuracy while reducing wall-clock latency. We show that SpecHop can approach oracle latency gains with enough active threads. Empirically, on retrieval-augmented multi-hop tasks, SpecHop closely matches theoretical predictions and reduces latency by up to 40\% in some settings. Code: https://github.com/mehrdadsaberi/spechop
comment: Accepted at the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

AI.title_translation: SpecHop：加速多跳检索智能体的连续推测框架
AI.tldr: SpecHop 利用快速推测工具进行多线程连续推测与异步验证，在保证输出完全无损的前提下将多跳检索智能体的延迟降低高达 40%。
AI.motivation: 大语言模型在利用外部工具（如网页搜索和文档检索）解决复杂多跳任务时，每次调用都必须等待工具返回观测结果才能继续，这导致了严重的端到端延迟问题。
AI.method: 提出了名为 SpecHop 的连续推测框架：借助快速但不太可靠的推测工具维护多个推测线程；当目标工具的真实输出到达时异步验证预测的观测结果；提交正确的分支并回滚错误的分支，在活跃线程足够时能逼近理论最优（oracle）加速比。
AI.result: 在检索增强的多跳任务上的实证结果与理论预测高度吻合，在某些设置下端到端延迟降低了高达 40%，且在不改变最终轨迹（保持精度无损）的前提下显著缩短了耗时。
AI.conclusion: SpecHop 能够在保证智能体执行轨迹完全无损（即与基线一致）的前提下，通过连续推测与异步验证有效压缩多跳检索过程中的等待延迟，为加速复杂工具调用智能体提供了一种可靠且高效的机制。
AI.translation: 大语言模型越来越多地利用外部工具（如网络搜索和文档检索）来解决信息密集型任务。然而，在复杂任务中多跳使用工具会带来巨大的延迟，因为模型必须在继续之前反复等待工具的观测结果。我们在假设可以使用更快但可靠性较低的推测工具的前提下，研究了如何在不改变模型未加速时原本最终轨迹的情况下加速此类轨迹。我们建立了一个多跳工具使用场景下无损推测的理论框架，刻画了可实现的最优延迟增益。我们提出了 SpecHop，一个连续推测框架，它维护多个推测线程，在目标工具输出到达时异步验证预测的观测结果，提交正确的分支并回滚错误的分支。这在减少实际运行延迟的同时保持了准确性。我们证明，在拥有足够活跃线程的情况下，SpecHop 可以逼近预言机级别的延迟增益。实验表明，在检索增强的多跳任务中，SpecHop 紧密符合理论预测，在某些设置下可降低高达 40% 的延迟。
AI.summary: 本文针对大模型在多跳工具使用中因频繁等待工具返回观测而导致的高延迟问题，提出了 SpecHop 连续推测框架。该方法利用快速推测工具并发探索多条执行路径，并随真实工具输出的到达异步进行验证、提交正确分支及回滚错误分支。在保证模型输出完全无损的前提下，该方法在检索增强的多跳任务中实现了最高达 40% 的延迟降低。
AI.keywords: 多跳检索 (Multi-Hop Retrieval), 智能体 (Agents), 连续推测 (Continuous Speculation), 延迟加速 (Latency Reduction), 工具调用 (Tool Use)
AI.comments: 创新性在于将推测执行（Speculative Execution）机制创造性地拓展至大语言模型多跳工具调用场景，建立了无损推测的理论框架；重要性在于有效缓解了检索增强智能体频繁等待外部工具观测结果的高延迟痛点；局限性在于其最大收益依赖于推测工具的准确度以及并发维护多线程所带来的计算/资源开销。

title: TransitLM: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Map-Free Transit Route Generation
summary: Public transit route planning traditionally depends on structured map infrastructure and complex routing engines, and no existing dataset supports training models to bypass this dependency. We present TransitLM, a large-scale dataset of nearly 13 million transit route planning records from four Chinese cities covering 120,845 stations and 13,666 lines, released as a continual pre-training corpus and benchmark data for three evaluation tasks with complementary metrics. Experiments show that an LLM trained on TransitLM produces structurally valid routes at high accuracy and implicitly grounds arbitrary GPS coordinates to appropriate stations without any explicit mapping. These results demonstrate that transit route planning can be learned entirely from data, enabling end-to-end, map-free route generation directly from origin-destination information. The dataset and benchmark are available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/GD-ML/TransitLM, with evaluation code at https://github.com/HotTricker/TransitLM.

AI.title_translation: TransitLM：用于无地图公共交通路线生成的大规模数据集与基准
AI.tldr: TransitLM 是一个包含近 1300 万条公交路径记录的大规模数据集与基准，验证了 LLM 可脱离传统地图引擎、直接实现端到端的无地图公交路线规划。
AI.motivation: 传统公共交通路线规划高度依赖结构化地图基础设施和复杂的路由引擎，而现有数据集无法支持训练能够摆脱这种依赖的智能模型。
AI.method: 构建并开源了 TransitLM 数据集，包含中国四个城市的近 1300 万条路线规划记录（涵盖 120,845 个站点和 13,666 条线路），作为持续预训练语料库和包含三项评估任务的基准；基于该数据集训练大语言模型以实现路线生成。
AI.result: 在 TransitLM 上训练的 LLM 能以高准确率生成结构有效的路线，并能在没有任何显式映射的情况下，将任意 GPS 坐标隐式关联到相应的站点。
AI.conclusion: 实验证明公共交通路线规划完全可以通过纯数据驱动方式进行学习，从而能够仅依靠起止点信息实现端到端、无需地图的路线生成。
AI.translation: 公共交通路线规划传统上依赖于结构化的地图基础设施和复杂的路由引擎，目前尚无现有数据集支持训练模型以摆脱这一依赖。我们提出了 TransitLM，这是一个包含来自中国四个城市的近 1300 万条公交路线规划记录的大规模数据集，涵盖 120,845 个站点和 13,666 条线路，作为持续预训练语料库和具有互补指标的三项评估任务的基准数据发布。实验表明，在 TransitLM 上训练的大语言模型（LLM）能以高准确率生成结构有效的路线，并在无需任何显式映射的情况下将任意 GPS 坐标隐式对齐到合适的站点。这些结果证明公共交通路线规划完全可以从数据中学习，从而能够直接根据起止点信息实现端到端、无需地图的路线生成。该数据集和基准可在 https://huggingface.co/datasets/GD-ML/TransitLM 获取，评估代码见 https://github.com/HotTricker/TransitLM。
AI.summary: 本论文针对传统公交路径规划依赖地图底图与路由引擎的问题，提出了大规模数据集与基准 TransitLM。基于近 1300 万条规划记录训练的大语言模型展示了无需地图、仅依靠起止点 GPS 坐标即可高精度生成有效公交路线的能力，开辟了纯数据驱动的端到端路径规划新途径。
AI.keywords: 公共交通路线规划, 大规模数据集, 基准测试, 无地图路径生成, 大语言模型
AI.comments: 该研究的创新之处在于跳脱了传统交通路线规划对地图拓扑与路由引擎的强依赖，开创性地探索了利用大语言模型进行端到端、无地图路径生成的可能性；同时发布了千万级大规模数据集和基准，对交通空间智能领域具有重要推动作用。潜在局限在于当前数据仅来源于四个城市，对于未覆盖区域的泛化能力以及实时调度/班次动态的适应性仍有待进一步验证。

title: AMUSE: Anytime Muon with Stable Gradient Evaluation
summary: Modern deep learning commonly relies on AdamW with prescribed learning rate schedules, but recent works challenge both components: Schedule-Free optimization removes explicit schedules via iterate averaging, and Muon improves the update geometry by orthogonalizing momentum for matrix parameters. Despite Muon's strong empirical performance, its underlying mechanism remains partially understood. We study Muon through the river-valley loss landscape, where useful training progress occurs along a flat, low-curvature bulk subspace (the river), while high-curvature dominant directions form steep valley walls that induce oscillations. We empirically show that while Muon's orthogonalization accelerates river progress by increasing the bulk component, it also amplifies dominant-direction noise, causing oscillatory trajectories. Building on this, we propose Anytime MUon with Stable gradient Evaluation (AMUSE), which integrates Muon's rapid bulk progress with the stabilizing effect of Schedule-Free averaging. AMUSE uses a time-varying interpolation coefficient that initially evaluates gradients near the fast Muon sequence for rapid adaptation, then gradually shifts toward the stable averaged sequence to suppress valley-wall oscillations. As a result, AMUSE requires no learning rate schedules and supports anytime training. Across vision tasks and large language model pretraining, AMUSE consistently improves the performance-iteration Pareto frontier over (Schedule-Free) AdamW and Muon.

title: DeltaBox: Millisecond-Scale Sandbox Checkpoint and Rollback for Stateful AI Agents
comments: 16 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables. Accepted to SIGOPS ATC 2026
summary: Emerging LLM-powered AI agent workloads, such as test-time tree search and reinforcement learning (RL), require high-frequency state exploration, relying on rapid checkpoint/restore (C/R) of the complete sandbox state, including files and process state. Existing mechanisms duplicate the entire state, causing hundreds of milliseconds to seconds of latency per C/R, which severely bottlenecks deep search and large-scale fan-outs. We observe that consecutive sandbox states between checkpoints differ only marginally. Therefore, instead of full duplication, a sandbox should only duplicate the changes between consecutive checkpoints (Key Insight), yet the lack of OS support makes this hard to realize. We propose a new OS-level abstraction, DeltaState, that delivers change-based C/R for agents through co-designed OS mechanisms. First, DeltaFS checkpoints file state by freezing the writable layer and inserting a new one, turning updates into copy-on-write and rollback into a layer switch. Second, DeltaCR quickly restores process state by forking from a frozen template process. A coordinator pairs the two so each checkpoint is one consistent (filesystem, memory) state. Building on these mechanisms, we present DeltaBox, an agent sandbox with millisecond-level C/R. On SWE-bench, DeltaBox hides its checkpoint work (10.83 ms) under inference and rolls back in a mean 1.86 ms, with the same warm-template fork driving low-cost RL rollout fan-out. DeltaBox is open-sourced at https://github.com/delta-box.

title: SA-RAG: Structuring Noisy Conversations for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been widely adopted in conversational applications. However, their reliance on parametric knowledge limits reliability in real-world scenarios that require dynamic or domain-specific information. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses this limitation by incorporating external knowledge during generation, but existing RAG methods often struggle with noisy or irrelevant contexts, as they typically assume that high-quality structures are already available. In this work, we propose Structure-aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation (SA-RAG), a principled structure induction and generation framework that constructs reliable intermediate structures directly from noisy conversational data. SA-RAG uses tables as compact and controllable structured representations. We introduce a quality-aware structure induction framework that jointly models semantic and structural consistency. Furthermore, we explore both training-free and training-based structure generation strategies to further improve structure quality while maintaining fidelity. Experiments on two noisy real-world datasets show that SA-RAG significantly outperforms existing RAG baselines. Further analysis highlights that high-quality structural representations are crucial for robust RAG applications.

title: From Facts to Insights: A Persona-Driven Dual Memory Framework and Dataset for Role-Playing Agents
summary: While role-playing agents excel in short-term interactions, long-term conversations overwhelm context windows, motivating external memory frameworks. Current systems typically rely on persona-agnostic summarization, which records facts without persona-specific interpretation, yielding generic responses that compromise persona fidelity. To bridge this gap, we introduce RoleMemo, a dataset featuring four reasoning tasks where the factual fragments must be interpreted through the persona to reach the correct answer. Evaluation on RoleMemo exposes critical limitations of persona-agnostic frameworks. We thus propose DualMem, which decouples memory into two streams: factual cognition and persona-conditioned insight. Trained through Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL), our framework with a 4B-parameter model outperforms zero-shot persona-agnostic frameworks powered by DeepSeek-V3.2 for sustained persona fidelity. Our resources are available at https://github.com/Collab-Gen/RoleMemo.

title: Certified Policy Optimisation for Nested Causal Bandits via PAC-Bayes Risk
summary: Critical sequential decisions are rarely single-timescale: a strategic decision causally shapes the context in which every subsequent tactical choice is made; standard bandit and reinforcement-learning theory does not capture this causal coupling between timescales. We formalise the problem class as Nested Contextual Causal Bandits (NCCBs), a hierarchical SCM where each level's action sets the next level's context distribution, and propose Nested Causal Thompson Sampling (NCTS), which draws one mechanism-factorised belief per episode and acts recursively under it. Our main theoretical result is a causal PAC-Bayesian excess-risk bound that certifies any candidate deployment policy from historic data alone, off-policy and anytime, answering the deployment question: can we trust this agent here, and at what risk? Experiments on a hierarchical SCM show that, against a matched RFF-GP joint regression on the same function class, the factorised SCM-mechanism posterior transfers significantly better zero-shot under exogenous distribution shifts, the recursive meta-to-inner commit significantly dominates the joint-commit alternative in distribution, and the certificate significantly contracts as offline data accumulates. Combining these results, we establish progressive certified handover, a safe-deployment method: each timescale flips from a legacy controller to NCTS when gains can be certified, independently of the others.

title: Listing Even Cycles Faster than the Submodular-Width Barrier
comments: 19 pages. Accepted to PODS 2027. To appear in Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data (PACMMOD), Vol. 4, No. 5 (PODS), Article 305, November 2026
summary:
A classic result of Alon, Yuster, and Zwick (AYZ, Algorithmica 1997) shows that all $2k$-cycles in an $m$-edge graph can be listed in $\tilde O(m^{2-1/k}+t)$ time, where $t$ is the output size. This bound underlies the {\em submodular width} of Marx (JACM 2013) and the PANDA framework of Abo Khamis, Ngo, and Suciu (PODS 2017), which extend AYZ to arbitrary conjunctive queries with degree constraints. A central open question is whether combinatorial algorithms can beat the submodular-width barrier.
  Bringmann and Gorbachev (STOC 2025) gave lower-bound evidence that submodular width may be optimal for general conjunctive queries under combinatorial algorithms. The picture changes for $2k$-cycles on undirected graphs, whose queries have self-joins and symmetric EDBs: recent works improve on AYZ for even-cycle detection and listing. Pinning down the complexity of $C_{2k}$-detection and listing is thus a natural step toward overcoming the submodular-width barrier for such queries.
  For detection, Dahlgaard, Knudsen, and St{ö}ckel (STOC 2017) solved $C_{2k}$-detection in $\tilde O(m^{2k/(k+1)})$ time. Listing is harder. Jin and Xu (STOC 2023), and independently Abboud, Khoury, Leibowitz, and Safier (FSTTCS 2023), listed 4-cycles in $\tilde O(m^{4/3}+t)$ time; Vassilevska~Williams and Westover (ITCS 2025) listed 6-cycles in $\tilde O(m^{8/5}+t)$ time, improving the AYZ bounds of $\tilde O(m^{3/2})$ and $\tilde O(m^{5/3})$. The general case has remained open for 30 years.
  Building on these works, we list $2k$-cycles in $\tilde O(m^{(2k^2-k+1)/(k^2+1)}+t)$ time, improving AYZ for every $k\geq 3$. The key ingredient is an \emph{asymmetric supersaturation} result for even cycles. Our algorithms use only join and project operators over multiple tree-decomposition plans, making them naturally implementable in database systems, in contrast to prior BFS-based graph approaches.

title: Evidence-Guided Neural Architecture Selection under Uncertainty for Subject-Specific Blood Glucose Forecasting
summary: Reliable neural architecture selection is an open challenge in time-series forecasting under limited, noisy, and heterogeneous data, where standard heuristic architecture design and validation approaches fail to ensure accurate and reliable prediction and generalization. We propose EVIDENT (EVidence-based IDEntification of Neural archiTectures), a framework for architecture selection that integrates Bayesian training, evidence-based ranking, and task-specific validation under uncertainty. The framework explores the candidate architecture pool and identifies the lowest-capacity model that satisfies a prescribed validation criterion. We demonstrate this method using temporal convolutional networks (TCNs) for individualized blood glucose forecasting in type 1 diabetes patients. The results show that EVIDENT systematically rejects both under- and over-parameterized TCN architectures on population-level diabetes data, while identifying models that generalize reliably to unseen patients. When multiple architectures are competitive, the framework further supports plausibility-weighted ensemble predictions that enhance predictive performance. Compared with a random-search baseline, EVIDENT identified smaller architectures with more consistent forecasting performance on unseen patients. These findings establish EVIDENT as a strategy to neural architecture discovery, enabling reliable model selection for high-consequence forecasting in data-limited and heterogeneous settings.

title: Generative Molecular Morphing for Flexible-Size Design via Unbalanced Optimal Transport
summary: The success of generative molecular design depends on a model's steerability toward high-reward samples. Because many molecular properties are intrinsically linked to molecular size, accurately capturing the joint distribution of properties and the number of atoms is essential. However, current diffusion and flow-based models fix the number of atoms, which ultimately limits their ability to navigate this complex relationship. To address this, we introduce Morph, a flexible-size generative model for conditional and unconditional 3D molecular design based on geometric graphs. By dynamically adapting size, Morph can seamlessly integrate existing structural priors, like scaffolds, and significantly enhances property steering. We show that Morph matches current fixed-size state-of-the-art models while significantly increasing sampling flexibility. We demonstrate out-of-distribution generation in regimes where previous models fail, paving the way for enhanced generative modeling for molecular design.

title: Larch: Learned Query Optimization for Semantic Predicates
summary: With the advent of Large Language Models (LLMs), many database systems introduced semantic operators that enabled analytical queries over unstructured data (e.g. text, images, videos). Semantic operators typically incur high inference costs and latencies making semantic (AI) SQL queries challenging to apply on large scale datasets. At the same time, their semantic nature leads database engines to treat them as black boxes, making AISQL queries difficult to optimize. In this paper, we introduce Larch, a framework for optimizing the execution of semantic filters in AI SQL queries. Larch was inspired by two key observations: i) the high latency of semantic operators leaves significant room for computationally-heavy runtime optimization techniques, ii) unstructured data are typically accompanied by semantic information in the form of embeddings allowing for efficient semantic comparisons between AI_FILTER prompts and data values. Based on these two key observations, we present two Larch variants: Larch-A2C and Larch-Sel. Larch-A2C encodes arbitrary semantic filters expression tree using an embedding-augmented Gated Graph Neural Network and formulates the filter evaluation order as a Markov decision process. In contrast, Larch-Sel leverages a supervised learning model to predict filter selectivities, subsequently applying dynamic programming to find a near-optimal evaluation order for each input row. Evaluated across diverse real-world datasets and comprehensive synthetic workloads, both Larch variants always outperform existing semantic filter optimization techniques in terms of token usage on every dataset and workload. Our results demonstrate that Larch is robust across diverse workloads across text and image modalities, 6%--30% lower total token costs and 3x--19x lower token costs overhead than Palimpzest and Quest.

title: Express Language Modeling
summary: We introduce a new tool, Express, for converting a non-causal attention approximation into a causal approximation with matching approximation guarantees. When combined with the state-of-the-art Thinformer approximation, Express improves upon the best known causal attention guarantees, delivering $\log^{3/2}(n)/s$ approximation error with only $O(s)$ memory and $O(s^2 \log^2(n))$ compression overhead for a sequence of length $n$. We pair these developments with an efficient I/O-aware Triton implementation, demonstrate substantial speedups over FlashAttention 2, and use Express to overcome four resource bottlenecks in the language modeling pipeline: long-context prefill, KV cache compression, long-form memory-constrained decoding, and long-form compute-constrained decoding.

title: A Horizon-Specific Attribute-Conditioned Neural Network for Estimating Health-State Transition Probabilities in Irregular Longitudinal Data: The LANTERN Framework
summary: Accurate estimation of health-state transition probabilities is essential for long-term care insurance modeling. Conventional actuarial multi-state models provide an interpretable framework but may be restrictive in capturing nonlinear relationships and accumulated health histories from irregular longitudinal observations. This paper proposes LANTERN, a history-dependent neural framework that integrates recurrent health representations, elapsed observation time, and adaptive demographic and socioeconomic attribute conditioning to estimate horizon-specific transition probabilities among Healthy, Mild disability, Severe disability, and Death states. Using longitudinal Health and Retirement Study data, we evaluate our model against a recurrent neural network, multinomial logistic regression, gradient-boosted trees, and an actuarial continuous-time Markov chain across one-, two-, and three-year forecast horizons. At the primary two-year horizon, LANTERN achieves competitive predictive accuracy and calibration, with improvements over selected benchmarks. Its aggregated transition-matrix estimates outperform multinomial logistic regression and are comparable to those of the strongest remaining benchmarks. These findings suggest that history-conditioned neural estimation provides a flexible and competitive approach to estimating horizon-specific health-state transition probabilities, with potential applications in actuarial long-term care modeling.

title: EdgeZSAD: Value-Range Quantization for Deploying Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection on Edge Neural Processing Units
comments: 22 pages. Substantially revised version with a focus on Value-Range Quantization and native edge deployment evaluation
summary: Quantizing zero-shot industrial anomaly detectors for edge neural processing units can degrade defect detection and localization. We present EdgeZSAD (Edge Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection), a deployment framework whose methodological contribution is Value-Range Quantization (VRQ). We diagnose how attention Value tensors inherit overly wide ranges from fused query-key-value projections and assign independent ranges calibrated on source data, without retraining or changing quantized weights. The engineering application is native deployment of a foundation-model detector for industrial inspection, evaluated on three public benchmarks and Qualcomm edge devices. Under minimum-maximum and mean-squared-error calibration, VRQ improves image-level discrimination and per-region overlap. In the primary calibration set, it recovers 90-98% of the loss in combined image and pixel discrimination relative to half precision, with a small increase in latency over baseline quantization. Matched tensor overrides reproduce the recovery without adding graph nodes, identifying independent Value-range assignment as the effective intervention in the evaluated runtime family.

title: Robots that Collaborate: Sequential Asymmetric Imitation for Learning Coupled Robot Policies
summary: Collaborative mobile manipulation requires robots to coordinate with a partially observed partner while physically interacting through shared objects. This is difficult because failures often arise not from poor local skills, but from mistimed waiting, yielding, pulling, releasing, or repositioning. We study this problem with two bimanual mobile manipulators coupled through rigid and deformable objects. We propose Sequential Asymmetric Imitation (SAI), a single-teleoperator curriculum for learning coupled multi-robot behaviors without synchronized dual-operator demonstrations or explicit inter-robot communication. SAI trains Robot A from unilateral demonstrations with a compliant human partner, trains Robot B against the deployed Robot A policy, and then refines Robot A using sparse interventions near coordination failures. This staged process exposes the policies to increasingly realistic partner behaviors, including delay, phase mismatch,insufficient yielding, and interaction conflict. Across real-world dual-robot manipulation tasks, SAI improves task success, phase synchronization, and partner-contingent yielding over independent imitation and curriculum-ablation baselines. These results suggest that physically coupled collaboration can be learned through the structure of the imitation curriculum, rather than through synchronized multi-operator demonstrations or explicit coordination mechanisms. More videos on project page:http://cyc0429.github.io/sai-project-page/

title: CoffeeBench: Benchmarking Long-Horizon LLM Agents in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Economies
comments: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations and Datasets Track)
summary: LLM agents are increasingly capable of handling complex, long-horizon tasks and may eventually take on business management, a role traditionally performed by humans. Deploying them safely requires monitoring their capabilities and behavior in environments that reflect real economies. We introduce CoffeeBench, a benchmark built on a compact simulation of a coffee supply chain with realistic business mechanics. Six autonomous LLM coding agents run its farmers, roasters, and retailers, and negotiate and trade with one another to maximize their own net income over 90 simulated days. We evaluate eight recent proprietary and open-weight models by letting each run one roaster while a fixed background model runs the other five firms, and scoring that roaster's net income. Claude Sonnet 5.5 earns the highest net income, closely followed by GPT-6 Astra. The leaders sell at higher prices, and the best model also buys its inputs far more cheaply, whereas weaker models trade at thin margins. Since performance targets are a common cause of accounting fraud in human firms, we also test whether agents under KPI pressure inflate their numbers. Under a revenue target, circular trades occur for some pairs of models: one agent proposes that the two rival firms sell goods back and forth at inflated prices so that both book revenue, and the rival accepts. We hope CoffeeBench serves as an early step toward a future in which LLM agents manage firms without misconduct. We release our code and agent trajectories.
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations and Datasets Track)

title: Long-Distance Real-World Navigation of the Legged-Wheeled Robot Go2-W Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
summary: Legged-wheeled robots have been extensively studied for their potential to combine the efficient flat-ground mobility of wheels with the rough-terrain adaptability of legs. However, their application to long-distance autonomous navigation in real environments remains limited. This paper reports our efforts to build a deep reinforcement learning-based locomotion controller and an autonomous navigation system for the commercially available Go2-W legged-wheeled robot. The study focuses on the integrated system and the practical challenges associated with its sustained operation over long distances in real-world environments. For locomotion control, we extended our proprioception-only policy, previously developed for quadruped robots, to Go2-W, a 16-degree-of-freedom legged-wheeled robot. We additionally found that wheeled locomotion concentrates the load on the hip joints, resulting in heat concentration that hinders sustained travel. To address this issue, we developed a policy with periodic foot-lifting motion that distributes the joint loads and mitigates heat concentration. We evaluated the integrated system at the Tsukuba Challenge 2025. The robot autonomously traversed an approximately \SI{2.8}{\kilo\meter} route that included sidewalks, a park, and stairs without stopping owing to overheating.

title: Importance Sampling for Event Discovery via Guesswork
comments: Short version submitted to ITW 2026. This is a longer version after being accepted to ITW, correcting reviewers comments, organizing and rephrasing, and adding more complete proofs, comments, etc
summary:
Traditional importance sampling (IS) is designed to estimate rare-event probabilities by minimizing estimator variance. However, many applications prioritize rapid discovery: the generation of a trajectory within a rare set $A_n$. This requires a shift from ensemble-based estimation to a design principle focused on the hitting time $τ_{A_n} := \inf\{t \ge 1 : Y_t^n \in A_n\}$.
  We formalize a Quality of Discovery problem as the problem of minimizing the description length (surprisal) of the discovered trajectory under the nominal model $p$. We prove that minimizing this description length is equivalent to minimizing the nominal rank exponent $J_{\mathrm{rank}}(q_n) := \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n} \log G_n(Y^n)$, where $G_n(x^n)$ is the guesswork of sequence $x^n$. For i.i.d.\ models and type-defined rare sets $Γ$, we show that while classical IS targets the mass-dominating type $Q_{\mathrm{IS}}^* \in \arg\min_{Q \in Γ} D(Q\|p)$, discovery optimality is achieved by $Q_{\mathrm{GW}}^* \in \arg\min_{Q \in Γ} [H(Q) + D(Q\|p)]$. This framework identifies a fundamental rule: minimizing the guesswork exponent ensures the discovered sequence is the "least surprising" representative of the set relative to the nominal model's search order. We further demonstrate that under budgetary constraints, this exponent serves as a lexicographic tie-breaker when the hitting-time minimizer is not unique. This establishes $H(Q) + D(Q\|p)$ as a natural objective for discovery-based importance sampling, providing a formal bridge between randomized sampling and systematic search.

title: MMAO: A Metabolic Multi-Agent Optimizer with Endogenous Resource Allocation for Continuous and Discrete Optimization
summary: Traditional meta-heuristics often rely on fixed population sizes, manually chosen search scales, and externally attached parameter-control modules. This paper presents the Metabolic Multi-Agent Optimizer (MMAO), a cross-domain optimization framework in which adaptation is derived endogenously from a private-public metabolic resource loop. Each agent carries internal energy, a continuous role state, motion or structural memory, and local search history, while the population shares a communal resource pool. Fitness improvements are converted into normalized metabolic gains through a robust progress scale and a recent success statistic; the same closed loop then regulates sensing intensity, search amplitude, role drift, branching, pruning, respawning, and elite reinvestment. In the continuous setting, MMAO uses energy-regulated symmetric zero-order probing and role-interpolated motion. In the discrete setting, the same control law is instantiated through structural sensing, local route improvement, guided perturbation, and energy-weighted edge reuse. The paper combines an implementation-faithful formulation with a reproducible experimental study on a CEC2017 subset (10D/30D, 20 seeds) and five TSPLIB instances (100 discrete runs in total). The current evidence supports MMAO primarily as a parameter-light, self-calibrating optimization framework whose main validated originality lies in metabolically endogenous resource allocation across heterogeneous search behaviors, rather than as a universally superior optimizer.

title: Disentangling Continuous-Time Latent Dynamics: Identifiability of Latent SDEs via Diffusion Shifts
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (camera-ready version). 53 pages, 15 figures
summary: Causal representation learning for time series has developed strong identifiability results in discrete-time latent causal models, but identifiability in continuous-time latent stochastic differential equation (SDE) models remains largely open. We address this gap using environment-induced shifts in diffusion covariance. We study additive-noise latent SDEs observed through an unknown nonlinear diffeomorphism, with shared drift but environment-specific diffusion covariance. We show that two diagonal diffusion regimes with pairwise distinct coordinate-wise variance ratios identify the latent coordinates up to permutation, coordinate-wise scaling, and a possible constant shift, without any sparsity assumption on the drift. We first prove this result for linear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck systems and then extend it to general additive-noise latent SDEs. Under mild smoothness, the instantaneous drift-Jacobian causal graph is identifiable up to the same permutation. We propose a two-stage estimator for latent disentanglement and optional graph recovery; experiments on synthetic systems confirm the predicted identifiability boundary, and an application to Hardanger Bridge monitoring data illustrates the approach on real sensor trajectories.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (camera-ready version). 53 pages, 15 figures

title: Agent Security Meets Regulatory Reality -- A Practitioner Systematization of Autonomous-Agent Threats and Controls in Regulated Financial Systems
comments: Substantially revised and expanded version. Added five reference algorithms, a formal execution model, theorem and proofs, security and performance analysis, and an open-source reference implementation. Expanded authorship to reflect substantial contributions from two additional coauthors
summary: Large language model agents are entering regulated financial systems, yet research on their attack surface remains predominantly laboratory-based, and practitioner guidance is neither peer-reviewed nor connected to a formal threat model. Using production evidence, we map six agentic threat categories, namely prompt injection, identity and authorization, action auditability, tool abuse, data residency, and boundary policy enforcement, to the specific control obligations imposed by US and EU financial regulation (ECOA and Regulation B, EU AI Act, GDPR Article 22, and FINRA's 2026 agent guidance), showing how legal accountability increases their operational significance. We distill these obligations into five runtime control invariants with reference algorithms that enforce them at auditable architectural boundaries. We develop a formal model expressing each invariant as a predicate over a case-bound event chain and prove the audit reconstruction gate is sound and complete with respect to these invariants: compliance is decidable from the case identifier alone. We show that two of the invariants constrain audit cost and throughput rather than constituting pure operational overhead. We document four architectural patterns from a production Know Your Customer (KYC) deployment for a consumer credit product that reduced multi-day manual processing to same-day automated resolution for approximately four in five cases. Finally, we report three negative results, two identified through internal audit or production observation rather than adversarial testing. We conclude that securing agents in regulated environments depends less on novel attack classes than on rendering auditability, least-privilege authorization, and boundary policy enforcement, with verifiable compliance and bounded audit cost at scale.
