title: Mean Square Error Analysis of Stochastic Runge-Kutta Integrators
summary: We analyze the mean square error of stochastic Runge--Kutta integrators for overdamped Langevin dynamics whose potential is strongly convex outside a bounded region. A decomposition splits the local error into a mean-zero term and a smaller remainder, and the discrete Poisson equation turns their moments into a bound on the error of a time average. We carry this out for two stochastic Runge--Kutta integrators proposed by Yang \& Wang (2026), both of strong order $\frac32$ and weak order $2$, which evaluate the gradient of the potential and no higher derivative. We show that their laws approach the law of the exact solution at second order in Wasserstein-1 distance, up to a logarithm, uniformly in the number of steps. For a test function with bounded derivatives up to third order, we prove that the mean square error over $N$ steps with step size $h$ is $\mathcal O ( \frac{1}{Nh} + h^4 )$, which is the optimal order in the discretization. Experiments measure the strong and weak orders and the sampling bias on a nonconvex potential in $\mathbb R^2$, and compare the integrators on a diffusion model of CIFAR-10.

title: Reproducibility in the Age of Agentic AI: Context Engineering at the Timescale of a Codebase
summary: Reproducible research practices are context engineering for AI coding agents. I argue that agents lower the cost of maintaining tests, commit histories, repository structure, instructions, and decision records while making their benefits immediate. Researchers remain responsible for verifying these artifacts and the scientific judgments they encode.

title: Cloud-Edge LLM Collaborative Learning via Accelerating Personalized Bilevel Optimization
comments: We have fixed all issues, and submitted to IEEE TPAMI
summary: Amid the rapid advancement of physical-world intelligence, cloud-edge collaborative large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a promising roadmap for practical LLM deployment. However, existing cloud-edge paradigms struggle to balance global consensus with local personalization, which fails to satisfy the need for a unified knowledge foundation on the cloud and domain-specific adaptation at the edge. To address this, we propose a personalized bilevel optimization framework that formalizes cloud-edge LLM collaboration as a dual structure: the upper level optimizes edge-side personalization, while the lower level governs cloud-side knowledge transfer, reaching cloud-edge evolving in coordination. We then propose CIDERS: while the cloud performs knowledge transfer to the learnable backbone, the key lies in embedding global trajectories into each local personalization step via consensus-variate correction to reconcile personalization with consensus. We provide a comprehensive theoretical analysis, including a geometric characterization of the local trajectory and a full convergence guarantee, revealing an explicit trade-off structure between personalization and global convergence. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen2-1.5B show CIDERS high performance and can significantly improve the accuracy (as much as 200\%+). Control-state diagnostics further show strong preservation of the local orthogonal component, while a separate cross-domain evaluation finds only a small matched-domain response advantage.
comment: We have fixed all issues, and submitted to IEEE TPAMI

title: Beyond Embedding Transfer: Architectural Interfaces, Iso-Parameter Scaling, and Preconditioner-Governed Consolidation in Grokking
summary: Grokking, or delayed generalization after memorization, incurs substantial training steps across algebraic tasks. Cross-operator transfer from a grokked donor accelerates target acquisition, yet post-grokking AdamW continuation triggers test-accuracy relapse as unannealed updates drift across residual interfaces and decaying second moments amplify late gradients. Across depths one to three on modular arithmetic ($\mathbb{Z}_{113}$), non-Abelian $S_5$ conjugation, and real-sensory MNIST modular arithmetic, we separate representational transfer from preconditioner-governed consolidation across thirteen experimental batteries. First, co-transferring internal blocks accelerates one-layer and two-layer modular takeoff beyond boundary interfaces, while graded prefix pinning bounds depth-three drift under unannealed continuation. Second, an iso-parameter $S_5$ scaling grid separates attention head dimension from MLP width: widening two-head attention to dimension $64$ reaches $98.54\%$ cold accuracy at $427\mathrm{k}$ parameters and $85.95\%$ boundary-only transfer, while final-slot representations refine conjugation directly across blocks without an intermediate binary-product bottleneck. Third, Plateau-Gated Leaky Consolidation pairs validation-envelope step damping with leaky second-moment decay, reaching $84.85\%$ zero-leakage validation-gated risk-constrained accuracy across five pre-saturation two-layer $S_5$ suites while cutting step budget relative to hard anchoring. Fourth, transferring a grokked visual trunk and blocks to image-disjoint MNIST targets reaches $92.27\%$ and $90.76\%$ accuracy, prunes odd centroid harmonics, and reaches $90.42\%$ risk-constrained accuracy across $60/60$ branches without hyperparameter retuning.

title: ResGraph: Cross-Model Graph-based Index Migration via Residual Reachability in ANN Search
summary: Approximate nearest neighbor search (ANNS) underpins large-scale vector retrieval in search, recommendation, and retrieval-augmented generation. Graph-based indexes have demonstrated state-of-the-art search performance for ANNS: they connect each corpus vector to a small set of nearby or navigationally useful vertices and answer queries by traversing the resulting graph. Because these edges are selected using construction-time distances, the graph index is tied to the embedding model; re-encoding a corpus with a new model may change distances and neighborhoods of the vectors, and reconstructing the graph for the new embedding vectors incurs substantial construction cost and delays deployment. When the embedding model changes, we observe a phenomenon in the old graph index that we call residual reachability: although derived from different models, the vectors describe the same underlying objects and often retain part of their similarity structure, which the old graph reflects as connectivity, leaving many exact new-model neighbors reachable within a few hops. Motivated by this observation, we develop ResGraph, an index-migration framework that exploits the residual reachability of the old graph index to construct the new graph index faster. ResGraph provides two migration paths. Res-Local performs parallel shallow expansion over the inherited graph index and screens second-hop candidates with packed position sign codes before exact evaluation. Res-Search uses hop-bounded beam traversal to explore beyond shallow expansion. Across eight text and image migrations, ResGraph attains up to 17.43 times speedup on constructing the new graph index than the fastest degree-matched reconstruction method while keeping competitive recalls.

title: Contract-Based Decomposition of Temporal Logic Specifications for Networked Systems under Arbitrary Partitions
summary: Computational complexity is an inherent limitation of formal synthesis for networked systems, and decomposing the global specification into local ones relaxes this limitation at the cost of conservatism. Since the granularity of the partition governs this trade-off, it is reasonable to treat the partition as a design variable, which calls for local specifications that remain correct for every partition. To this end, this paper gives each agent a local specification, written as an assume-guarantee contract that the agent can establish from local information. We first derive a necessary and sufficient condition for these contracts to decompose the global specification under a given partition. Building on this, we then present a condition under which the decomposition is correct for every partition, so that the partition becomes a free design variable. For linear dynamics and signal temporal logic formulas with affine predicates, we further synthesize a controller for each coalition by a tube-based approach. Finally, simulations on a network of input-coupled tanks show how the choice of partition trades computational cost against conservatism.

title: Hidden not Deleted: How Networks Suppress Entangled Features
summary: When a neural network stops reporting a feature, has it forgotten the feature or merely hidden it? Shared representations complicate the answer: removing one feature's direction can also damage another feature. We study this problem in a small autoencoder that compresses and reconstructs inputs, allowing individual feature contributions to be traced directly. With the representation fixed, restoring a single bias partially recovers target detection by exposing a signal hidden behind the output's activation threshold. Tests on target-absent inputs distinguish this recovery from interventions that simply increase output. The same bias intervention becomes less effective when the representation is allowed to change. We find that training only the other outputs can weaken the target's contribution, even without a loss on its own output. A conditional theoretical analysis explains how interference with retained predictions creates this pressure. Yet more flexible predictors still detect residual target information. These findings show how recovery depends on feature geometry and on which parameters are trained, and why a silent output is insufficient evidence of forgetting.

title: UltraBench 2: Towards Robust Evaluation of Vision Foundation Models on Ultrasound
comments: Accepted to Proceedings of the 6th Machine Learning for Health Symposium (ML4H 2026), PMLR Volume 346
summary: Benchmarking is an increasingly critical part of research in machine learning and the domains where it is applied, including healthcare. Yet, despite the steady development of new ultrasound foundation models in recent years, the development of well-designed benchmarks to evaluate them has lagged behind. This deficiency has led to fragmented and inconsistent evaluations of competing models, making it difficult to measure progress. To address this issue, we introduce UltraBench 2, a comprehensive benchmark with wide anatomical and task coverage, and a focus on standardization, reproducibility, and ease-of-use. Using this benchmark, we compare existing vision foundation models for ultrasound image analysis. Our analyses demonstrate that ultrasound-specific pretraining still leads on classification, but that state-of-the-art general-purpose models have drawn level on segmentation.
comment: Accepted to Proceedings of the 6th Machine Learning for Health Symposium (ML4H 2026), PMLR Volume 346

title: The Alignment Illusion in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Layer-wise visual-text similarity in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) is widely interpreted as evidence that the language model progressively integrates visual content into a shared representation space. This reading rests on the assumption that scalar alignment scores reflect content-level cross-modal interaction. To test this assumption, we apply controlled interventions to the visual stream. Across 13 MLLMs from five families spanning 0.5B to 72B parameters, replacing projector-output visual tokens with Gaussian noise sharply reduces task accuracy, yet four standard scalar measures (CKA, SVCCA, MIR, and the leading principal-angle cosine) fail to consistently separate the corrupted stream from the original. We call this failure the alignment illusion and trace it to the shared language-model pathway: anisotropic MLP down-projections pull visual and text tokens toward common output directions, producing weight-induced alignment. We introduce the principal-angle gap (PA gap), defined as the difference between the top two principal-angle cosines, to distinguish leading-direction dominance from the broader overlap observed with structured visual content. Under graded visual corruption, the PA gap tracks task accuracy more consistently than the scalar scores we consider; under a structured but irrelevant image, it further exposes regimes in which internal geometry and task accuracy come apart. Internal visual-text alignment in MLLMs is therefore best read as a geometric diagnostic of the visual stream inside the language model rather than a direct proxy for content-level cross-modal interaction, and is most informative when calibrated by controlled task evidence.

title: ReCo: When to Relocate Sensor Kits under Deployment Constraints -- A NILM Case Study
comments: 9 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables. Accepted at the CONSTRAINT Workshop at IEEE BigData 2026. Updated manuscript and author affiliation
summary: Many sensing tasks obtain training labels only by deploying instruments in the field. With a limited number of sensor kits, a collection deadline, and measurement downtime at every move, the collector must repeatedly decide whether to stay at the current site or relocate. We study this decision in non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM), which estimates the power drawn by individual appliances from a home's main meter and is trained on data from homes temporarily fitted with appliance-level sub-meters. In NILM, appliance usage varies with the appliance, season and climate, and the value of new data depends on how diverse the combinations of target operation and background load are. To address this, we propose a constraint-based relocation framework and instantiate it for NILM as ReCo (Relocation by Coverage gain). ReCo counts new operating regimes in a joint target--background feature space, forecasts each home's future gain from the data collected so far, and each night weighs the gain of staying against the gain of moving elsewhere after the downtime. In replayed deployments on the Plegma dataset under two kit counts and two downtime costs, ReCo outperforms fixed-dwell and count-based schedules and a threshold rule using the same metric in every setting. Its advantage is not explained by collecting more days alone and is consistent with allocating the days to more valuable homes and periods.
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables. Accepted at the CONSTRAINT Workshop at IEEE BigData 2026. Updated manuscript and author affiliation

title: From Data to Program: Fast & Direct Generative Program Inference from Empirical Data
summary: Estimating probability densities from a finite set of samples typically requires dataset-specific model fitting. We introduce PRODiGI, a pretrained data-to-program model that infers an explicit, executable generative program in a single forward pass. Pretrained on synthetic datasets paired with their ground-truth programs, PRODiGI accommodates diverse generative families and data dimensionalities through template prediction and non-autoregressive program parameter decoding. Its inferred programs support direct sampling, density and score evaluation, and inspection independently of the pretrained model. We further introduce program-space fine-tuning, which refines differentiable program parameters by maximizing the likelihood of empirical data while keeping model parameters intact. Experiments show that PRODiGI-FT achieves better density and score metrics than existing pretrained models, while offering multi-fold speedups over its closest competitors. Program-space fine-tuning further reduces generation MMD by 90%. By turning empirical data into explicit, reusable programs, PRODiGI introduces a new direction for fast, interpretable tabular generative modeling.

title: Mind the RefGAP: Correcting Reference Attention in Diffusion-Based Visual Editing
summary: Reference-guided diffusion editors struggle to faithfully reproduce user-provided references. We observe that many diffusion editors allocate limited attention to the reference. For example, in LoomVideo, edit-region queries assign less than 1% of their attention mass to the reference. We introduce RefGAP, a training-free correction that determines logit-offset magnitudes online at each layer from the reference-attention mass measured during the forward pass. Positive offsets to reference logits strengthen reference usage by edit-region queries, while negative offsets for keep-region queries limit reference-induced changes outside the edit. Two global coefficients control the correction; they are selected once on validation data from four development diffusion editors and held fixed. Across seven diffusion-based image/video editors, RefGAP improves identity fidelity in head swapping and face swapping, where identity takes priority; on some editors this raises pose error, which delaying the correction reduces. RefGAP achieves a fidelity-preservation trade-off comparable to separately tuned constant edit-side biases, without per-approach strength sweeps. Additional experiments on virtual try-on and background replacement evaluate transfer beyond identity editing.

title: MeanFlowAdvantage: Stable Reward Fine-Tuning for Few-Step Average-Velocity Generators
summary: MeanFlow enables efficient few-step generation by predicting interval-average velocities, but this representation creates a mismatch for reward fine-tuning: existing advantage-based objectives are typically defined on instantaneous velocities or equivalent $x_0$-space predictions, whereas inference directly uses the learned average-velocity map. We introduce MeanFlowAdvantage, a signed advantage-weighted least-squares objective for average-velocity generators. Our key construction uses a shared, detached MeanFlow derivative correction to express the reward objective in prediction space while making rollout and reference regularization exact penalties on the average-velocity network deployed at inference. The resulting formulation preserves MeanFlow's native few-step sampler and provides a direct mechanism for transferring reward improvements to the deployed flow map. On SD3.5-Medium, MeanFlowAdvantage improves all eight reported metrics over the matched four-step MeanFlowNFT baseline and, with only four NFEs, matches or exceeds the 40-step DiffusionNFT baseline on six of eight metrics. The same objective also transfers to DNA promoter design, where it supports both teacher-free on-policy RL for a generator defined on a manifold and teacher-guided reward-graded distillation, with the latter yielding the lowest one-step Sei profile MSE among the compared configurations.

title: When a Flatness Proxy Is Not a Function: Robustness Certificates and Training Interventions
summary: A valid curvature upper bound need not justify either a robustness certificate or an intervention on an intrinsic predictor property. We demonstrate this distinction for a last-layer relative-flatness proxy used in both settings. First, empirical-risk stationarity does not eliminate pointwise first-order loss terms: at a finite global empirical-risk minimum, the retained certificate expression underestimates a loss increase by over $210\times$. We derive a globally valid, gauge-invariant feature-space repair. Second, common-row softmax shifts preserve predictions and the exact contraction while making the proxy unbounded. Even standard reference-class choices double it on average relative to the centered representation. For a single fixed-feature example with at least three classes, scalar retuning generically cannot align the induced probability updates. Row centering gives the orbit-minimized bound and restores value and full-model gradient invariance under this symmetry. Across 45 paired one-step tests on algorithmic and image models, amplified shifts separate raw-regularized predictors while quotient-regularized predictors remain aligned. Long-horizon CIFAR-10 experiments show substantial, reversible suppression of generalization, while evidence for selective delay after memorization is less consistent. Together, these results show that validity as a curvature upper bound does not by itself justify either inversion into a robustness certificate or differentiation into an intrinsic training intervention.

title: Parameterization method of reservoir properties for ensemble-based data assimilation using intermediate latent space of StyleGAN
summary: Ensemble smoothers are the most successful and efficient techniques currently available for history matching. However, because these methods rely on Gaussian assumptions, their performance is severely degraded when the prior geology is described in terms of complex facies distributions (non-Gaussian). In this way, for these methods, we need to apply efficient parameterization techniques. Currently, the most efficient methods for performing parameterization are deep learning models. However, given the variety of existing deep learning models, studies have not identified which is most suitable for use with ensemble-based methods, although some important models had already been evaluated. Based on a recent literature review, the most promising models selected were VAE-GAN, Latent Diffusion, and StyleGAN models. As a novel aspect of this work, data assimilation with the second generation of StyleGAN (StyleGAN2) model was performed using the latent z-space and intermediate w-space, separately. They were applied in two 2D case studies: one categorical (three facies) and the other continuous. The results demonstrated that all three models are highly efficient, with the StyleGAN2 model standing out for generating samples with geological realism and achieving excellent data matching in the cases studied. Our findings show that performing data assimilation with StyleGAN2 using the intermediate space (w-space) yielded better results than the traditional application in the latent space (z-space). This is due to the fact that ESMDA uses linear updates and the w-space is much more linear and disentangled than the highly entangled z-space, thereby ensuring that the updated vectors remain close to realistic geological patterns. These results were validated using main geostatistical and history matching metrics.

title: A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Conversational Home Energy Management Systems
comments: 25 pages, 7 figures, 9 tables. Re-set in the HUBS Lab paper layout (HUBS Lab Paper No. 2026-006); content unchanged
summary: The growing complexity in home energy management (HEM) demands advanced systems that guide occupants toward informed energy decisions reflecting their background, preferences, and context. Large language model (LLM)-integrated HEM systems (HEMS) have demonstrated promise, but previous studies relied on single-turn or single-task evaluations with response accuracy as the primary metric. Whether such systems deliver effective interactions across the extended multi-turn dialogues typical of real-world use remains an open question. This study introduces a comprehensive evaluation framework of LLM-integrated HEMS derived from the Goal-Question-Metric methodology, organized across five categories: task performance, factual accuracy, interaction quality, control capability, and system efficiency. A total of 23 metrics across multi-turn conversations are proposed and an LLM-as-judge pipeline is employed to enable scalable automated scoring. Its reliability is validated against three trained human coders: after iterative rubric calibration, twelve of the fifteen LLM-scored metrics reached strong agreement (ICC >= 0.73), three of them perfect, while the remaining three exhibited near-zero variance in human scores and are instead reported via mean absolute error (0.04-0.28). To demonstrate the framework's effectiveness, 970 dialogues -- 16 scenarios and five personas -- were generated and evaluated across four conversational HEMS configurations spanning a sophistication gradient, from a vanilla LLM with raw energy data to a multi-agent HEMS. The framework distinguished the four configurations across multiple evaluation dimensions, revealing their respective strengths and weaknesses. This study contributes to conversational HEMS by providing a reproducible, multi-dimensional evaluation methodology that comprehensively assesses sustained, context-aware system performance.

title: Cross-Benchmark Transfer from RL on Agentic Coding Tasks
comments: 15 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at ARRSI 2026, a workshop at AACL-IJCNLP 2026; also accepted as a non-archival paper at R2A-FM 2026
summary: Coding agents often fail in the last mile: they build most of a feature but drop a requirement, test only the cases their implementation already handles, break behavior that was supposed to stay intact, or validate against an unchecked assumption. We ask whether reinforcement learning (RL) on expert-built agentic coding tasks closes this gap, and whether what the agent learns transfers beyond the training distribution. We post-train Kimi K2.7 Code, a 1T-parameter (32B active) open-weight mixture-of-experts model, with RL alone on 1,700 tasks: 1,000 repository tasks graded by hidden fail-to-pass tests and by pass-to-pass tests of existing behavior, and 700 terminal tasks graded by expert-written hidden verifiers. The reward is the fraction of target checks passed and drops to zero if any pass-to-pass test fails. One epoch of GSPO on a rank-32 LoRA adapter improves pass@1 on each of the six external benchmarks we evaluated, across three agent harnesses: SWE-Bench Pro (60.1 to 64.8), DeepSWE (31.0 to 43.4), Terminal-Bench 2.1 (67.4 to 82.0), Terminal-Bench 3 (1.4 to 12.1), Terminal-Bench 4 (0.0 to 7.6), and SWE-Marathon (5.0 to 25.0). Pooled over the five independent task sets (Terminal-Bench 4 revises Terminal-Bench 3), the improvement is significant (p < 0.001), and it remains significant on the three sets released after the training data was collected (p = 0.004); the model also improves under both harnesses never used in training. Median trajectories on DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench 3 are 24-35% shorter in agent steps. The base model's failed DeepSWE runs are mostly near-misses, and on the tasks the trained model newly solves, paired trajectories show it avoiding each of the four failure modes above.
comment: 15 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at ARRSI 2026, a workshop at AACL-IJCNLP 2026; also accepted as a non-archival paper at R2A-FM 2026

title: AdaptViT: Runtime-Adaptive Vision Transformer Deployment on Custom RISC-V
comments: Accepted for publication at the 2026 IEEE 33rd International Conference on Electronics, Circuits and Systems (ICECS)
summary: Deploying Vision Transformers (ViTs) on low-power edge devices is challenging due to high computational demands. Conventional pruning frameworks require a separate compiled binary for each sparsity level, increasing storage overhead and limiting runtime adaptability. This paper presents an end-to-end deployment pipeline that transforms pretrained ViTs into a single runtime-configurable binary, enabling dynamic compute-budget switching on embedded CPUs. This is achieved by restructuring generated C kernels with modified loop bounds and binary-mask control logic, allowing execution to switch across discrete sparsity levels via compact external configuration files. Compared to multi-binary deployment, the proposed runtime-adaptive approach reduces on-device storage by up to 4.86x, requiring only 163 MB for ViT-Base instead of nearly 800 MB. To maximize pruning efficiency, we introduce a hardware-aligned block pruning strategy for Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) layers. In addition, a custom ISA extension is proposed to exploit input-reuse patterns in linear projection kernels. On a Synopsys TRV32P3FX RISC-V processor, the full system achieves up to 2.8x speedup at 65% MLP and 50% attention-head pruning for ViT-Base. The ISA extension alone provides a 1.56x speedup and 33% lower inference energy, with a 24.7% area overhead in a TSMC 28 nm implementation.
comment: Accepted for publication at the 2026 IEEE 33rd International Conference on Electronics, Circuits and Systems (ICECS)

title: Nearly Optimal Fixed-Confidence Best-Arm Identification with 1-Bit Feedback
comments: To appear in Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 39 (NeurIPS 2026, Spotlight)
summary: We study fixed-confidence best-arm identification under strict 1-bit feedback constraints. At each round, the learner selects an arm and a query set, and receives only a single bit indicating whether the sampled reward belongs to that set. We consider a distribution-free finite-variance setting with arm-wise localization, where direct empirical mean estimation is no longer available and clipping becomes unavoidable. We first formulate a time-uniform 1-bit mean-estimation primitive based on randomized threshold queries and a clipped tail-integral identity. We then embed this primitive into candidate-challenger best-arm identification algorithms. A fixed-clipping algorithm gives a simple anytime $(ε,δ)$-PAC guarantee, while a phased adaptive-clipping algorithm matches the clipping level to the current resolution and yields a gap-adaptive sample complexity. We also prove a $K$-arm worst-case information-theoretic lower bound showing that the logarithmic penalty caused by finite-variance 1-bit feedback is intrinsic. This bound matches the leading dependence of the phased algorithm up to logarithmic factors.
comment: To appear in Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 39 (NeurIPS 2026, Spotlight)

title: From TS-SUF-2 to TS-SUF-4: Practical Security Enhancements for FROST2 Threshold Signatures
summary:
Threshold signature schemes play a vital role in securing digital assets within blockchain and distributed systems. FROST2 stands out as a practical threshold Schnorr signature scheme, noted for its efficiency and compatibility with standard verification processes. However, under the one-more discrete logarithm assumption, with static corruption and centralized key generation settings, FROST2 has been shown by Bellare et al. (in CRYPTO 2022) to achieve only TS-SUF-2 security, which is a consequence of its vulnerability to TS-UF-3 attacks.
  In this paper, we address this security limitation by presenting an enhanced variant of FROST2, namely, FROST2+ which achieves the TS-SUF-4 security level under the same computational assumptions as the original FROST2. FROST2+ strengthens FROST2 by integrating additional pre-processing token verifications that help mitigate TS-UF-3 and TS-UF-4 vulnerabilities while maintaining practical efficiency. We show that FROST2+ can achieve TS-SUF-4 security not only under the same conditions as the original FROST2 analysis, but also when initialized with a distributed key generation protocol such as PedPoP. Our benchmark using ZCash's FROST library shows that the performance of FROST2+ is comparable to FROST2 and about 64-79% faster than FROST when precomputation is enabled.

title: What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation
comments: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Continual World Models. Project Website: https://nishitanand.github.io/what-should-world-models-forget/
summary: Continual learning treats any drop in performance on previously seen data as forgetting, a convention inherited from settings where the prediction target is stationary. World models violate this assumption: their target is the environment, which changes, so knowledge that was accurate when learned can later become false, and revising it is correct behavior rather than a defect. Non-stationary ground truth is well studied in the concept drift literature and in the temporal factuality of language models, but it has not been formulated for world models, which are distinctive in that they also encode structural knowledge, such as physical laws and object permanence, that must never be degraded. We argue that continual world models need retention stratified by invariance timescale, the time over which knowledge stays true: invariants should be refined but never degraded, while instance-level facts should be revised once the environment changes. We show that standard forgetting metrics, used alone, count correct revision as forgetting and so rank a frozen model highest. We propose differential retention, which reports two quantities separately: invariant retention, checked after every adaptation round, and revision latency, the number of observations a model needs to pick up a change.
comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Continual World Models. Project Website: https://nishitanand.github.io/what-should-world-models-forget/

title: SyclKittens: A Tile Programming Model for Programmers and Coding Agents on Intel GPUs
summary: New AI accelerators arrive before the kernels that make them fast, because peak kernel performance requires architecture-specific expertise in operand pipelines and data-movement techniques. Coding agents can now write, compile, and tune kernels on their own, so they could greatly accelerate kernel development and optimization. What agents produce depends on the interfaces they are given. These interfaces may expose a machine's raw capabilities or encode the known-good methods for exploiting its hardware features efficiently. We test the performance impact of these two interfaces on Intel GPUs through controlled experiments with five coding models on three kernels. With raw SYCL and execution feedback, Opus 4.8, the strongest of the three models tested with Claude Code, writes a single-GPU GEMM kernel reaching only 57.5% of Intel's tuned oneDNN library. We present SyclKittens, a hardware-aware tile programming model for Intel GPUs that encodes these known-good methods, so its operations place operands in matrix-engine layouts, prefetch through the L1 cache, and communicate over the fabric that links GPU stacks into a node. With SyclKittens under the same agent, task, and feedback budget, the agent reaches 82.1%, showing that encoded methods turn hardware capabilities into performance. Workload-specific policies stay programmable, and engineers and agents jointly refine these schedules in SyclKittens to build a kernel suite that reaches approximately 96% of oneDNN in geometric mean across GEMM shapes. The suite runs Llama-3.1-8B inference 1.59 times faster than torch.compile on one GPU and up to 2.91 times faster than a matched multi-GPU decode path on Intel's oneCCL. SyclKittens is open source and available at https://github.com/intel/SyclKittens.

title: Lightweight Semantic EEG Foundation Model for Frozen Cross-Disorder Transfer
comments: Withdrawn pending administrative review of publication-related requirements
summary: Large-scale EEG foundation models have demonstrated promising transferability across neurological disorders, but often require millions of parameters and substantial computational resources. In this paper, we present the Universal Semantic EEG Foundation Model (USE-FM), a lightweight EEG foundation model that learns transferable neural representations through self-supervised signal reconstruction on the Temple University Hospital EEG Corpus (TUEG). After pretraining, the encoder is frozen and evaluated on two clinically distinct downstream tasks, abnormal EEG detection (TUAB) and epileptic seizure recognition (TUEP), using a unified frozen-transfer protocol against recent EEG foundation models, including LUNA-Base and CBraMod. With only 1.46 million parameters, approximately one-fifth the size of existing models, USE-FM achieves competitive overall performance, including strong sensitivity and F1-score on TUEP (SEN $75.00 \pm 14.14$, F1 $70.37 \pm 4.01$), while maintaining competitive performance on TUAB (AUC $85.24 \pm 5.61$). Beyond downstream classification, latent representation analysis using $k$-means clustering together with PCA and t-SNE demonstrates that USE-FM learns organized semantic EEG representations comparable to substantially larger foundation models. These results suggest that large-scale self-supervised pretraining enables lightweight architectures to learn transferable semantic EEG representations, providing a computationally efficient foundation for cross-disorder analysis and future clinical decision support in neurological disorders.

title: Proof-Grounded Patient-Specific Clinical Explanations from Knowledge-Graph Reasoning
summary: Clinical decision support can lack auditable links from observations and encoded knowledge to conclusions and recommendations. Downstream of a frozen, training-free clinical knowledge-graph reasoner, the CKG Clinical Explanation Engine converts patient inference states and disease knowledge into typed facts, explicit rule traces, provenance-linked conclusions, and policy-licensed recommendations. Separate availability, representation completeness, and disease-specific activation distinguish observed zero-activation and partial evidence from unobserved evidence. Language-generation evaluation remains future work. Across six usable workbooks (11,289 patients, 33,867 patient-disease traces, 1,715,928 feature-evidence rows), IG-range validity, knowledge provenance, cross-sheet numerical fidelity (203,202/203,202), and exported fact/report field presence (33,867/33,867) reached 100.00%. Availability-representation consistency reached 99.29% (1,703,811/1,715,928), with 12,117 disagreements across five systematic feature-cohort patterns. Observed zero-activation and partial instances numbered 111,488 and 226,880, respectively. A separate seeded 30-patient end-to-end audit ran failure-free, passing all prespecified trace, licensing, provenance, and state-consistency checks. Paired comparisons (90 traces, fixed inherited diagnostic scores and policy catalogue) showed the availability-only baseline changed every report but no action sets. State collapse changed 20 action sets and removed 10 urgent-review occurrences. Rule replay reproduced all 40 action changes from reclassifying partial evidence as unobserved. The bounded validator detected all 450 single-fault mutants. Structural and implementation auditability were established. Clinical correctness and utility remain unestablished.

title: When to Rethink: Learning Multi-Perspective Self-Verification for Vision-Language Models
comments: The authors request withdrawal of this preprint. We have obtained additional experimental results and are substantially rewriting the manuscript to incorporate these findings and expand the analysis. No replacement version is currently available
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance in multimodal reasoning, yet they remain prone to generating plausible but incorrect answers. Self-verification offers a practical way to improve answer reliability without relying on external judges, but existing methods typically depend on a single verification criterion or fixed prompt, resulting in incomplete and unstable reliability estimates. We first systematically analyze how verifier capability and prompt design affect verification performance. Our findings show that stronger verifiers provide more reliable judgments, while verification performance is highly sensitive to prompt choice, with no single prompt consistently dominating across tasks. Guided by these findings, we propose \texttt{MOTIVE}, a \textbf{M}ulti-View Self-Verificati\textbf{O}n wi\textbf{T}h Rel\textbf{I}ability-Guided Selecti\textbf{VE} Rethinking framework for reliable multimodal reasoning. \texttt{MOTIVE} evaluates each candidate answer from complementary verification perspectives and learns a correctness-aligned reliability score through correctness-grounded multi-view verification learning. During inference, this score governs an accept-or-rethink decision, allowing reliable answers to be returned directly while uncertain ones trigger history-guided rethinking. Extensive experiments across diverse multimodal benchmarks and VLM backbones demonstrate that \texttt{MOTIVE} consistently outperforms strong self-verification and self-correction baselines. Further results show that reliable verification improves accept-or-rethink decisions and reduces unnecessary reasoning turns, enabling more reliable and efficient self-verification without an external judge.

title: Fast Non-Parametric Heteroscedastic Imitation Learning With Geometric Priors
summary: When learning probabilistic policies from human demonstrations, data-efficient learning and fast adaptations to new scenarios are key requirements. One popular way to achieve intuitive and reliable adaptations is through non-parametric, typically kernel-based, methods. However, existing solutions either fail to account for the geometry of manifolds common in robotics, limiting data efficiency, or, when geometry-aware, provide unreliable uncertainty estimates or require retraining to adapt. We propose a non-parametric approach leveraging geometric priors in scenarios of data scarcity and heteroscedastic uncertainties for probabilistic modeling. We utilize the method to formulate policies based on time or robot state, where non-separable diagonal kernels allow capturing uncertainty relations between degrees of freedom for same-sized in- and outputs. Fast updates, requiring less than 3 ms for a trajectory involving both position and orientation are possible through an optimized formulation. Our approach supports both manifold-valued input and manifold-valued output with large orientation changes. Using task parameterization, adaptation to different object poses is easily possible. We evaluate the approach on a set of toy examples and on real robot manipulation tasks both in autonomous execution and in shared control scenarios.

title: Similar Predictive Fit but Different Latent Dynamics: Characterizing Learned Dynamical Structure in Personalized Models of Brain Disorders
comments: Withdrawn pending administrative review of publication-related requirements
summary: As AI models move toward clinical decision-making and personalized treatment, understanding \emph{what} a model learns is important beyond predictive accuracy alone. We investigate whether personalized latent dynamics reveal clinically associated differences even when predictive fit is similar. A lightweight CNN--Transformer EEG foundation model pretrained on the Temple University EEG Corpus (TUEG) extracts segment-level representations. Using the Temple University Epilepsy Corpus (TUEP), representations are mapped to a shared latent-state space, and sparse multinomial logistic transition distributions (mLTD) are fit independently to each subject to obtain personalized transition-dependency graphs $W_n$. Analyses include $n{=}198$ subjects (99 epilepsy / 99 non-epilepsy). At $k{=}4$, epilepsy subjects exhibit substantially denser learned dependency structure ($p{=}1.1\times10^{-7}$), with the same pattern at $k{=}6$ (19.90 vs. 13.46; $p{=}5.2\times10^{-5}$). Graph-derived features provide moderate group discrimination under 5-fold subject-wise cross-validation (AUROC 0.68 at $k{=}4$; 0.65 at $k{=}6$). In contrast, held-out log-likelihood is nearly identical between groups at $k{=}4$ ($-0.992$ vs. $-0.991$; $p{=}0.95$), with similarly matched next-state prediction (AUROC 0.855 vs. 0.861; $p{=}0.54$). Thus, similar predictive fit does not imply similar learned dynamics: groups can be comparably predictable while differing substantially in the internal dynamical structure learned by personalized models. This distinction motivates evaluating learned structure alongside predictive performance in personalized clinical models.

title: Synchronization Reveals Market Structure That Classical Randomness Tests Cannot Detect
comments: 33 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. v3: adds out-of-sample HAR baselines and an economic-value analysis, uses closed-bar information timing, and corrects forecast statistics affected by opening-time alignment of multi-timeframe data. Submitted to The North American Journal of Economics and Finance
summary: Whether asset prices contain structure beyond a random walk is classically assessed with variance-ratio tests of the random-walk hypothesis. Synchronization measures from physics, notably the Kuramoto order parameter applied across trading timescales, have been proposed as an alternative diagnostic of market state, but they have been validated on single asset classes and never compared with the variance-ratio test on the same data. We compute a cross-timeframe Kuramoto coherence measure and a heteroskedasticity-robust Lo-MacKinlay variance ratio on identical windows for 61 instruments spanning cryptocurrencies, foreign exchange, metals, equity indices and single-name equities. The two diagnostics are statistically independent. We explain this analytically: coherence decomposes exactly into a direction-agreement channel and a volatility-agreement channel, and under sign-symmetric returns the direction channel is independent of the variance ratio and of every other statistic built from squared returns; simulations confirm the prediction. Coherence tracks the directional cleanliness of recent price moves in all five asset classes, whereas the variance-ratio test cannot reject the random walk for most of the panel. Held to finance benchmarks with strict information timing, however, coherence adds almost nothing to heterogeneous autoregressive volatility forecasts out of sample, and trading rules built on it earn no gross return outside cryptocurrency, where trading the coherence direction at high coherence breaks even at about five basis points per round trip. Failing to reject weak-form efficiency therefore does not rule out directional structure, but the structure that synchronization reveals is mostly descriptive and economically thin.

title: Tiling 3D Space by (Translates of) a Single Polycube is Undecidable
comments: 10 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables, 15 snippets. Added rotation/reflection results and corresponding table
summary: We prove co-RE-completeness, and thus undecidability, of the following problem: given a single (connected) polycube, decide whether it tiles 3D Euclidean space by translations. The same result holds if we also allow rotations and/or reflections. We reduce from Wang tiling using the decorated two-prime Sudoku construction of Greenfeld and Tao and a cyclic encoding adapted from OpenAI's 3D aperiodic tile, and apply a reduction of Kim to make the prototile connected (via faces). Dimension three is optimal: translational monotiling is known to be decidable in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and for a single (possibly disconnected) polyomino in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

title: Symbolic-Permutation-Based Direct Sparse Jacobian Assembly for Accelerated Power-Flow Analysis
summary: The repeated assembly of the sparse Jacobian matrix constitutes a primary computational bottleneck in the Newton-Raphson power-flow analysis. Through an algebraic operator equivariance analysis of the Jacobian matrix, this paper formalizes the reduction process and proposes a direct sparse Jacobian assembly method based on symbolic permutation. By pre-applying the permutation to the admittance matrix during a fast one-time symbolic phase via its sparse prefix-sum property, the runtime bus-type projection overhead and indirect mapping caches are entirely eliminated. Consequently, complex Jacobian differentiation and global matrix assembly fuse into a single operation, yielding a single-pass, branchless algorithm that streams values directly into contiguous memory. The proposed algorithm is implemented in the open-source RustPower solver. Benchmarks on IEEE test systems and PEGASE 9241 demonstrate that the proposed assembly is 28.1-37.9 times faster than the MATPOWER-style baseline and 8.9-9.7 times faster than the in-house Schäfer-Braun-inspired assembly (V1); on PEGASE 9241, it outperforms optimized traditional C++ assembly routines by 3.72 times in cold construction and 2.59 times across iterations. End-to-end, the iteration-loop solve time with KLU is 1.16-1.97 times faster than the native C++ LightSim2Grid and up to 95.5 times faster than pandapower, while leaving numerical results and convergence behavior unchanged. The method extends directly to general problems where a sparse Jacobian inherits its structure from a static network operator, including transient stability analysis, EMT simulation, and OPF Hessian assembly.

title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
summary: Large language models struggle to reliably identify and correct errors in their own reasoning. Unlike prior training-based approaches that fine-tune an LLM to generate revisions or feedback, we learn where to intervene in failed rollouts and determine how to redirect them. To choose where to intervene, we train a 130K-parameter MLP head on a frozen encoder using only final-answer correctness. For redirection, we find that under a fixed generation budget, the tested inline injections fail to reliably redirect reasoning, whereas presenting the same instruction in a new user turn changes the model's course. The resulting correction framework, UPTURN (User-Prompt TURN injection at a learned position), requires no LLM fine-tuning: it retains a selected prefix, injects an instruction as a new user turn, and regenerates the suffix. Across four reasoners and six math benchmarks, UPTURN improves average accuracy in every setting over a 32-rollout baseline. It outperforms self-correction and reflection-token injection baselines under matched correction budgets, transfers across reasoners and to GPQA-Diamond without retraining, and complements GRPO and self-correction methods.

AI.title_translation: 注入轮次而非标记：学习在何处重定向大语言模型推理以实现自我修正
AI.tldr: 提出免微调LLM的UPTURN框架，通过130K参数的MLP学习干预截断点，并以“新增用户轮次”注入引导指令，有效实现模型推理的自我纠错。
AI.motivation: 大语言模型难以可靠识别并纠正自身推理错误；且在固定生成预算下，现有的行内注入（inline injections）方法往往无法有效引导模型重定向推理方向。
AI.method: 提出免微调LLM的自修正框架UPTURN：1. 仅利用最终答案正确性弱监督，在冻结编码器上训练一个130K参数的MLP头来判定干预位置；2. 截取并保留模型错误推理的前缀；3. 不采用行内标记，而是将引导指令作为新的用户轮次（user turn）注入对话中；4. 重新生成推理后缀。
AI.result: 在4个推理模型和6个数学基准上，UPTURN在各种设置下的平均准确率均优于32-rollout基线；在相同计算预算下超越了自我修正与反思标记（reflection-token）注入基线；无需重训即可跨推理模型泛化并迁移至GPQA-Diamond，同时能与GRPO及传统自我修正方法形成良好互补。
AI.conclusion: 通过仅依赖答案正确性训练的轻量化MLP定位干预点，并以新用户轮次而非行内标记的形式注入提示，能够以免微调的方式显著且稳健地实现大模型推理的自我修正。
AI.translation: 大语言模型很难可靠地识别和纠正自身推理中的错误。与以往微调LLM以生成修订或反馈的基于训练的方法不同，我们学习在失败的生成路径中应在何处进行干预，并确定如何重定向它们。为了选择干预位置，我们仅基于最终答案的正确性，在冻结的编码器上训练了一个13万参数的MLP头。在重定向方式上，我们发现固定生成预算下，所测试的行内标记注入无法可靠地重定向推理，而将相同的指令作为新的用户轮次呈现则能改变模型的方向。由此产生的修正框架UPTURN（在学得位置进行用户提示轮次注入）不需要微调LLM：它保留选定的前缀，注入作为新用户轮次的指令，并重新生成后缀。在4个推理模型和6个数学基准测试中，UPTURN在各种设置下均比32次采样的基准提高了平均准确率。在预算匹配的情况下，它优于自我修正和反思标记（reflection-token）注入基线，无需重新训练即可跨推理模型迁移并泛化至GPQA-Diamond，并与GRPO及自我修正方法形成互补。
AI.summary: 针对LLM难以自我修正推理错误的问题，本文提出UPTURN框架。该方法无需微调主干LLM，而是训练一个13万参数的轻量MLP预测推理干预点，并创新性地发现以“新用户轮次”呈现修正指令相比行内token注入能更可靠地改变模型推理方向。实验表明，该方法在多个模型与基准上显著提升推理准确率且泛化性优秀。
AI.keywords: 大语言模型, 自我修正, 轮次注入, 推理重定向, UPTURN
AI.comments: 该研究创新性地指出大模型对“对话轮次（user turn）”的敏感度远高于行内标记（inline tokens），为推理干预提供了新的视角。其提出的UPTURN框架仅需训练13万参数的轻量分类头且无需微调底层LLM，兼具计算高效性、即插即用性与泛化能力。局限在于该方法依赖于截断并重新生成后缀，在极长推理链条下仍需权衡重新生成的计算开销。

title: PATTERN Can Be Solved from Memory: Testing Graph Neural Networks on Unseen Patterns
summary: PATTERN asks graph neural networks to find a planted subgraph in a new host graph. The hosts change, but the benchmark draws just 100 patterns and reuses them across training and test splits. A lookup that extracts these patterns from the training labels achieves 96.6% class-weighted accuracy on the official test split, above every published result, without fitting a model or consulting the generator. On unseen patterns, the same lookup scores 50.6%. A matcher that also uses the generator reaches 99.2% on the official split. Among five graph networks we retrained, GRASS and PPGT go from the top two on the official split to the bottom two on unseen patterns. Each loses 8.1 percentage points even when familiar and unseen patterns are matched in size. Logistic regression on two-hop node statistics scores above every run of the five networks on unseen patterns. For CKGConv, the advantage follows the training patterns: it reappears with each of three independently drawn pattern libraries and disappears when every training and validation graph gets a new pattern. Generator-based inference also scores 82.3% on CLUSTER, compared with a published best of 81.6%. On Minesweeper's released board, four of eight planned chains produced samples within the time budget; none converged, but their pooled predictions reached 99.86% ROC AUC, above the published best of 99.55%. PATTERN's official split tests its intended task of finding familiar patterns in new graphs. We recommend reporting the same checkpoint's score on unseen patterns alongside it.

AI.title_translation: PATTERN 数据集可仅凭记忆解决：在未见模式上测试图神经网络
AI.tldr: PATTERN 基准复用了训练集中的 100 种模式，使得免训练的查表法即可刷新纪录；一旦在未见模式下测试，主流 GNN 性能大幅崩溃甚至不如简单逻辑回归。
AI.motivation: 检验图基准测试 PATTERN 是否存在由于训练集和测试集复用仅 100 种固定子图模式而导致的“凭记忆解题”漏洞，并评估图神经网络在面对从未见过的模式时的真实泛化能力。
AI.method: 设计了一种无需训练、仅从训练标签中提取已知模式的查表法（lookup）以及结合生成器的匹配器；构建未见模式（unseen patterns）测试集重新评估了 5 种前沿图神经网络；引入基于两跳节点统计特性的逻辑回归作为对比基线；并将基于生成器的推理方法拓展至 CLUSTER 和 Minesweeper 数据集上。
AI.result: 无需拟合模型的查表法在官方测试集上取得 96.6% 的类别加权准确率（结合生成器可达 99.2%），超越所有已发表成果，但在未见模式上骤降至 50.6%；在未见模式下，原本在官方测试集中名列前茅的 GRASS 和 PPGT 准确率下降 8.1% 并跌至垫底；在未见模式下，简单的两跳节点统计逻辑回归跑赢了全部 5 种重新训练的 GNN；此外基于生成器的推理在 CLUSTER（82.3%）和 Minesweeper（ROC AUC 99.86%）上也均刷新了最优表现。
AI.conclusion: PATTERN 官方划分实质上仅测试了模型在宿主图中寻找“熟悉模式”的记忆与识别能力，而非结构归纳与泛化能力。作者建议未来在该数据集上评估模型时，应同时汇报在未见模式上的测试成绩。
AI.translation: PATTERN 任务要求图神经网络在新的宿主图中找到植入的子图。虽然宿主图会发生改变，但该基准测试仅抽取了 100 种模式并在训练集和测试集划分中复用它们。一种直接从训练标签中提取这些模式的查表法在官方测试集划分上达到了 96.6% 的类别加权准确率，超过了所有已发表的结果，且无需拟合模型或咨询生成器。在未见模式上，同样的查表法仅得 50.6 分。如果使用结合了生成器的匹配器，在官方划分上更可达到 99.2%。在我们重新训练的五种图网络中，GRASS 和 PPGT 在官方划分上排名前两位，但在未见模式上却跌至倒数两位；即使在熟悉模式和未见模式的大小相匹配时，它们也各自下降了 8.1 个百分点。在两跳节点统计数据上运行的逻辑回归，在未见模式下的得分超过了这五种网络的每一次运行。对于 CKGConv 而言，性能优势依赖于训练模式：在使用三个独立抽取的模式库时优势都会重现，但当每个训练图和验证图都使用新模式时优势便消失了。基于生成器的推理在 CLUSTER 上的得分也达到了 82.3%（此前已发表的最佳得分为 81.6%）。在扫雷（Minesweeper）公开的棋盘上，规划的八条采样链中有四条在时间预算内生成了样本；尽管均未收敛，但它们的汇总预测达到了 99.86% 的 ROC AUC，高于已发表的最佳成绩 99.55%。PATTERN 的官方划分测试的是其在全新图中寻找熟悉模式的既定任务。我们建议在汇报该任务表现的同时，并列汇报同一模型权重在未见模式上的得分。
AI.summary: 本文指出图神经网络基准数据集 PATTERN 由于在训练集和测试集中反复使用相同的 100 个子图模式，导致简单的查表法即可超越所有已发表的 GNN 模型。当测试环境切换至未见模式时，现有主流 GNN 的表现大幅跳水，甚至不如浅层的两跳逻辑回归模型。研究强调了该数据集在测试泛化能力方面的严重缺陷，并建议未来评估必须同时包含未见模式下的泛化测试。
AI.keywords: 图神经网络, PATTERN基准, 未见模式, 泛化评估, 记忆效应
AI.comments: 该论文敏锐地指出了图基准测试 PATTERN 中的一个严重缺陷：模式有限且在训练与测试间高度复用，导致模型倾向于“死记硬背”而非学习真正的图结构泛化能力。其创新之处在于通过极简的查表法和轻量统计基线（逻辑回归）直接击溃了复杂的前沿 GNN 模型，不仅揭示了现有评估协议的局限性，还提出了测试未见模式的合理建议，对图学习领域的基准评估具有重要的警示与修正意义。局限在于该分析主要聚焦于合成图检测场景，对真实大规模复杂图的泛化问题涉及较少。

title: Some complete $ω$-powers of a one-counter language in the difference hierarchy
summary: Fix a finite alphabet $Σ$ having at least two letters, and natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$. We denote by $D_n(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$ the class of differences of $n$ subsets of the Cantor space $Σ^ω$ in $\mathbfΠ^0_k$, and by $D^-_n(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$ the class of complements of sets in $D_n(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$. We prove, for any natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$, the existence of a finite alphabet $Σ$ having at least two letters and a finitary language $U_{n,k}$ over $Σ$ accepted by a one-counter automaton such that the $ω$-power $$U_{n,k}^\infty:=\{ w_0w_1\cdots\inΣ^ω\mid\forall i\inω~~w_i\in U_{n,k}\}$$ is $D_{2n-1}(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$-complete. We also prove a conditional result for the dual classes $D^-_{2n}(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$: under the assumption that there exists a finitary language $V_{n,3}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $ω$-power $V_{n,3}^\infty$ is $D^-_{2n}(\mathbfΠ^0_3)$-complete, there would also exist, for any integer $k > 3$, a finitary language $V_{n,k}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $ω$-power $V_{n,k}^\infty$ is $D^-_{2n}(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$-complete. Finally we add another conditionnal result about Wadge degrees of rational $\mathbfΔ^0_2$ omega powers, which completes the recent results of [FGL26].

title: Similar Models, Broken Odds: Where Luce's Axiom Fails in Chatbot Arena
comments: 20 pages, 5 figures, 10 tables; v3: adds a test on human summarization preferences and a calculation of votes needed for a release decision; clearer abstract, introduction and transfer results; appendix regrouped
summary: Chatbot Arena gives each language model one Bradley-Terry score, which fixes how often any model should beat any other. Choice theory predicts where this fails: near-copies are compared on the few details in which they differ, so votes between them are more decisive than their scores imply, exactly for the comparison a lab cares about, a new version against the old one. On 1.8 million Arena votes, votes between versions of one model are 1.37 times as decisive as Bradley-Terry predicts, between sizes of one generation 1.26 times and between models of one lab 1.12 times; a release a year later points the same way, and the effect survives tie, prompt, topic and timing checks. How alike two models' answers are worded and formatted tracks the effect. Plain scores leave the odds between relatives about 9% too close to even on held-out votes; a correction with four to six parameters roughly halves this and predicts held-out votes better, mostly by modeling ties, while the leaderboard order barely moves; frozen and carried to new releases, its gains in head-to-head odds are too small for our test to establish. With language-model judges and three-answer menus, a near-copy takes votes mostly from its twin when choices are pooled over prompts (log-odds shift +0.10, 95% interval 0.05 to 0.16), less so within a prompt.
comment: 20 pages, 5 figures, 10 tables; v3: adds a test on human summarization preferences and a calculation of votes needed for a release decision; clearer abstract, introduction and transfer results; appendix regrouped

title: PingpongDuo: Agile Humanoid Table Tennis Doubles with Safe Team Coordination
comments: 9 pages, 6 figures. Project page: https://www.archon.tech/research/PingpongDuo . Minor update
summary: Unlike singles, humanoid table tennis doubles requires teammates to strike in strict alternation while sharing a confined workspace. Rapid repositioning can compromise striking accuracy, while uncoordinated teammate movements introduce collision risks. We present PingpongDuo, a hierarchical framework for agile humanoid doubles with safe team coordination. At the team level, a planner jointly selects positioning targets and uses learned risk estimates to filter risky proposals, preferentially preserving the current striker's target. At the individual level, separate footwork and striking skills combine agile movement with precise racket control. The skills are guided by human motion references, including footwork collected from human doubles play, and trained from states produced by one another to support rapid transitions. A racket-arm residual further refines strikes after movement using return feedback from a simulator calibrated with real ball-flight and contact measurements. In simulation, PingpongDuo improves the ball-return success rate by 13.2% over the state-of-the-art baseline, while achieving approximately 2 cm positioning error during clearance. In real-world experiments, a robot completes a 2.15 m clearance-and-recovery cycle in 2.4 s with a peak speed of 2.23 m/s, while two robots sustain more than 10 consecutive strikes in strict alternation.

title: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
comments: NeurIPS 2026. 10 pages main text, 51 pages total. Code: https://github.com/hematteo/learning-to-read-out
summary: When does a language model acquire a capability? Developmental studies usually answer this by tracking when models start producing the correct token. But that prediction passes through the unembedding matrix, or readout, which is itself still being learned during pretraining. We show that a model's hidden states can encode task information before its own readout expresses it, so timelines read from outputs conflate what the model encodes with what its readout expresses. To track the readout directly, we introduce parameter-trajectory crosscoding, which fits one sparse dictionary to every token's readout row at every checkpoint. Unlike crosscoders on activations, it needs only checkpoint weights. We use it to locate a narrow early window, 0.4-1.1% of the way through Pythia's pretraining, in which the readout reorganizes and WordNet word categories become decodable from its rows. By then, linear probes on the hidden states already decode task information that the model's own outputs do not yet show. To test whether such gaps depend on how fast the readout learns, we pretrain small models from scratch that differ only in the readout's learning rate. We find that raising it makes the readout develop earlier and the gap close sooner, with little effect on final loss. Together, these results imply that early in training, where many developmental transitions are dated, a behavioral date can reflect when the readout learns to express task information and not when the model learns it.

AI.title_translation: 学会读出：语言模型预训练中的反嵌入动态
AI.tldr: 模型隐藏状态编码信息的时间早于反嵌入读出层表达信息的时间，仅凭输出行为评估会混淆模型的真实表征习得与读出能力的建立。
AI.motivation: 传统研究常通过模型生成正确 token 的时间来判断其何时掌握某种能力。然而，预测必须经过反嵌入层（即读出层），而该层自身也在预训练中演进。隐藏状态可能早在读出层表达之前就已编码了任务信息，导致从行为输出推断的时间线混淆了“模型编码的信息”与“读出层表达的信息”。
AI.method: 1. 提出参数轨迹跨编码（parameter-trajectory crosscoding），在各检查点对每个 token 的反嵌入权重行拟合单一稀疏字典（仅需模型权重，无需激活值）。 2. 结合隐藏状态线性探针（linear probes），对比内部表征与输出行为的解码时间差。 3. 从头预训练小模型，控制变量仅改变反嵌入层的学习率，检验读出层学习速度对表征与表达差距的影响。
AI.result: 1. 在 Pythia 预训练仅 0.4-1.1% 的极早窗口内，读出层发生重组，WordNet 词类开始可从中解码；而在该时期，隐藏状态探针已能解码出模型输出尚未体现的任务信息。 2. 提高反嵌入层的学习率能让读出层更早发展，显著加速弥合该表达差距，且对模型最终损失几乎没有影响。
AI.conclusion: 在语言模型训练早期，行为指标上测得的能力出现时间点，往往反映的是读出层学会表达该任务信息的时间，而非模型内部隐藏状态真正习得该信息的时间。
AI.translation: 语言模型何时习得某种能力？发展性研究通常通过追踪模型何时开始生成正确 token 来回答这个问题。但这种预测需要经过反嵌入矩阵（即读出层，readout），而该矩阵在预训练期间本身也在被学习。我们表明，模型的隐藏状态在自身的读出层能够表达任务信息之前，就已经对其进行了编码，因此从输出端推断的时间线混淆了模型所编码的内容与读出层所表达的内容。为了直接追踪读出层，我们引入了参数轨迹跨编码（parameter-trajectory crosscoding），该方法在每个检查点对每个 token 的读出层行拟合一个稀疏字典。与针对激活值的跨编码器不同，它仅需要检查点权重。我们利用它定位了 Pythia 预训练过程早期的一个狭窄窗口（进度为 0.4-1.1%），在此期间读出层发生重组，并且可以从其权重行中解码出 WordNet 词汇类别。在此期间，隐藏状态上的线性探针已经可以解码出模型自身输出尚未展现的任务信息。为了测试这种差距是否取决于读出层的学习速度，我们从头预训练了仅在读出层学习率上存在差异的小模型。我们发现，提高读出层学习率会使读出层更早发展，并更快缩小该差距，同时对最终损失几乎没有影响。综合来看，这些结果表明在训练早期（许多发展演变被定年之处），行为层面的时间节点可能反映的是读出层何时学会表达任务信息，而不是模型何时真正习得该信息。
AI.summary: 本文探讨了语言模型预训练过程中反嵌入层（unembedding/readout）对能力评估时间线的影响。作者指出隐藏状态编码信息往往早于输出端的表达。通过提出的仅需权重的参数轨迹跨编码方法、隐藏层探针以及调节反嵌入层学习率的实验，研究证明训练早期观察到的能力涌现时间点，很大程度上受限于读出层的学习速度，而非内部表征的实际习得时间。
AI.keywords: 反嵌入矩阵 (Unembedding Matrix), 模型预训练 (Pretraining), 读出动态 (Readout Dynamics), 跨编码 (Crosscoding), 线性探针 (Linear Probes)
AI.comments: 本研究切入点非常敏锐，深入探讨了大语言模型内部表征习得与最终读出层（unembedding matrix）表达能力之间的解耦现象，挑战了以往仅凭输出行为推断能力演变时间线的常规假设。提出的参数轨迹跨编码（parameter-trajectory crosscoding）方法仅依赖模型权重而无需推理激活值，具备很高的计算效率和实用价值；通过调整反嵌入层学习率的对照实验，有力地论证了读出延迟对行为测定的因果影响。

title: Finite Volume Convergence for a Heat Equation with a Measure-Valued Source
summary: Past work with Tom Seidman analyzed the spatial convergence order of the numerical finite element method applied to time-dependent diffusion-reaction equations with a measure-valued source term. For smooth source terms, the numerical method has second-order accuracy, but the non-smooth source terms introduce a limitation of the order that depends on the spatial dimension. This work in honor of Tom extends the analysis to the finite volume method in its clas- sical two-point flux form and shows that the regularity of the source term reduces the convergence order to 1 in two and 0.5 in three spatial dimensions which is reduced from the nominal second-order and depends on the space dimension. Computational tests with a point source modeled by a Dirac delta distribution exhibit the behavior predicted by the analytical results.

AI.title_translation: 含测度值源项热方程的有限体积法收敛性
AI.tldr: 本文研究了含测度值源项热方程的经典有限体积法收敛性，证明其精度从二阶退化为二维的1阶和三维的0.5阶，并通过点源算例进行了验证。
AI.motivation: 扩展过去针对时变扩散-反应方程有限元法的收敛性分析，探索在热方程中包含非光滑的测度值源项时，经典两点通量有限体积法的空间收敛阶如何受到源项正则性及空间维数的影响。
AI.method: 采用经典两点通量形式的有限体积法（finite volume method）对含测度值源项的热方程进行空间离散与收敛性分析，并采用狄拉克δ分布（Dirac delta distribution）构建点源数值算例进行验证。
AI.result: 理论推导表明源项的正规性将该方法的空间收敛阶从名义上的二阶降低至二维下的1阶和三维下的0.5阶；基于狄拉克δ分布点源的数值计算测试完全符合理论分析预测。
AI.conclusion: 具有测度值源项的热方程在采用经典两点通量有限体积法求解时，其空间收敛阶会受到源项低正则性与空间维数的严重限制，收敛阶从二阶退化为二维的1阶和三维的0.5阶。
AI.translation: 以往与Tom Seidman合作的研究分析了数值有限元法应用于含测度值源项的时变扩散-反应方程时的空间收敛阶。对于光滑源项，该数值方法具有二阶精度，但非光滑源项会引入依赖于空间维数的阶数限制。为了纪念Tom，本文将这一分析扩展到经典两点通量形式的有限体积法，并表明源项的正规性将收敛阶从名义上的二阶降低为二维空间的1阶和三维空间的0.5阶，这取决于空间维数。使用狄拉克δ分布建模的点源进行的计算测试展现了分析结果所预测的性态。
AI.summary: 本文分析了经典两点通量有限体积法求解含测度值源项热方程的空间收敛性。研究表明，源项的低正则性导致收敛阶从名义二阶退化为二维的1阶和三维的0.5阶，依赖于空间维数，数值实验验证了该理论结果。
AI.keywords: 有限体积法, 热方程, 测度值源项, 收敛阶, 狄拉克分布
AI.comments: 本文的重要意义在于将奇异/测度值源项的误差与收敛阶理论分析从有限元法推广至经典两点通量有限体积法，严格量化了维数效应对空间精度的制约（2D降至1阶，3D降至0.5阶）。局限在于仅针对经典两点通量格式，未探讨高阶或自适应网格等恢复精度的改进方案。

title: Chinese Decision: A Family of Language Models for Single-Pass Probabilistic Decision-Making
comments: 47 pages, 15 figures, 25 tables. Technical report v6. New since the previous arXiv version: unified 0.8B/2B/4B models with a typed span-extraction readout in the same weight file, the CJ-IE extraction mixture, and retention-cost analyses. Code: https://github.com/yanqiangmiffy/chinese-decision ; models: https://huggingface.co/quincyqiang
summary: Many applications need either a probability distribution over a few decisions or a set of typed spans from a text, and both are usually obtained by generating text. We present Chinese Decision, a family of Chinese models that answers both with a single forward pass and no generated token: candidate-letter logits give probabilities for Boolean, categorical, and ordinal decisions, and a small span head reading an echoed copy of the input gives typed character spans. Both readouts share one backbone and one merged LoRA, so a unified model is one weight file. We release decision-only and unified models at 0.8B, 2B, and 4B (Qwen3.5), trained for one epoch on 13.05 million decisions and, for the unified models, on CJ-IE, a 1.2-million-row Chinese extraction mixture. On the full 307,900-decision CJ-Bench, the unified 4B model reaches 86.86% accuracy, above every reported baseline and the decision-only 4B model (85.97%), and extracts spans on CJ-IE with micro F1 of 68.9. Retention has a price: against a 0.8B model continued on CJ-IE alone, which reaches 73.9 F1 but forgets CJ-Bench (71.02%), keeping decision ability costs 5.0 to 10.7 F1 points, shrinking with size. Gains of the unified models over decision-only ones are small, and all comparisons rest on single training runs with paired clustered bootstrap intervals.

AI.title_translation: 中文决策：用于单遍前向概率决策的语言模型家族
AI.tldr: 提出了无需生成 token 的 Chinese Decision 模型家族，仅通过单次前向传播即可同时输出概率决策与实体抽取片段，显著提升了推理效率。
AI.motivation: 许多实际应用需要获取少量决策选项的概率分布或从文本中抽取有类型片段，而传统方法通常依赖自回归文本生成，推理成本高且效率较低。
AI.method: 基于 Qwen3.5 架构构建 0.8B、2B、4B 的模型家族（包含纯决策与统一模型）。在不生成任何 token 的情况下通过单次前向传播完成任务：利用候选字母的 logits 计算布尔型、分类和序数决策概率；通过读取输入副本的小型 span 头提取有类型的字符片段。共享同一个骨干网络和合并 LoRA，并在 1305 万决策数据及 120 万 CJ-IE 抽取混合集上训练一个 epoch。
AI.result: 在包含 307,900 条决策的 CJ-Bench 上，4B 统一模型准确率达 86.86%，优于纯决策 4B 模型（85.97%）及所有基线；在 CJ-IE 抽取任务上微 F1 达到 68.9。相较于仅训练抽取的单任务模型，保留决策能力带来了 5.0 至 10.7 的 F1 损失，但该损失随模型规模增大而减小。
AI.conclusion: Chinese Decision 证明了无需自回归生成文本，仅通过单次前向推理即可高效联合实现离散概率决策与片段抽取；尽管保留决策能力对抽取 F1 带来了一定的性能折中，但该差距会随着模型参数量增大而缩小。
AI.translation: 许多应用需要几个决策上的概率分布，或者文本中的一组有类型片段（typed spans），而这两者通常是通过生成文本来获取的。我们提出了 Chinese Decision，这是一个中文模型家族，无需生成 token、仅凭单次前向传播即可同时解决上述两个问题：候选字母的 logits 提供了布尔型、分类和序数决策的概率，而一个读取回显输入副本的小型 span 头则提供带有类型的字符片段。两项读取任务共享一个骨干网络和一个合并的 LoRA，因此统一模型仅为一个权重文件。我们发布了基于 Qwen3.5 的 0.8B、2B 和 4B 的纯决策模型与统一模型，在 1305 万条决策数据上训练了一个轮次，统一模型还在包含 120 万条数据的中文抽取混合数据集 CJ-IE 上进行了训练。在完整的包含 307,900 条决策的 CJ-Bench 上，4B 统一模型达到了 86.86% 的准确率，优于所有已报告的基线以及 4B 纯决策模型（85.97%），并且在 CJ-IE 上的片段抽取达到了 68.9 的微 F1 值。能力保留是有代价的：相比于仅在 CJ-IE 上继续训练的 0.8B 模型（达到 73.9 F1，但遗忘了 CJ-Bench，准确率降至 71.02%），保留决策能力会导致 5.0 到 10.7 个 F1 点的损失，但这种差距会随模型规模增大而缩小。统一模型相对于纯决策模型的提升较小，且所有对比均基于单次训练运行及配对聚类自助抽样置信区间。
AI.summary: 本文提出了 Chinese Decision 语言模型家族，通过单次前向传播替代自回归文本生成，直接输出概率决策与有类型的字符片段。基于 Qwen3.5 的 4B 统一模型在 CJ-Bench 决策基准与 CJ-IE 抽取任务上均取得了优异表现，实现了高效、轻量的概率决策与信息抽取统一。
AI.keywords: 单遍前向推理, 概率决策, 片段抽取, 语言模型, 多任务学习
AI.comments: 创新性在于打破了传统大语言模型依赖自回归文本生成来完成分类决策和片段抽取的模式，利用单次前向传播（Logits加Span Head）同时解决两类任务，极大地降低了推理开销；重要性体现在构建了统一权重的高效中文决策模型家族。局限性在于多任务联合学习导致片段抽取性能相较单任务模型有一定折中（F1下降5.0-10.7），且结论基于单次训练实验。

title: Synthetic Image Oversampling for Rare-Class Representation Learning in Deep Facial Phenotyping
summary: Recent deep facial phenotyping methods can support the recognition of genetic syndromes, but patient images are often scarce and unevenly distributed across disorders. Synthetic facial images offer a way to supplement the training data without collecting additional patient photographs. Their usefulness, however, depends on whether they improve recognition of real patients: generated images may introduce artifacts or repeat features already represented in the training set. It is therefore necessary to examine both how much synthetic augmentation to use and which disorders benefit. We investigate disease-specific synthetic oversampling using images from the Phenotypic Disease Image Database to augment a subset of the GestaltMatcher Database. We compare increasing augmentation levels in an image-based model, GestaltMatcher-Arc, and a multimodal model, GestaltMML, while keeping the real training and patient-disjoint evaluation partitions fixed. Repeated training runs assess overall and disease-specific accuracy, and an exploratory embedding analysis examines changes in class compactness and separation. Augmentation improves mean recognition accuracy in both training setups, although gains remain modest in GestaltMatcher-Arc and continue across the tested levels in GestaltMML. These aggregate improvements are accompanied by uneven disease-level responses, including reduced accuracy for some disorders. In the embedding analysis, disorders with fewer real training images tend to gain more class separation, but geometric changes do not consistently track classification performance. Together, the findings support synthetic oversampling for limited-data facial phenotyping and emphasize the need to assess its amount and benefit for individual disorders within each training setup.

title: Self-Building Labs
summary: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific discovery by automating experimental execution and optimization. AI agents can increasingly propose new experiments, but existing SDLs can only run the procedures they were built for. Adapting them to a new experiment still requires extensive manual engineering, which makes laboratory flexibility the bottleneck for scaling discovery. We introduce the self-building laboratory (SBL), which designs, configures, and operates its own laboratory setup given a high-level scientific goal. SBL starts from whatever already exists, from an empty room to a working SDL, and builds the missing capabilities: the lab layout, its digital twin, robot skills, and experimental workflows. We demonstrate the system working across different robots and setups, scaling from a single workstation to laboratories with several robots working together. We validate SBL's end-to-end capabilities through a real-world quantum-dot synthesis experiment. By shifting human researchers from manually configuring and programming device automation to specifying scientific objectives, SBL makes scientific automation more accessible, flexible, and scalable. Project website: https://self-building-labs.github.io/

title: TorchTPU - A Hybrid Eager/Compiled Architecture for Native PyTorch Execution on TPU
summary: TorchTPU is an open-source collaboration between Google and Meta that introduces a native and principled PyTorch backend for Google TPUs. It enables seamless out-of-the-box model execution and TPU migration while delivering industry-competitive inference and training performance through eager execution optimizations, torch.compile integration, and native hardware acceleration.

title: FlashRT-PAI: Fast Kernels Are Not Fast Pipelines for Physical AI
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA), video-action (VA), and world action models (WAMs) form the backbone of modern physical AI systems, yet their real-time single-batch inference remains a defining bottleneck. Latency is dominated not by individual kernel computation, but by system-level overhead: thousands of short kernel launches, intermediate data movement across operator boundaries, and redundant recomputation across consecutive decisions. General-purpose graph compilers cannot address these costs, as they optimize individual calls in isolation and lack visibility into cross-call state semantics and global pipeline structure. We present FLASHRT-PAI, a low-latency inference engine built around model-hardware pipeline co-design rather than isolated kernel optimization. FLASHRT-PAI combines three core mechanisms: deep kernel fusion with launch overlap eliminates inter-operator boundaries and launch gaps; an execution contract formalizes the pipeline's stage DAG, update rates, and named buffers to enable cross-decision state reuse and selective refresh; and execution-state capsules enable fast snapshot, restore, and fork of persistent pipeline state. The system also supports drop-in acceleration of unmodified PyTorch models via parity- and latency-gated kernel replacement. Evaluation covers six policies on RTX 5090 and four on Jetson AGX Thor. At matched 16-bit precision, FLASHRT-PAI is 1.3-3.7x faster than official compiled paths. Combining pipeline co-design with reduced precision delivers 3.38-12.66x speedup over official eager implementations. In LIBERO-10, four-bit pi0.5 achieves 94.04% success on Thor and 93.32% on RTX 5090, compared with 92.4% for the measured official FP16 reference. FLASHRT-PAI is open source, distributed via Hugging Face Kernel Hub, and its opt-in pi0.5 kernels have been adopted into the LeRobot framework.

title: Assessing the CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models: A Case Study of GPT-6 Astra
comments: The paper contains 180 page long full report of CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models, and its 12 pages of summary. The project page is at: https://qiang-zou.github.io/projects/icad-eval-report/
summary: Recent advances in general-purpose AI models and agentic systems have enabled them to perform some CAD tasks. A systematic assessment is now needed to establish what these systems can accomplish and how well their outputs meet engineering requirements. This paper presents an empirical study of GPT-6 Astra, a SOTA general-purpose AI model, across four basic CAD tasks: model understanding, generation, editing, and evaluation. We design test cases spanning different levels of complexity and engineering requirements. The results show that GPT-6 Astra can support multiple stages of CAD workflows, with successful outcomes in cases involving nontrivial geometric complexity. This suggests that general-purpose AI is beginning to offer practical value in almost all steps in CAD workflow. However, gaps remain between generating visually plausible geometry and producing valid, functional, and editable CAD models. Recurring errors in freeform geometry, parameter dependencies, and mating relationships between parts limit engineering usefulness. Agentic iterative refinement can improve results but does not consistently resolve critical errors; long completion times further constrain practical use.
