title: Time Flies When You Parallelise: Pareto-efficient Time Series Foundation Models with Linear Recurrences
summary: Time series foundation models have demonstrated strong zero-shot forecasting performance, but computational efficiency remains a central architectural challenge. Temporal self-attention incurs quadratic cost in the number of temporal tokens, while nonlinear recurrent state transitions restrict parallel computation along the temporal dimension. We introduce ci-proto, a family of time series foundation models based on Mamba-3, whose linear state recurrences support chunk-wise parallel-in-time computation during training, and inference costs that scale linearly with sequence length. The architecture alternates recurrent temporal processing with cross-variate attention, supporting multivariate probabilistic forecasting with past-only and future-known covariates. Across fev-bench's 100 forecasting tasks, ci-proto XL sets a new state of the art among time series foundation models. The five ci-proto variants also make up the entire Pareto frontier for mean scaled quantile loss and mean absolute scaled error against both parameter count and median runtime.

title: S1-Evo: Experience-Guided Evidence Competition Attacks on Typed System-1 Decision Models
summary: Typed System-1 (S1) decision models are increasingly deployed in LLM agents for routing, moderation, and authorization to cut inference cost, yet untrusted context can still manipulate typed outputs and alter execution branches. Unlike autoregressive System-2 (S2) models, S1 interfaces score dynamic rules and options without token-by-token decoding, mismatching attacks targeting text continuation or explicit override commands. We propose S1-Evo, a self-evolving framework tailored to S1's contract-based option competition and margin feedback. S1-Evo perturbs untrusted fields via contract-aware evidence channels to induce \emph{evidence competition} with original task evidence while preserving fact invariance. Offline on seed tasks, it optimizes candidates via feedback search guided by directional margins and re-verification, distilling verified flips into experience cards. At test time, S1-Evo retrieves relevant cards to construct perturbations for unseen tasks. Across four benchmarks and three S1 models, S1-Evo reaches 71.99\% mean ASR and 57.47\% high-confidence ASR on \texttt{jev-1.14}, and causes up to 24.00\% E2E agent violations.

title: LazyWeights: Decode-on-Demand Edge LLMs
summary: Memory decides which LLMs an edge device runs, and how fast: capacity on a 4 GB Jetson Nano, bandwidth on an 8 GB Jetson Orin Nano Super. Deployed formats (GPTQ, AWQ, llama.cpp's K- and I-quants) spend equal bits on every integer code of a matrix, although the codes are far from uniform. LazyWeights keeps these formats but tunes GPTQ so the codes compress, Huffman-codes them losslessly in interleaved lanes, and decodes them on demand in a small unit between DRAM and L2, so GPU kernels run unchanged and DRAM moves only coded bytes. At 1% and 3.5% perplexity budgets, coded Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B and SmolLM-1.7B are 5.7-31.4% smaller than the best llama.cpp format. A bit-exact 0.21 mm^2 ASIC decoder unit (1 GHz, 7 nm) cuts Orin latency and energy per token by up to 36% and 38% (54% and 44% with prompt-lookup speculation). On the Nano, LazyWeights needs 58-64% less time and 53-57% less energy per token than CPU llama.cpp, and runs a streamed Mistral-7B 6.6x faster at 3.89 bits per weight. A Huffman decoder beats an rANS decoder in rate and area at equal throughput; the ASIC decoder unit runs bit-exact on a Zynq UltraScale+ FPGA (AMD ZCU102).

title: A Convex-Analytic Reformulation for Poisoning Attacks on Logistic Regression
summary: We study data poisoning attacks on logistic regression with $\ell_2$-regularization, where an attacker chooses the features of a fixed number of injected observations with prescribed labels to maximize the logistic loss on the clean training data. Strong convexity of the defender's problem yields an exact reformulation through its first-order optimality conditions. Using convex conjugacy of the softplus function, we replace the sigmoid relations by a single convex optimality-gap inequality and express the attacker's objective as a concave function. A change of variables makes the stationarity condition affine, leaving bounded bilinear equalities as the only nonconvex constraints. We derive finite bounds on all variables involved in these equalities, including a global bound on the coefficient norm and tighter bounds obtained by preprocessing based on convex optimization. Experiments on eight binary classification datasets evaluate attack effectiveness and compare the two reformulations when solved with SCIP. Attacks obtained by local optimization degrade predictive performance on most datasets, while the convex-analytic formulation produces substantially stronger reported dual bounds within a fixed time limit.

title: Learning Dynamics of the Influencer's Game in Resource Landscapes
summary: Across domains as varied as ecology, economics, and online platforms, individuals are incentivized to position themselves within resource-rich strategy spaces. In this work we introduce a new spatial game framework called the influencer's game. Within this new framework players' strategies are represented as positions within a trait space. Players then receive a share of a portion of a resource based on their relative influence at that resource's points traits. For the influencer's game, we show that there is a unique symmetric Nash equilibrium that exists under strict log-concavity of the influence kernel. Using the unique equilibrium we show that the stability of the system depends on the influence kernel's parameters, number of players, and the resource distribution shape. For any dimension we demonstrate a stability threshold that depends on both the scatter and curvature of the players. When this threshold is crossed, the symmetric equilibrium destabilizes and gives way to a variety of bifurcation types; including, specialist clusters, limit cycles, and sub-games that reproduce the larger game's structure. We ground these results using real-world data for resources as a demonstration of the game's application. Finally we extend the game dynamics to use multi-agent reinforcement learning and further show that the predicted bifurcation structure persists under partial observability and discretized strategy spaces. In all, the influencer's game provides a novel framework for predicting when competitive pressure drives convergence versus fragmentation with possible applications across domains.

title: HEIR: Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interactions
summary: For robots to assist, serve, and collaborate with humans, they must not only interpret human requests conveyed through language and multimodal intentional cues, but also execute long-horizon tasks that interleave navigation and manipulation. In this paper, we introduce HEIR, a resource for studying how to Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interaction. HEIR pairs human speech, measured gaze, and egocentric video with robot observations and teleoperated navigation-manipulation trajectories, while each session preserves successive episodes, with each request fulfilled through multiple execution subtasks. The captured data, together with human-authored annotations, support the study of intent grounding, execution planning, and task completion within a unified interaction setting. To demonstrate the value of HEIR, we conduct extensive offline experiments to evaluate how models benefit from additional human-centric context across these tasks, together with real-robot experiments that assess execution task completion. HEIR thus provides a valuable resource for studying user-centric robot interaction in naturalistic household environments. Our demo and dataset are available online.

title: Ballad: Bandit-Based LLM Routing for Automated Heuristic Discovery
summary: Modern automated heuristic discovery (AHD) systems increasingly rival hand-crafted heuristics by leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to iteratively mutate and refine solutions. A natural assumption is that more powerful and more expensive models consistently yield better heuristics. We challenge this empirically: across multiple NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems, we find no consistent advantage for larger, costlier models. This raises a deeper question: given a pool of LLMs spanning frontier and freely hosted or open-weight models, how should one adaptively select which model to invoke at each step of the search? The challenge is non-trivial. The optimal LLM may shift over the course of a run, and because one LLM's output seeds the context for subsequent calls, each model's reward signal is non-stationary and entangled across the heuristic population, thus violating the independence assumptions of classical online decision-making settings. We address this through Ballad (Bandit-based LLM Routing for Automated Heuristic Discovery), an online bandit algorithm that learns to orchestrate a pool of LLMs into an ensemble that matches or exceeds what any soloist LLM achieves alone. This orchestration is powered by an LLM selection policy that favors rare, high-scoring heuristics over stable averages, a DAG-based credit propagation mechanism through the genealogy of the heuristic population, and discounting of stale observations to remain attuned to each model's current utility. Across five NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems and a pool of four models of varying capability and cost, Ballad not only matches the best individual LLM in hindsight but, in several cases, surpasses every individual model while reducing API cost by up to 65.6% relative to always using the strongest model.

AI.title_translation: Ballad：用于自动化启发式发现的基于多臂老虎机的大语言模型路由算法
AI.tldr: 提出了基于老虎机算法的LLM动态路由框架Ballad，能在组合优化启发式搜索中智能调度不同成本的LLM，不仅降低高达65.6%的开销，性能还匹敌或超越单一最佳模型。
AI.motivation: 传统观点认为更强大、更昂贵的LLM必然能生成更好的启发式算法，但实验表明更大、更贵的模型并无稳定优势；同时，在搜索过程中不同LLM的最优性会动态变化且生成内容相互依赖，导致奖励信号非平稳并打破独立性假设，因此需要一种能自适应调度异构LLM池的算法。
AI.method: 提出了Ballad算法，这是一种在线多臂老虎机框架，包含三大核心机制：1）优先选择稀有、高分启发式算法而非稳定均值的LLM选择策略；2）基于种群家谱的有向无环图（DAG）信用传播机制；3）对过时观测进行折扣以适应各模型的当前效用。
AI.result: 在5个NP难组合优化问题以及包含4种不同能力与成本的LLM池上，Ballad不仅能匹敌事后最佳的单模型，还在多个案例中超越了所有单一模型，同时相较于始终调用最强模型降低了最高达65.6%的API成本。
AI.conclusion: 通过基于多臂老虎机的动态LLM路由策略（Ballad），能够打破单一模型依赖，在显著降低API调用成本的同时，发现优于或匹配单一最强模型的启发式算法。
AI.translation: 现代自动化启发式发现（AHD）系统通过利用大语言模型（LLM）迭代变异和优化解，日益能与人工设计的启发式算法相匹敌。一个自然的假设是，更强大且更昂贵的模型总能持续生成更好的启发式算法。我们在多个NP难组合优化问题上对这一假设进行了实证挑战，发现更大、更昂贵的模型并不具备一致的优势。这引出了一个更深层的问题：在包含前沿模型以及免费托管或开源权重模型的LLM候选池中，应如何在搜索的每一步自适应地选择调用哪个模型？这一挑战并非微不足道：最优LLM可能会在运行过程中发生转变；由于一个LLM的输出会作为后续调用的上下文输入，每个模型的奖励信号是非平稳的，且在启发式算法种群间相互交织，从而打破了经典在线决策设定的独立性假设。我们通过Ballad（用于自动化启发式发现的基于多臂老虎机的大模型路由算法）解决了该问题，该在线老虎机算法通过学习将LLM池编排为一个集成系统，其效果能够匹敌甚至超越任何单一LLM单独达到的水平。该编排机制由三部分驱动：倾向于稀有高分启发式算法而非稳定平均表现的LLM选择策略、贯穿启发式种群家谱的基于有向无环图（DAG）的信用传播机制，以及对陈旧观测进行折扣以实时契合各模型当前效用。在5个NP难组合优化问题和由4个不同能力与成本的模型组成的候选池上的实验表明，Ballad不仅与事后最佳的单一LLM表现相当，在多个情况下还超越了所有单一模型，同时相对于始终使用最强模型，API成本最高降低了65.6%。
AI.summary: 本文研究了自动化启发式发现（AHD）中异构大语言模型（LLM）的动态选择问题。针对大模型未必总是最优以及搜索过程中奖励信号非平稳、强耦合的挑战，提出了基于在线多臂老虎机的路由算法Ballad。该算法利用偏向高分极值的选择策略、基于家谱的DAG信用传播和遗忘衰减机制协同编排LLM池，在5个组合优化问题上以最多降低65.6%成本的代价，取得匹敌甚至超越单一最优模型的搜索效果。
AI.keywords: 自动化启发式发现, 大语言模型路由, 多臂老虎机, 组合优化, 信用分配
AI.comments: 该论文针对自动化启发式发现中盲目依赖昂贵大模型的误区提出了质疑，并针对启发式搜索过程中奖励信号非平稳且相互交织的难点，创新性地结合DAG信用传播与老虎机算法实现多LLM动态路由，在降低成本的同时甚至超越了单一最佳模型的性能，具有很高的实用价值和理论启发意义。

title: ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research
summary: Model architecture shapes the scaling behavior, training efficiency, and inference cost of LLMs, making it a central focus of both industry and academia. In industry, teams such as those behind DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi routinely introduce architectural innovations, yet public reports rarely document which ideas succeeded, which were abandoned, and why. In academia, limited compute and inconsistent baselines often restrict evaluations to small-scale, single-point comparisons, making it difficult to establish whether improvements hold at larger scales or translate into broader impact. ArchSpace addresses both gaps as a public platform for Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing Architecture Research: each proposal is recorded with its experiments and reasoning, reviewed by the community, and referenced by later work. To evaluate ideas before costly large-scale training, ArchSpace leverages scaling laws to predict model loss at larger scales from smaller experiments, a practice widely adopted in industry. We provide initial references that make the platform usable: Qwen3.5 and OLMo3 baselines, fitted scaling laws, and a reusable training recipe. Ideas validated through this review can in turn become new baselines, and ArchSpace thereby aims to broaden the range of ideas that shape the next generation of models.

AI.title_translation: ArchSpace：大语言模型架构研究的记录、评审与参考平台
AI.tldr: ArchSpace 是一个针对大模型架构研究的公共平台，结合标度律预测与开源基准，规范并促进架构想法的记录、评审与引用。
AI.motivation: 工业界虽然频繁创新，但很少公开记录架构创新的成败及原因；学术界则受限于算力与不一致的基线，难以验证小规模对比的改进能否扩展到更大规模。两界之间存在明显的架构研究验证与经验共享鸿沟。
AI.method: 构建公开平台 ArchSpace，记录架构提案的完整实验与推理并接受社区评审；借鉴工业界做法，利用标度律（Scaling Laws）通过小规模实验预测模型在大规模下的损失表现；提供包含 Qwen3.5、OLMo3 基准、拟合好的标度律及可复用训练配方在内的初始参考资源。
AI.result: 成功搭建了 ArchSpace 平台框架，并提供了可直接使用的 Qwen3.5 与 OLMo3 基线、拟合的标度律模型以及可复用的训练配方，使经评审验证的架构方案能够持续转化为新的基准。
AI.conclusion: ArchSpace 旨在通过建立标准化的记录、评审和基于标度律的预测机制，拓宽能够真正影响下一代模型构建的创新架构构想范围。
AI.translation: 模型架构决定了大语言模型（LLM）的标度行为、训练效率和推理成本，因而成为工业界和学术界关注的核心。在工业界，诸如 DeepSeek、Qwen 和 Kimi 等团队经常推出架构创新，但公开报告很少记录哪些想法成功了、哪些被放弃了以及背后的原因。在学术界，有限的算力和不一致的基线往往将评估局限于小规模的单点对比，难以确定性能提升是否能在更大规模下保持或转化为更广泛的影响。ArchSpace 作为一个用于“记录、评审和参考架构研究”的公共平台弥补了这两个差距：每个提案都记录其实验和推理过程，由社区评审，并供后续工作引用。为了在进行昂贵的大规模训练之前评估想法，ArchSpace 利用工业界广泛采用的方法，借助标度律从小规模实验中预测更大规模下的模型损失。我们提供了使该平台立即可用的初始参考：Qwen3.5 和 OLMo3 基准、拟合的标度律以及一套可复用的训练配方。通过评审验证的想法进而可成为新的基准，ArchSpace 藉此旨在拓宽塑造下一代模型的想法范围。
AI.summary: 本文提出了用于大模型架构研究的公共平台 ArchSpace。针对工业界记录不透明与学术界算力/基准受限的问题，ArchSpace 结合了社区记录评审机制与标度律预测评估方法，并开源了标准基线和训练配方，以系统性促进下一代模型架构创新的验证与积累。
AI.keywords: 大语言模型, 模型架构, 标度律, 基线评测, 开源平台
AI.comments: 该研究的重要创新在于建立了连接工业界实际工程经验与学术界创新探索的桥梁，解决了大模型架构研究中负面实验结果不公开、小规模评估难以推广至大尺度等痛点。其采用标度律来低成本验证架构创新的思路非常务实。潜在局限在于架构创新若改变了基本范式，标度律外推预测的准确性可能面临挑战，且平台的可持续发展高度依赖社区的活跃参与。

title: Online Nonconvex Decision Making with Approximate Oracles
summary: We study online decision making with possibly nonconvex (for example, combinatorial or integer) local feasible sets and convex long-term constraints. At each period, a decision maker selects a local action to maximize cumulative reward while ensuring that the sequence of actions satisfies the global constraints in the long term. It is known that $O(\sqrt{T})$ long-term constraint violation and $O(\sqrt{T})$ reward regret are achievable if given access to a local optimization oracle that exactly solves optimization problems over each local feasible set. Instead of requiring exact optimization over each local feasible set, we assume access to an approximate local optimization oracle that permits optimization errors quantified by two parameters $(δ_+,δ_\times)$. We develop an approximate online dual mirror descent algorithm and show that its guarantees depend on a feasibility slack parameter $\underline d$, which measures the compatibility between local feasible sets and the long-term constraint. Under the standard random permutation model, when $δ_+=O(1)$, $δ_\times<\underline d$ and $\underline d-δ_\times=Ω(1)$, the algorithm achieves $O(\sqrt T)$ long-term constraint violation and reward regret up to $O\bigl(\sqrt T+δ_\times T\bigr)+δ_+ T$. We also show a matching limitation: when $δ_+=0$ and $δ_\times>\underline d$, no online algorithm relying on such approximate oracle outputs can guarantee sublinear long-term constraint violation in general.

title: Quantum Channel Testing in Average-Case Distance
summary:
We study the complexity of testing properties of quantum channels. First, we show that testing identity to any channel $\mathcal N: \mathbb C^{d_{\mathrm{in}} \times d_{\mathrm{in}}} \to \mathbb C^{d_{\mathrm{out}} \times d_{\mathrm{out}}}$ in diamond norm distance requires $Ω(\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{in}}} / \varepsilon)$ queries, even in the strongest algorithmic model that admits ancillae, coherence, and adaptivity. This is due to the worst-case nature of the distance induced by the diamond norm.
  Motivated by this limitation and other theoretical and practical applications, we introduce an average-case analogue of the diamond norm, which we call the average-case imitation diamond (ACID) norm. In the weakest algorithmic model without ancillae, coherence, or adaptivity, we prove that testing identity to certain types of channels in ACID distance can be done with complexity independent of the dimensions of the channel, while for other types of channels the complexity depends on both the input and output dimensions. Building on previous work, we also show that identity to any fixed channel can be tested with $\tilde O(d_{\mathrm{in}} d_{\mathrm{out}}^{3/2} / \varepsilon^2)$ queries in ACID distance and $\tilde O(d_{\mathrm{in}}^2 d_{\mathrm{out}}^{3/2} / \varepsilon^2)$ queries in diamond distance in this model. Finally, we prove tight bounds on the complexity of channel tomography in ACID distance.

title: Efficient LP warmstarting for linear modifications of the constraint matrix
summary: We consider the problem of computing the optimal solution and objective value of a linear program whose constraint matrix changes linearly with a parameter, for a predefined set of values of this parameter. Based on the information given by a precomputed basis, we present three efficient LP warm-starting algorithms, based on the eigenvalue decomposition, the Schur decomposition and the Hessenberg decomposition, to evaluate the optimal solution and optimal objective value of these problems. The three algorithms have an overall complexity of $O(pm^2+pmn)$ where $m$ (resp. $n$) is the number of constraints (resp. variables) of the original problem and $p$ the number of parameter values after an initial preprocessing step. We also provide theorems related to the optimality conditions to verify when a basis is still optimal. When the perturbation of the basis matrix has a low rank $ρ$, as is often the case in practice, we then reduce all the computations to a $ρ\timesρ$ matrix built with $ρ$ solves with the factorization of the basis maintained by the simplex solver; with it, we compute, in each direction, an interval on which the basis is guaranteed to remain optimal, together with a bound on the objective. In practice, these intervals are close to the exact ones, and they remain useful for degenerate bases. We also propose a matrix-free method based on shifted Krylov subspaces. Numerical experiments on 398 instances built from real models, with up to 349,120 constraints, assess the accuracy, the cost and the range of applicability of all the methods. On the interval on which a basis remains optimal, once this interval is known, the low-rank and Krylov methods compute the optimal objective value 117 to 304 times faster than a warm start of the solver, in median.

title: Bias-Optimal Bounds for Stochastic Gradient Descent
summary: The non-asymptotic analysis of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) typically yields bounds that decompose into a bias term and a variance term. In this work, we focus on the bias component and study the extent to which SGD can match the optimal convergence behavior of deterministic gradient descent. Assuming only (strong) convexity and smoothness of the objective, we derive new bounds for the full range of constant step-sizes $γL \in (0,2)$. This includes critical and large step-size regimes that were previously unexplored without additional variance assumptions, in both the convex and strongly convex cases. Those bounds are bias-optimal, in the sense that the bias term coincides with the worst-case rate of gradient descent, for all non-critical step-sizes. For critical step-sizes, we show that no bounds can be obtained with an optimal bias term, but that this optimal bias can be approximated arbitrarily closely. As an immediate application, we provide new complexity bounds for the Stochastic Proximal algorithm, without the need of regularity assumptions.

title: Recovering the Euclidean Geometry of High-Dimensional Data Under Heterogeneous Noise
summary: Pairwise Euclidean distances provide a simple geometric representation of high-dimensional data and underlie many data analysis methods, including clustering, visualization, and manifold learning. However, in real-world applications, these distances can be severely corrupted by heterogeneous noise, where different data points are subject to different, and potentially large, noise levels. Such noise distorts the distances inhomogeneously, leading to a misrepresentation of the underlying data geometry. In this work, we ask whether the underlying clean Euclidean geometry can nevertheless be recovered from the corrupted pairwise distances. We answer this question affirmatively, showing that, perhaps surprisingly, such recovery is possible across a broad class of high-dimensional settings with underlying low-dimensional geometry, even when the noise magnitudes vary substantially across observations. We develop a principled approach for recovering the clean pairwise distances, without prior knowledge of either the clean data structure or the noise distribution, and establish probabilistic recovery guarantees. In particular, the recovery error converges to zero at polynomial rates as the feature dimension and dataset size increase simultaneously. Experiments on synthetic datasets demonstrate accurate recovery of the Euclidean geometry in challenging regimes and improved robustness of downstream methods that rely on pairwise distances. When applied to real single-cell RNA sequencing data, our method reliably recovers local neighborhood structure, enabling accurate nearest-neighbor identification used in many downstream analyses.

title: Toric geometry of ReLU neural networks
summary: Given a continuous piecewise linear function $f:\mathbb{R}^{n_0} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a fixed architecture of feedforward ReLU neural networks, the exact function realization problem asks when a network of that architecture realizes $f$. In contrast, expressivity concerns characterizing all functions exactly realizable by a given architecture. To address these questions systematically, we establish a connection between toric geometry and ReLU neural networks, allowing tools from algebraic geometry to analyze the structures. Starting with an unbiased ReLU network with rational weights, we define the ReLU fan, the ReLU toric variety, and the ReLU Cartier divisor associated with the network. This work also relates the tropical and the toric geometry: the former captures combinatorial data of ReLU networks, while the latter recovers the underlying geometric structure. As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of the functions realizable by unbiased shallow ReLU networks with rational weights. The characterization is expressed in terms of intersection numbers of ReLU Cartier divisors with torus-invariant curves and leads to a decomposition of piecewise-linear functions into shallow and non-shallow components.

AI.tldr: 本文将环面几何理论引入ReLU神经网络的研究中，利用代数几何中的相交理论完整刻画了无偏置浅层有理权重ReLU网络的表达能力。
AI.motivation: 为了系统性地解决前馈ReLU神经网络的精确函数实现问题（即某特定网络架构何时能够精确实现给定的连续分段线性函数）以及网络表达能力的刻画问题。
AI.method: 建立环面几何与ReLU网络的对应关系，针对具有有理权重的无偏置ReLU网络，定义了ReLU扇（ReLU fan）、ReLU环面簇（ReLU toric variety）以及ReLU卡蒂埃因子（ReLU Cartier divisor），并将热带几何的组合数据与环面几何的代数几何结构相关联。
AI.result: 完整刻画了具有有理权重的无偏置浅层ReLU网络所能实现的所有函数，该表征通过ReLU卡蒂埃因子与环面不变曲线的相交数给出，并据此实现了分段线性函数向浅层与非浅层分量的分解。
AI.conclusion: 环面几何为系统性分析ReLU神经网络的函数实现机制与表达能力提供了有力的代数几何工具，证明了相交理论在解析神经网络函数空间结构中的有效性。
AI.translation: 给定一个连续分段线性函数 $f:\mathbb{R}^{n_0} \to \mathbb{R}$ 和前馈ReLU神经网络的固定架构，精确函数实现问题探讨的是该架构的网络在何时能够精确实现 $f$。相比之下，表达能力则关注刻画由给定架构完全可精确实现的所有函数。为了系统性地解决这些问题，我们建立了环面几何与ReLU神经网络之间的联系，从而能够使用代数几何工具来分析其结构。从具有有理权重的无偏置ReLU网络出发，我们定义了与网络相关的ReLU扇、ReLU环面簇以及ReLU卡蒂埃因子。这项工作还将热带几何与环面几何联系起来：前者捕获了ReLU网络的组合数据，而后者恢复了其底层的几何结构。作为应用，我们获得了由具有有理权重的无偏置浅层ReLU网络可实现函数的完整刻画。该刻画通过ReLU卡蒂埃因子与环面不变曲线的相交数来表达，并导出了一种将分段线性函数分解为浅层和非浅层分量的方法。
AI.summary: 本文建立了环面几何与ReLU神经网络之间的联系，引入了ReLU扇、ReLU环面簇和ReLU卡蒂埃因子等代数几何工具。通过结合热带几何与环面几何，论文基于相交数理论完全刻画了无偏置、有理权重的浅层ReLU网络所能实现的函数类，并给出了分段线性函数的分解方法。
AI.keywords: ReLU神经网络, 环面几何, 表达能力, 热带几何, 卡蒂埃因子
AI.comments: 本文的创新之处在于将现代代数几何（特别是环面簇与相交理论）引入到深度学习理论中，架起了热带几何组合性质与环面几何空间结构之间的桥梁，为精确函数实现问题提供了全新的严格几何判据。其潜在局限在于当前理论主要限制在“无偏置”和“有理权重”的浅层网络设定，推广到带偏置、实数权重及任意深层网络在数学上面临更高的复杂度。

title: Model-Free Assessment of Simulator Fidelity via Quantile Curves
summary: As generative AI models are increasingly used to simulate real-world systems, quantifying the ``sim-to-real'' gap is critical. For each input setting of interest -- which we call a \emph{scenario}, such as a survey question or operating condition -- the real and simulated systems are associated with unobserved latent population parameters, and their discrepancy varies across scenarios. A fundamental challenge is that, for any given scenario, this discrepancy cannot be observed directly, since both systems are accessible only through finite samples, often of heterogeneous sizes across scenarios. Standard predictive inference methods are therefore ill-suited, as they quantify uncertainty in observable outputs rather than latent population parameters. To address this, we construct confidence sets for these latent parameters and use them to derive a robust proxy for the sim-to-real discrepancy. We then estimate the quantile function of this proxy to obtain a distribution-level risk profile of the simulator, which supports a broad range of statistical summaries, including statistical inference for the real output distribution in a new scenario, the calculation of risk measures like Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), and principled comparisons across simulators. Our method is model-agnostic and handles general output spaces, such as categorical survey responses and continuous multi-dimensional data. We demonstrate the practical utility of this method by evaluating the alignment of four major LLMs with human populations on the WorldValueBench dataset.

AI.title_translation: 基于分位数曲线的无模型模拟器保真度评估
AI.tldr: 提出了一种无模型的通用评估框架，通过构建潜在参数置信集并估计分位数曲线，有效量化生成式模拟器与真实系统之间的保真度差距及分布级风险。
AI.motivation: 随着生成式AI广泛用于系统模拟，量化'仿真到现实'（sim-to-real）的差距至关重要；但由于各场景下系统仅能通过有限且样本量异构的数据访问，潜在参数差异无法直接观测，且传统的预测推断方法无法量化潜在总体参数的不确定性。
AI.method: 为真实与模拟系统的潜在总体参数构建置信集，由此推导'仿真到现实'差异的鲁棒代理指标，并估计该代理指标的分位数函数以获得模拟器的分布级风险概况；该方法属于模型无关方法，适用于分类和多维连续等通用输出空间。
AI.result: 所提方法成功支持了对新场景真实输出的统计推断、CVaR等风险测度计算以及模拟器间的原则性比较，并在WorldValueBench数据集上成功评估了四种主流LLM与人类群体的对齐情况。
AI.conclusion: 本文提出的基于分位数曲线的无模型评估方法，能够有效解决有限和异构样本下潜在参数差异无法直接观测的难题，为评估模拟器保真度和风险概况提供了一种原则性强且实用的统计推断工具。
AI.translation: 随着生成式人工智能模型越来越广泛地用于模拟现实世界系统，量化“仿真到现实”（sim-to-real）的差距变得至关重要。对于所关注的每个输入设定（我们称之为“场景”，如调查问题或运行工况），真实系统与模拟系统都关联着未观测到的潜在总体参数，且二者的差异在不同场景下各有不同。一个根本性的挑战在于，在任何给定场景中，由于这两个系统只能通过有限样本进行访问（且各场景间样本量通常是异构的），因此无法直接观测到这种差异。标准的预测推断方法因其量化的是可观测输出的不确定性而非潜在总体参数的不确定性，因而不适用。为了解决这一问题，我们为这些潜在参数构建了置信集，并利用它们推导出了sim-to-real差异的鲁棒代理指标。随后，我们估计该代理指标的分位数函数，以获取模拟器的分布级风险概况，该概况支持广泛的统计汇总，包括对新场景下真实输出分布的统计推断、条件在险价值（CVaR）等风险指标的计算，以及模拟器之间的原则性比较。我们的方法是无模型的，能够处理通用的输出空间，例如分类调查回答和连续多维数据。我们通过在WorldValueBench数据集上评估四种主流大语言模型与人类群体的对齐情况，展示了该方法的实际应用价值。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种无模型的模拟器保真度评估方法。针对有限异构样本下潜在系统参数差异不可直接观测的挑战，该方法通过构建潜在参数的置信集和估计差异代理指标的分位数曲线，实现模拟器分布级风险概况的量化，并在大语言模型的人类对齐度评测中验证了其实用性。
AI.keywords: 模拟器保真度, 仿真到现实差距, 分位数曲线, 无模型评估, 大语言模型对齐
AI.comments: 该研究针对生成式AI评估中常见的有限样本和未观测潜在参数难题，创新性地结合置信集与分位数函数构建了无模型的风险评估框架；其模型无关性以及对分类、高维连续输出的通用兼容性，使其在LLM与现实对齐度量等场景具有广泛的应用前景。

title: Similarity-Sensitive Entropy under Representation Change and Inference
comments: 26 pages. v3: Revised abstract; generalized coarse graining proof; added further directions; revised theorem statements
summary: Similarity-sensitive entropy measures the uncertainty of a probability law relative to a similarity kernel that encodes the distinguishability of states. We develop the measure-theoretic treatment covering both finite similarity matrices and general probability spaces, and study how the law and similarity kernel transform under measurable maps, channels, and conditioning operations. This yields data-processing inequalities, so a reduction in entropy quantifies how much distinguishability is lost under representation change. We also define a conditional similarity-sensitive entropy theory, give a counterexample to a recent conjecture on concavity, and identify a practical one-dimensional Laplace kernel class where concavity holds.
comment: 26 pages. v3: Revised abstract; generalized coarse graining proof; added further directions; revised theorem statements

AI.title_translation: 表征变化与推断下的相似度敏感熵
AI.tldr: 本文建立了涵盖一般概率空间的相似度敏感熵测度论框架，导出了数据处理不等式，提出了条件熵理论，并证伪了凹性猜想且证明了一维拉普拉斯核下的凹性。
AI.motivation: 为了在一般概率空间中建立考虑状态间可区分度（由相似核编码）的不确定性度量理论，并探明该度量在表征变换（映射、信道、条件化等）下的演化与损失规律。
AI.method: 基于测度论方法构建了涵盖有限相似矩阵和一般概率空间的理论体系；分析了分布与相似核在可测映射、信道和条件化操作下的演化规律；建立了条件相似度敏感熵理论并进行数学反例与特例证明。
AI.result: 推导出了相似度敏感熵的数据处理不等式，明确了其熵减量可用于量化表征变换中可区分度的损失；提出了条件相似度敏感熵理论；给出了一个反例推翻了近期关于该熵凹性的猜想，并证明了一类实用的一维拉普拉斯核具有凹性。
AI.translation: 相似度敏感熵通过编码状态可区分度的相似核来度量概率法则的不确定性。我们建立了涵盖有限相似矩阵和一般概率空间的测度论处理方法，并研究了概率法则与相似核在可测映射、信道和条件化操作下的变换规律。这导出了数据处理不等式，从而使熵的减少能够量化表征变化中损失了多少可区分度。我们还定义了条件相似度敏感熵理论，针对近期关于凹性的一个猜想给出了反例，并确定了一类凹性成立的实用一维拉普拉斯核。
AI.summary: 本文为相似度敏感熵建立了通用的测度论分析框架，涵盖离散与连续概率空间。作者研究了该熵在可测映射、信道及条件化操作下的变换特征，导出了数据处理不等式以量化表征改变造成的可区分度损失。同时，作者构建了条件相似度敏感熵理论，推翻了近期的凹性猜想，并证明了一维拉普拉斯核类满足凹性。
AI.keywords: 相似度敏感熵, 相似核, 数据处理不等式, 条件熵, 凹性
AI.comments: 该论文的重要创新在于突破了以往多局限于有限离散状态的设定，将相似度敏感熵推广至一般测度空间，并建立了形式严谨的条件熵理论与数据处理不等式。此外，通过构造反例推翻了此前的凹性猜想，不仅纠正了该领域的认知偏差，还找出了凹性成立的具体核函数类，具有重要的理论修正与指导价值。局限性在于目前凹性的正向保证仅限于特定的一维拉普拉斯核类，更高维及更广泛核函数的性质仍待进一步发掘。

title: The Leibniz adjunction in homotopy type theory, with an application to simplicial type theory
comments: v4: Corrected links to Agda HTML. To appear at CSL 2027
summary: Simplicial type theory extends homotopy type theory and equips types with a notion of directed morphisms. A Segal type is defined to be a type in which these directed morphisms can be composed. We show that all higher coherences can be stated and derived if simplicial type theory is taken to be homotopy type theory with a postulated interval type. In technical terms, this means that if a type has unique fillers for $(2,1)$-horns, it has unique fillers for all inner $(n,k)$-horns. This generalizes a result of Riehl and Shulman for the case $n = 3, k \in \{1, 2\}$. Our main technical tool is the Leibniz adjunction: the pushout-product is left adjoint to the pullback-hom in the wild category of types. While this adjunction is well known for ordinary categories, it is much more involved for higher categories, and the fact that it can be proved for the wild category of types (a higher category without stated higher coherences) is non-trivial. We make profitable use of the equivalence between the wild category of maps and that of families. We have formalized the results in Cubical Agda.

AI.title_translation: 同伦类型理论中的莱布尼茨伴随，及其在单纯类型理论中的应用
AI.tldr: 本文扩展了同伦类型理论到单纯类型理论，通过假定的区间类型处理了高阶相干性问题，并利用莱布尼茨伴随证明了其在类型狂野范畴中的有效性。
AI.motivation: 本文旨在将同伦类型理论扩展至单纯类型理论，为类型配备有向态射的概念，并定义可组合这些有向态射的Segal类型。主要动机是处理高阶范畴中的高阶相干性问题，特别是证明莱布尼茨伴随在没有明确高阶相干性的类型狂野范畴中的有效性。
AI.method: 研究方法是将单纯类型理论视为带有假定区间类型的同伦类型理论。通过证明如果一个类型具有唯一的(2,1)-角填充，则它具有所有内部(n,k)-角的唯一填充，从而推导出所有高阶相干性。核心技术工具是莱布尼茨伴随，即在类型狂野范畴中，推出-积是拉回-同态的左伴随。此外，还利用了映射狂野范畴与族狂野范畴之间的等价性，并在Cubical Agda中对结果进行了形式化。
AI.result: 结果表明，如果将单纯类型理论视为带有假定区间类型的同伦类型理论，则所有高阶相干性都可以被陈述和推导，具体表现为若一个类型具有唯一的(2,1)-角填充，则它具有所有内部(n,k)-角的唯一填充。这推广了Riehl和Shulman在n=3, k∈{1,2}情况下的结果。主要技术工具莱布尼茨伴随被证明在类型狂野范畴中成立，这是一个非平凡的发现。所有结果已在Cubical Agda中形式化。
AI.conclusion: 本文的结论是，通过将单纯类型理论视为带有假定区间类型的同伦类型理论，可以成功陈述和推导所有高阶相干性。关键在于莱布尼茨伴随在没有明确高阶相干性的类型狂野范畴中得到了证明，这解决了高阶范畴理论中的一个非平凡问题。
AI.translation: 单纯类型理论扩展了同伦类型理论，并为类型配备了有向态射的概念。Segal类型被定义为其中这些有向态射可以组合的类型。我们表明，如果将单纯类型理论视为带有假定区间类型的同伦类型理论，则所有高阶相干性都可以被陈述和推导。从技术上讲，这意味着如果一个类型具有唯一的(2,1)-角填充，则它具有所有内部(n,k)-角的唯一填充。这推广了Riehl和Shulman在n=3, k∈{1,2}情况下的结果。我们的主要技术工具是莱布尼茨伴随：在类型狂野范畴中，推出-积是拉回-同态的左伴随。虽然这种伴随对于普通范畴是众所周知的，但对于高阶范畴来说要复杂得多，并且它可以在类型狂野范畴（一个没有明确高阶相干性的高阶范畴）中被证明这一事实是非平凡的。我们充分利用了映射狂野范畴与族狂野范畴之间的等价性。我们已在Cubical Agda中形式化了这些结果。
AI.summary: 本文将同伦类型理论扩展为单纯类型理论，引入有向态射和Segal类型。研究表明，通过假定一个区间类型，单纯类型理论能够陈述和推导所有高阶相干性，即(2,1)-角填充的唯一性蕴含所有内部(n,k)-角填充的唯一性，从而推广了现有结果。核心贡献是证明了莱布尼茨伴随在类型狂野范畴中的有效性，这是一个在高阶范畴理论中非平凡的成果。所有结果已在Cubical Agda中形式化。
AI.keywords: 同伦类型理论, 单纯类型理论, 莱布尼茨伴随, 高阶相干性, Segal类型
AI.comments: 本文的创新性在于在高阶范畴理论中，非平凡地证明了莱布尼茨伴随在没有明确高阶相干性的类型狂野范畴中的成立，这为处理高阶相干性提供了关键工具。通过将单纯类型理论与假定区间类型相结合，成功地推广了现有关于高阶相干性的结果。此外，在Cubical Agda中进行形式化，增强了研究的严谨性和可信度。

title: On sparsity, extremal structure, and monotonicity properties of Wasserstein and Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport plans
summary: This note gives a self-contained overview of some key properties of the Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distance, compared with the standard linear optimal transport (OT) framework. More specifically, I explore the following questions: are GW optimal transport plans sparse? under what conditions does there exist an optimal plan supported on a permutation? do optimal plans satisfy a form of cyclical monotonicity? In particular, I present the conditionally negative/positive definite (CND/CPD) properties and show that, when they hold, there exist GW optimal plans that are sparse and supported on a permutation. In the last section, I also give examples where no permutation is optimal when the CND or CPD assumption is dropped.

title: ViroGym: Realistic Large-Scale Benchmarks for Evaluating Viral Proteins
summary: Protein language models (pLMs) have shown strong potential for zero-shot prediction of missense variant effects, yet systematic benchmarking on viral proteins remains limited, a critical gap given the need for proactive tools that can anticipate emerging mutations ahead of experimental validation. Here we introduce ViroGym, a comprehensive benchmark evaluating pLMs across three tasks: 79 deep mutational scanning (DMS) assays covering eukaryotic viruses with 552,065 mutated sequences across 7 phenotypic readouts, 21 influenza neutralisation tasks, and a real-world pandemic prediction task for SARS-CoV-2. We benchmark well-established pLMs on fitness landscapes, antigenic diversity, and pandemic forecasting, and find that the ProGen2 family consistently achieves the strongest performance across all three tasks. Crucially, DMS and neutralisation performance reliably identifies models that generalise to real-world emergence, even though the mutation sets they surface barely overlap, revealing that complementary in vitro benchmarks capture the evolutionary constraints needed for real-world mutation forecasting. The data and code supporting this study are publicly available on GitHub at https://github.com/GSK-AI/viroGym

title: A Variational Latent Equilibrium for Learning in Neuronal Circuits
summary: Brains remain unrivaled in their ability to recognize and generate complex spatiotemporal patterns. While AI is able to reproduce some of these capabilities, deep learning algorithms remain largely at odds with our current understanding of brain circuitry and dynamics. This is prominently the case for backpropagation through time (BPTT), the go-to algorithm for learning complex temporal dependencies. In this work we propose a general formalism to approximate BPTT in a controlled, biologically plausible manner. Our approach builds on, unifies and extends several previous approaches to local, time-continuous, phase-free spatiotemporal credit assignment based on principles of energy conservation and extremal action. Our starting point is a prospective energy function of neuronal states, from which we calculate real-time error dynamics for time-continuous neuronal networks. With this, as a first contribution we provide a simple and straightforward derivation of the adjoint method dynamical equations, the time-continuous equivalent to BPTT. Importantly, additional approximations are necessary to avoid unphysical temporal non-localities. One such approximation was recently proposed in Generalized Latent Equilibrium (GLE), but enforcing temporal locality of the backpropagating dynamics induces an error in the gain that becomes problematic when processing complex signals. Thus, our second contribution is to design a learning rule for the backward weights to find a fully local (in space and time) set of equations for neuron and synapse dynamics that corrects for this gain difference. With this inclusion of backward weight learning, our theory provides a rigorous framework for spatiotemporal deep learning in the brain, while simultaneously advancing a blueprint for physical circuits capable of carrying out these computations.

title: Auto-differentiable data assimilation: Co-learning of states, dynamics, and filtering algorithms
summary: Data assimilation algorithms estimate the state of a dynamical system from partial observations, where the successful performance of these algorithms hinges on costly parameter tuning and on employing an accurate model for the dynamics. This paper introduces a framework for jointly learning the state, dynamics, and parameters of filtering algorithms in data assimilation through a process we refer to as auto-differentiable filtering. The framework leverages a theoretically motivated loss function that enables learning from partial, noisy observations via gradient-based optimization using auto-differentiation. We further demonstrate how several well-known data assimilation methods can be learned or tuned within this framework. To underscore the versatility of auto-differentiable filtering, we perform experiments on dynamical systems spanning multiple scientific domains, such as the Clohessy-Wiltshire equations from aerospace engineering, the Lorenz-96 system from atmospheric science, the generalized Lotka-Volterra equations from systems biology, and the two-layer quasi-geostrophic model from geophysical fluid dynamics. Finally, we provide guidelines for practitioners to customize our framework according to their observation model, accuracy requirements, and computational budget.

title: Faster Symmetric Rendezvous on Four or More Locations
summary:
In the symmetric rendezvous problem, two players follow the same (randomized) strategy to visit one of $n$ locations in each time step $t=0,1,2,\dots$. Their goal is to minimize the expected time until they visit the same location and thus meet. A canonical strategy due to Anderson and Weber (J. Appl. Probab., 1990) is known to be optimal for $n=2$ and $n=3$ (Weber, Math. Oper. Res. 2012), but whether it remains optimal for larger values of $n$ has been an open question since 1990. We show that it does not remain optimal: for any finite $n\geq 4$, we construct an explicit symmetric strategy that achieves a strictly smaller expected meeting time than the Anderson-Weber strategy.
  In the Anderson-Weber strategy players stay at a dedicated home location for $n-1$ steps with a certain probability $θ$ and with the remaining probability tour all non-home locations in a random order. Our improving strategy introduces carefully chosen correlations between consecutive tours of the non-home locations. The construction is uniform in $n$ and is guided by a graph-theoretic view in which tours correspond to permutations and meetings to edges in the complement of the derangement graph. By exploiting the clique structure of this graph we obtain a correlated strategy that improves on the Anderson-Weber strategy. For $n=4$, we give an exact expression for the improvement; for any $n\geq 5$, we obtain a lower bound on the expected improvement of $\frac{483(1-θ)^6}{(n-1)^8}$, where $θ\in [0,1)$ is the probability of staying at the home location. The graph-theoretic framework we introduce may be useful more widely in the design and analysis of correlated strategies for rendezvous.

title: Minimizing classical resources in variational measurement-based quantum computation for generative modeling
summary: Measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) is a framework for quantum information processing in which a computational task is carried out through one-qubit measurements on a highly entangled resource state. Due to the indeterminacy of the outcomes of a quantum measurement, the random outcomes of these operations, if not corrected, yield a variational quantum channel family. Traditionally, this randomness is corrected through classical processing in order to ensure deterministic unitary computations. Recently, variational measurement-based quantum computation (VMBQC) has been introduced to exploit this measurement-induced randomness to gain an advantage in generative modeling. A limitation of this approach is that the corresponding channel model has twice as many parameters compared to the unitary model, scaling as $N \times D$, where $N$ is the number of logical qubits (width) and $D$ is the depth of the VMBQC model. This can often make optimization more difficult and may lead to poorly trainable models. In this paper, we present a restricted VMBQC model that extends the unitary setting to a channel-based one using only a single additional trainable parameter. We show, both numerically and algebraically, that this minimal extension is sufficient to generate probability distributions that cannot be learned by the corresponding unitary model.

title: mlr3torch: A Deep Learning Framework in R based on mlr3 and torch
summary: Deep learning (DL) has become a cornerstone of modern machine learning (ML) praxis. We introduce the R package mlr3torch, which is an extensible DL framework for the mlr3 ecosystem. It is built upon the torch package, and simplifies the definition, training, and evaluation of neural networks for both tabular data and generic tensors (e.g., images) for classification and regression. The package implements predefined architectures, and torch models can easily be converted to mlr3 learners. It also allows users to define neural networks as graphs. This representation is based on the graph language defined in mlr3pipelines and allows users to define the entire modeling workflow, including preprocessing, data augmentation, and network architecture, in a single graph. Through its integration into the mlr3 ecosystem, the package allows for convenient resampling, benchmarking, preprocessing, and more. We explain the package's design and features and show how to customize and extend it to new problems. Furthermore, we demonstrate the package's capabilities using three use cases, namely hyperparameter tuning, fine-tuning, and defining architectures for multimodal data. Finally, we present some runtime benchmarks.

title: Kernel-based potential mean-field games with unbiased random Fourier $U$-statistics
summary: We study the subclass of potential mean-field games in which the running interaction cost and the terminal target cost are both expressed through reproducing-kernel maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) penalties, and develop a computational framework that exploits this kernel structure. Both costs are estimated from finite-sample empirical distributions using a random Fourier U-statistic representation that is unbiased and has linear cost in the batch size. The drift of the controlled diffusion is parametrized by a neural network and trained via stochastic gradient descent. For population near-minimizers we prove convergence to the terminal-constrained problem as the penalty diverges, and show that the same limit is recovered almost surely when such controls are evaluated on independent finite samples under explicit coupling conditions on the penalty, random-feature count and sample size. The framework includes the kernel-MMD-penalty Schr{ö}dinger bridge problem as the special case of a vanishing interaction cost. Numerical experiments illustrate the method on the Schr{ö}dinger bridge problem in dimensions up to one hundred, and on an electric vehicle charging coordination problem with per-vehicle physical heterogeneity, where a control-dependent aggregate-demand cost produces a trade-off between peak normalized charging power and the terminal service level.

title: An annihilation-number Caro-Wei bound: a TxGraffiti conjecture and an independence-number bracket
summary: Computable independence bounds give intervals that can be compared by containment or by their worst-case endpoint ratios. For positive maximum degree $Δ$, the Caro-Wei sum $W$ bounds the independence number from below, while $(Δ+1)W/2$ bounds it from above. A second interval has the Havel-Hakimi residue as its lower endpoint and the annihilation number as its upper endpoint. This note proves that the annihilation number does not exceed the Caro-Wei upper endpoint. This upper bound is sharp, with equality for regular graphs of positive degree and even order. Since the residue is at least $W$, this upper bound places the residue-annihilation interval inside the Caro-Wei interval. Both endpoints can improve strictly on one graph, although the sharp worst-case endpoint ratio remains unchanged, even for connected graphs. The annihilation-number bound also proves a conjectured lower estimate based on the annihilation number and residue for every connected graph with at least three vertices. Equality in this estimate holds for exactly eight graph types, while the single edge violates it. For maximum degree at least three, however, the estimate never exceeds the residue, even without connectedness.

title: A Spectral Proximal DC Algorithm with Nonmonotone Line Search and Extrapolation
summary: The paper proposes a novel proximal difference-of-convex (DC) algorithmic framework to solve general nonconvex, nonsmooth optimization problems. The basic pBBDCA method combines Barzilai-Borwein (BB) parameter selection with a nonmonotone directional line search, requiring only one proximal solve per iteration. We also develop two extrapolated variants using restart and safeguarding mechanisms. The global convergence of the proposed framework is rigorously established under the Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz property. Numerical experiments on the SCAD-regularized least squares problem and graph Ginzburg-Landau image segmentation models demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve highly competitive efficiency and accuracy.

title: Kusner's conjecture on equilateral sets is false
comments: The counterexample (Theorem 1) has been formalised in Lean from standard axioms. Lean proof: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23786173
summary: We disprove Kusner's 1983 conjecture that every equilateral set in $\ell_p^n$ with $2<p<\infty$ has at most $n+1$ points: there exist $58$ points in $\mathbb{R}^{56}$ whose pairwise $\ell_5$ distances are all equal, so the maximum equilateral-set size satisfies $e(\ell_5^{56})\ge58>57$. This is the first equilateral set of more than $n+1$ points in $\ell_p^n$ for any finite $p\ge2$. The construction persists on an open interval of exponents around $5$. The configuration is specified by the unique solution of an explicit polynomial system with rational coefficients in a rational box; existence and uniqueness are proved by exact integer inequalities. The existence of the $58$-point equilateral set in $\ell_5^{56}$ has been formalised in Lean from standard axioms.

title: The $α$-Limit Problem: Convergence of a Linear Degenerate Interface Transmission Problem
summary: We study the singular limit of a family of linear degenerate interface transmission problems arising from a regularization procedure in the newly proposed Two-Parameter Diffuse Domain Method (DDM2p). For $α>0$, the regularized problem admits a strictly convex variational formulation on $H^{1}(Ω)$. In the limit $α\to0$, the problem degenerates to a weakly coupled interface system with a nonstandard energy structure. To characterize the limit, we introduce a closed Hilbert subspace $\mathcal{H}\subset H^{1}(Ω)$, defined through an auxiliary Helmholtz problem on an annular subdomain $Ω_2\subset Ω$, and identify the limiting energy functional $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ on $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that the regularized energies $\mathcal{E}_α$ restricted to $\mathcal{H}$ $Γ$-converge to $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ in the strong $L^{2}(Ω)$ topology, using the standard framework. Consequently, minimizers of $\mathcal{E}_α$ converge to the unique minimizer of $\mathcal{E}_{0}$, which is shown to be equivalent to the solution of the limiting interface problem. We further prove a strong convergence $u_α\to u_{0}$ in $H^{1}(Ω)$ and establish a convergence rate of $O(α)$. Numerical experiments in one spatial dimension exhibit first-order convergence, suggesting that the proved $O(α)$ upper bound is sharp.

title: Self-Supervised Learning for Robust Resonance Mass Regression in Cascade Decays
comments: 9th Workshop on Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences (ML4PS 2026)
summary: Reconstructing the mass of a heavy resonance from its decay products with missing energy is one of the central tasks that directly determine the sensitivity in new physics searches at collider experiments. Supervised learning approaches to this problem often struggle to generalize well due to the presence of various systematic uncertainties and distribution shifts. Exhausting all possible variations in the labeled data can be very compute-intensive, while a failure of the model to generalize can corrupt the reconstructed resonance widths that are critical in peak-hunting analyses. In this work, following the foundation model paradigm, we use a self-supervised approach to pre-train a transformer encoder with VICReg to learn an embedding invariant to various corruptions, then fine-tune it for mass regression on a heavy resonance with masses ranging from 2.5 to 6.5 TeV and a SUSY-like cascade decay into an eleven-body final state. We show that the pre-trained model reconstructs sharper resonance peaks and has a more stable performance under various realistic corruptions, compared to a supervised model of the same architecture trained on the same augmented data from scratch.

title: Similarity Pairing with Energy Mover's Distance for Self-Supervised Pre-Training at the LHC
comments: 9th Workshop on Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences (ML4PS 2026)
summary: Many self-supervised methods for training foundation models at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) rely on data augmentations to encourage the model to embed events into a representation space invariant to certain physical or detector symmetries. A common challenge arises from the large freedom in choosing a proper set of augmentations on which downstream performance depends. The implementation of augmentations involves either modifying existing events, potentially breaking the event fidelity, or simulating more event variants, which is computationally intensive. In this work, we present a data-driven method of pairing events by their similarity via the energy mover's distance (EMD), which measures how similar two events are in terms of the work required to transform one into the other. With this approach, distinct events are sampled and matched by their similarity to serve as views for learning invariance, keeping the physics content of each event intact without handcrafted distortions. We demonstrate this augmentation-free pairing method by pre-training on QCD jets via self-distillation and show that it can yield semantic jet embeddings with downstream discrimination power comparable to or better than an augmentation-based baseline.

title: Dynamic Pooling and Regional Participation in Deceased-Donor Organ Allocation
summary: Moving from geographically fragmented to pooled waiting lists in deceased-donor organ transplantation can improve efficiency, but it raises concerns about regional fairness and participation incentives. This paper studies Pareto gains from such transitions in a multiclass queueing model with impatient agents, perishable items, and a tractable homogeneous compatibility friction. In contrast to standard approaches that emphasize static match quality or overlook regional incentives in dynamic contexts, this analysis identifies dynamic risk pooling as the primary source of Pareto improvements for regions. Pooling reduces organ waste resulting from stochastic supply-demand fluctuations, temporal mismatches, and random compatibility outcomes. Although this dynamic surplus theoretically enables Pareto improvements, a purely utilitarian policy that treats all patients equally across regions often fails to achieve these improvements when regions are asymmetric. In these situations, utilitarian redistribution removes an excessive number of organs from high-supply regions and violates their participation constraints. To address this conflict, it is demonstrated that the set of achievable utilities can be represented by mixtures of static priority index policies. Building on this structure, the Constrained Pareto Frontier Search (CPFS) is proposed as a polynomial-time procedure that computes an approximately optimal allocation policy with arbitrarily small participation-constraint violations, implemented as a single priority list with a lottery at registration. The results indicate that, by adjusting priority indices to ensure redistribution remains within the gains from pooled supply, demand, and compatibility risk, policymakers can achieve global efficiency while maintaining local participation incentives.

title: Generative sequence modeling for infinite memory processes via predictive states
summary: We consider estimating the one-step-ahead conditional distribution of a multivariate stochastic process. Many existing approaches rely on assumptions such as finite-range memory, sparsity, or additivity, which can be poorly suited to processes with long-range nonlinear interactions. However, without such structural assumptions, nonparametric estimation is challenging due to the curse of dimensionality. To address this challenge, we introduce a new estimator based on learning representations of the \emph{predictive states} of a stochastic process. We show that the statistical complexity of the estimation problem is determined by the dimension of this predictive state representation. Furthermore, we show that a $p$-dimensional predictive state space can be represented in a $2p+1$-dimensional feature space. Our results imply that faster convergence rates are achievable when the predictive state space is lower-dimensional, i.e., when the past history can be compressed into a lower-dimensional statistic that is sufficient for predicting the future. We establish theoretical convergence rate guarantees for an instantiation of our method based on deep neural network estimators. We implement our method in PyTorch and evaluate its performance on synthetic data and real \emph{C. elegans} data.

title: High-Dimensional Online Calibration from Harmonic Weights
comments: In-depth talk about this work: https://youtu.be/2aL0viNUveE
summary:
We study the online calibration of multidimensional forecasts over an arbitrary convex set $Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ relative to an arbitrary error norm $\|\cdot\|_L$. For forecasting $d$ binary outcomes simultaneously ($Y=[0,1]^d$), we give the first algorithm that achieves $\varepsilon$-calibration in a number of rounds that is polynomial in $d$ for every fixed accuracy. It requires $d^{O(1/\varepsilon)}$ rounds, exponentially improving the dimension dependence of previous bounds. For multi-class forecasting ($Y=Δ_d$), we obtain the same $d^{O(1/\varepsilon)}$ rate, improving the $d^{\widetilde{O}(1/\varepsilon^2)}$ bounds of Peng and Fishelson, Golowich, Mohri, and Schneider.
  Our algorithm is simple: on each round, it outputs a harmonically weighted distribution over harmonically smoothed past outcomes. The same algorithm works for every forecast set and error norm. More generally, it achieves $\varepsilon$-calibration after $\exp(O(γ(Y,L)/\varepsilon))$ rounds, where $γ(Y,L)$ is a geometric parameter defined by a matrix discrepancy problem. The harmonic weights are motivated by the fact that the discrete Hilbert transform matrix achieves the optimal discrepancy up to a universal constant, simultaneously for every $L$. This optimality result may be of independent interest.
  The same harmonic responses also yield an algorithm for high-dimensional Blackwell approachability. Its guarantees are governed by a sharpened geometric parameter that captures the joint geometry of the outcome and action sets.

title: ECGGuard: Deep Watermarking of Electrocardiogram Signals With Error-Correcting
summary: Wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings pass through multiple networks and systems before automated interpretation, leaving patient metadata vulnerable to loss. Digital watermarking can embed this metadata in the signal, but conventional methods fail under time shifts, and high waveform similarity does not guarantee the same downstream diagnosis. We present \rev{ECGGuard}, a deep watermarking framework for single-lead ECG. A fully convolutional generator embeds the payload without signal quantization, a detector decodes the message frame by frame and checks for watermark presence, and during training a frozen arrhythmia classifier penalizes changes that would alter its predictions. Because high bit accuracy does not ensure whole-message recovery, the payload is protected by extended Hamming codes, \rev{a validation-selected channel ordering}, and soft-decision decoding. On the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, \rev{averaged over three training runs, ECGGuard} keeps bit accuracy above \rev{98\%} under time shifts of 10 to 50 samples, where transform-domain baselines drop to chance. The coded 16-bit payload is recovered exactly in \rev{99.95\%} of clean segments\rev{, in over 96\%} under time shifts, 10\% sample deletion, or 10\% packet loss\rev{, and in 99.1\% for unseen subjects}. \rev{For the guiding classifier, the diagnostic loss limits the drop in ventricular-beat sensitivity to 1.6 percentage points on the test records (35.0 without it) and to 12.2 points for unseen subjects (67.0 without it); the drop grows to 10.3 points for independently trained classifiers, and the protection does not transfer to an external database.} \rev{ECGGuard} has 0.56 million parameters and needs about \rev{19}~ms per segment on a desktop CPU.

title: Logics vs doctrines, a mirror symmetry
comments: Corrected minor mistakes and introduced the notion of tightness in Section 5
summary: We study the relationship between doctrines, encoding 2-categories of theories in predicate logic, and fragments of geometric logic, defined through Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi. After a brief historical account of the notion of doctrine, we propose our working definition. Our main result then establishes a Galois connection between doctrines and subgeometric logics. This connection suggests a mirror symmetry between the world of doctrines and the world of logics, in which constructions and results on either side admit counterparts on the other. We develop this symmetry through constructions of syntactic categories and classifying topoi in both settings, recovering the familiar examples from categorical logic. We prove paired Diaconescu-type theorems and give symmetric descriptions of the two closure operators induced by the Galois connection. Finally, we characterise when passing from a doctrine to its closure induces a reflection between the corresponding 2-categories of algebras, and we relate this reflection to conceptual completeness.

title: Integrate the Reward, Don't Sample It: Window Likelihood for Interruptions and Backchannels in Full-Duplex Speech Models
summary: When a user talks over a full-duplex dialogue model, it must decide whether the user is interrupting (stop) or backchannelling (carry on). Post-training can improve this discrimination or change how readily it stops. In our GRPO runs the second dominates: no configuration lowers both error rates on more than one model, and two released checkpoints discriminate no better than their bases. We trace this partly to how the reward is estimated. The probability of stopping inside a short window is a known function of a few stop probabilities the policy emits, yet GRPO estimates it by sampling. A group of rollouts that all agree gives no gradient, even when all fail; the push on the stop threshold is strongest where the model is unsure, whichever outcome is right; and whole-rollout credit reaches decisions the reward never judges. Confining the credit to the window removes only that leakage. Window likelihood (WL) samples the words but integrates over the stop decisions, so the probability of the correct outcome is computed exactly and its logarithm maximised. On HumDial-FDBench, across four open models, WL gives the best F1 and lowers both error rates by more than their confidence intervals, without talking into silence.

title: Quantum query complexity of Hurwitz stability testing
summary: Determining whether every trajectory of the linear system $\dot{x}=Ax$ converges to zero (or, equivalently, whether $A$ is Hurwitz stable) is a fundamental problem in control theory. It arises, for example, in verifying the stability of feedback controllers and state observers, as well as of linearized dynamical models. We study the quantum query complexity of deciding whether a matrix $A\in\mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ is Hurwitz stable, given an exact normalized block-encoding of $A$. The query complexity is characterized in terms of the system dimension $n$ and a supplied lower bound $0<ν\leq ω_A$ on the imaginary-axis distance $ω_A:=\min_{t\in\mathbb{R}}σ_{\min}(A-\mathrm{i}tI)$, where $σ_{\min}(A)$ is the smallest singular value of $A$. We prove a query-complexity lower bound of $Ω(\sqrt{n}/ν)$, which holds even when $A$ is restricted to be real and diagonal. For general matrices with nonzero $ω_A$, we encode an approximation of the right-half-plane spectral projector $\operatorname{sign}^+(A):=(I+\operatorname{sign}(A))/2$ as a block of a matrix inverse, where $A$ is Hurwitz if and only if the projector is zero. To test this, we produce a quantum algorithm which determines if a $(β,b,1/(4\sqrt{n}))$-block-encoded projector matrix (like $\operatorname{sign}^+(A)$) is zero or not; for constant success probability, it has complexity $Θ(β\sqrt{n})$. When the zero test is applied to specific approximations of $\operatorname{sign}^+(A)$, this yields an upper bound of $O(\sqrt{n}ν^{-2}\log(\sqrt{n}/ν))$ queries in the general case, and $O(\sqrt{n}ν^{-1}\log n)$ when $A$ is Hermitian or normal. The latter upper bound matches the lower bound up to a logarithmic factor. Thus the dimension dependence of quantum Hurwitz testing is nearly optimal, while the remaining factor in the non-normal case isolates an open conditioning gap.

title: Trajectory Density Ratios under Weak Support: A Survey across the Sciences
summary: Many problems across the sciences compare two stochastic processes through the sequences they generate. Reinforcement learning asks what a new policy would return from the trajectories of an old one; molecular simulation asks how much more a ligand binds from samples of the unbound state; climate attribution asks how a heat wave shifted under warming; and language-model post-training asks what a deployed agent will do from logged interactions. In every case, one quantity would answer all these questions at once: the ratio of the two probability laws over their generated sequences, the trajectory density ratio. This ratio exists only under strong conditions. When one process reaches states the other cannot, the ratio does not exist; when their overlap is thin, its variance grows without control with the sequence length; and when they concentrate on different lower-dimensional sets, the ratio is undefined altogether. Weak support of this kind is the norm for sequence data, not a sampling accident, and its price is paid in identifiability rather than in noise alone. This survey organizes the field around a three-level diagnosis of weak support and a map of the nine retreats that methods take when the full ratio is out of reach, from direct estimation and reweighting through staged decomposition, stationarization, and partial-identification bounds to smoothing, transport couplings, operator spectra, and direct estimation of a single functional. Each retreat keeps part of what the ratio offers and pays for the rest, and each application domain has standardized the retreat its data force. The survey closes with open problems: testable diagnostics at every level, partial identification at the trajectory level, a rate theory of time-amplified error, and benchmarks with ground truth.

title: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
summary: Intraoperative scene perception in ophthalmic microsurgery is limited by instrument occlusion: when a tool enters the high-magnification field, it conceals tissue from both the surgeon and the perception components of robot-assisted systems that process the video. Generative inpainting can remove the occluder but replaces the missing image content with synthesis, which is unsuitable when visual provenance matters. Many video inpainters also depend on future frames and cannot operate online. We present TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time. Every restored value is obtained by resampling a recorded frame using geometric transforms fitted only to visible regions. The system provides per-pixel confidence and provenance and marks unsupported pixels as abstentions. We evaluate TransGHOST on a new veterinary clinical corpus of canine cataract surgery with pixel-level instrument and anatomy labels. Only the occluded region is scored, and each scoring target is verified to differ from the reference supplied to the system. Safe mode reaches 31.89 dB masked PSNR and 0.915 masked SSIM at 51.7 ms median and 85.5 ms 95th-percentile latency. On a pre-declared held-out cohort using instrument cutouts excluded from segmentation training, it reaches 29.83 dB masked PSNR, while matched-mask evaluation on validation shows a 3.45 dB advantage over LaMa. Region-aware reference selection improves masked PSNR by 3.60 dB over recency when candidate references can themselves be occluded. Reference-age analysis further defines the operating interval for the brief, repeated occlusions targeted by TransGHOST.

title: Quantum-Assisted Counterfactual Regret Minimization for Bounded-Payoff Imperfect-Information Games
summary: Imperfect-information games with a graded-reward structure present significant computational challenges for equilibrium computation, since the payoff expectations must be estimated across exponentially large strategy spaces. Counterfactual Regret Minimization over the years has proven effective for approximating Nash equilibria, but Monte Carlo variants create a large overhead of sampling costs when the counterfactual values are estimated from sampled game-tree trajectories. We propose a novel Quantum-Assisted Counterfactual Regret Minimization, a framework that uses Quantum Amplitude Estimation to reduce the computational complexity of the regret updates in bounded-payoff imperfect-information games, while preserving the convergence of its classical counterpart. We give a theoretical analysis of the resulting exploitability bound, discuss NISQ-compatible amplitude-estimation variants, the structure of their resource requirements, and outline what is needed to validate the potential advantage empirically.

title: An Invariant Neural-Network Eddy-Viscosity Closure with Iterative Solver Coupling for Molten Salt Fast Reactor Thermal-Hydraulics
summary: System thermal-hydraulics codes such as the System Analysis Module (SAM) close turbulence on coarse meshes with algebraic zero-equation mixing-length models. These models cannot represent the non-equilibrium turbulence, flow separation, and large-scale recirculation of open-cavity advanced reactors. We develop an invariant neural-network eddy-viscosity closure for SAM and apply it to the Molten Salt Fast Reactor (MSFR). The closure predicts the turbulent kinetic energy and timescale of each element from the flow and geometry of its neighbors, without solving turbulence transport equations. The resulting non-negative eddy viscosity enters the implicit diffusive operator, which keeps the momentum equations well conditioned. We prove that the closure is exactly invariant to translation, Galilean boost, rotation, reflection, and neighbor ordering. A network trained on high-order Nek5000 fields sees a different feature distribution on the coarse SAM mesh. We remove this covariate shift by iteratively retraining the network on SAM flow states against fixed Nek5000 targets. For a held-out steady state, the coupled closure reproduces the single recirculation cell and eddy-viscosity plume of the Nek5000 reference. In a 120 s pump-coastdown transient, it halves the velocity error of the mixing-length model, from 37.6% to 17.7%, and matches the Nek5000 eddy viscosity with a time-averaged relative error of 12%. The remaining velocity error comes from the coarse mesh. The coupled transient takes about 0.2 core-hours, compared with about 330 core-hours for Nek5000. The results show that the closure can recover two-equation RANS turbulence behavior in a coarse-mesh system code at a small fraction of the CFD cost.

title: When to Move: Online Repositioning of Movable Antenna Arrays Under a Long-Term Actuation Energy Budget
summary: Movable antenna (MA) arrays improve multiuser throughput by repositioning their elements, but mechanical movement reduces transmission time and consumes actuation energy. Changes in user configurations create nonuniform demand for repositioning over time, while each movement determines which positions are reachable in subsequent slots. Thus, online control must decide when to spend a limited actuation-energy budget, not only where to position the antennas. We formulate causal effective-throughput maximization under displacement-dependent movement delay, inter-slot reachability, and a long-term average actuation-energy constraint. We propose Lyapunov-based online movable-antenna repositioning (LOMA), which adjusts the price of movement through a virtual queue and solves the resulting nonconvex position problem via proximal minorization--maximization, accounting for nonsmooth movement delay and promoting sparse antenna updates. We establish monotone ascent of the smoothed per-slot objective, a finite-horizon sample-path energy bound, almost-sure long-term budget feasibility under a Gaussian fading model with bounded large-scale gains, and a state-matched throughput comparison separating temporal energy allocation from per-slot optimization error. Simulations show that LOMA concentrates actuation after intermittent user changes and improves effective throughput over optimized fixed arrays and a per-slot-budget counterpart, while continuous channel drift favors more frequent incremental repositioning. Additional simulations with pilot-based channel estimates in sparse millimeter-wave channels show that LOMA retains most of the throughput benefits of online repositioning while operating near its prescribed long-term actuation-energy budget.

title: Brain-inspired Beam Selection for mmWave RIS Communication
summary: Beam selection at large passive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) requires either full channel knowledge or beam training, both of which entail unwanted overhead. On the other hand, learned models that predict the optimal codeword from channels sampled at a few active elements avoid both, at the cost of energy-demanding multiply-and-accumulate operations. In this paper, we propose spiking neural network (SNN)-based beam selection for a semi-active RIS assisting a mmWave multiple-input single-output communication system. Direct and sigmoid rate coding are compared against a multi- layer perceptron (MLP) of identical architecture. Energy analysis further reveals that the input layer dominates SNN energy consumption.

title: Efficient Design of Flag Sequence Sets for Delay-Doppler Estimation via Riemannian Optimization
summary: This letter investigates the design of a Flag sequence set with peak-curtain auto-ambiguity functions to enable low-complexity delay-Doppler estimation. Given the predefined Curtain sequences, the Flag sequence set design problem is formulated as the minimization of the weighted integrated masked sidelobe level. To solve this problem, we first reformulate it as an unconstrained optimization problem on the unimodular manifold. Then, a tailored unimodular manifold conjugate gradient (UM-CG) algorithm is developed. Compared with the existing define algorithm, the proposed UM-CG algorithm reduces computational and storage requirements. Moreover, the global convergence of the proposed UM-CG scheme is theoretically derived under mild conditions. Numerical results demonstrate the superior optimization performance of the proposed UM-CG algorithm and show that the designed Flag sequences exhibit nearly ideal peak-curtain properties.

title: Anomalous Sound Detection Using Separation Features and Paired-Mixture Representation Learning
comments: 11 pages, 3 figures; 6-page supplementary material included as an ancillary file. Submitted to IEEE Sensors Journal
summary: Acoustic condition monitoring often relies on normal recordings with limited operating-condition information. This study proposes an anomalous sound detection system that learns from normal recordings without external pre-training and uses machine-type information to organize training and normal references. A separator learns target-component estimation from mixtures of normal target and non-target recordings. With the separator frozen, regional attention and multi-stage fusion are trained on paired mixtures sharing a target, using contrastive and target-reference consistency objectives. Paired-mixture embedding differences provide covariance statistics for correction with normal-reference centering, followed by cosine nearest-neighbor scoring. On Task 2 development-test data from the 2022 Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events challenge, the two-block, 64-channel system achieves an overall harmonic mean of 64.56% on average across three independent training and evaluation runs, with a sample standard deviation of 0.33 percentage points. This mean exceeds that of direct paired-mixture learning by 2.23 percentage points and is 0.31 percentage points below that of the evaluated distillation system using an externally pre-trained teacher. For the learned embeddings, cosine nearest-neighbor scoring outperforms the evaluated Mahalanobis scorers based on global normal statistics. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining separation-based representation learning, interference-based correction, and local normal-reference scoring for anomalous sound detection without detailed operating metadata.
